short_description.id: Zhulong adalah naga merah raksasa dan dewa matahari dalam mitologi Tiongkok, yang membuka dan menutup matanya untuk mengatur siang dan malam.
short_description.en: Zhulong is a giant red dragon and solar deity in Chinese mythology, whose opening and closing eyes make day and night.

long_description.id: Zhulong adalah naga merah raksasa dan dewa matahari dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Ia digambarkan berwajah manusia dan bertubuh ular.
long_description.en: Zhulong is a giant red dragon and solar deity in Chinese mythology. He is portrayed with a human face and a serpent's body.

long_description.id: Membuka dan menutup matanya menciptakan siang dan malam, sedangkan napasnya menciptakan angin musim. Teks Shanhaijing menyebut dewa Gunung Zhong bernama Zhuyin: tiupannya menjadi musim dingin dan embusannya musim panas, ia tidak minum, makan, atau bernapas, napasnya menjadi angin, dan tubuhnya panjang seribu li. Ia berwajah manusia, bertubuh ular, berwarna merah, dan tinggal di kaki Gunung Zhong.
long_description.en: Opening and closing his eyes produces day and night, while breathing produces seasonal winds. The Shanhaijing text names the god of Mount Zhong as Zhuyin: his blowing makes winter and his exhaling makes summer, he does not drink, eat or breathe, his breath becomes wind, and his body is a thousand li long. He has a human face and a snake body, is red in colour, and dwells at the foot of Mount Zhong.

long_description.id: Bagian padang liar utara Shanhaijing menyebut dewa berwajah manusia dan bertubuh ular yang merah; bila ia memejam dunia gelap dan bila ia melihat dunia terang, dan ia mendatangkan angin dan hujan. Dialah yang disebut Zhulong. Huainanzi menyebut Zhulong berada di utara Yanmen, terlindung oleh Gunung Weiyu sehingga tidak terlihat matahari.
long_description.en: The northern wilds section of the Shanhaijing describes a red god with a human face and snake body; when he shuts his eyes it is dark and when he looks it is light, and he summons wind and rain. He is the one called Zhulong. The Huainanzi says Zhulong is north of Yanmen, hidden by Mount Weiyu so that it does not see the sun.

long_description.id: Chu Ci memuat varian nama Chuolong dan Zhuolong. Nama Zhuyin dan Zhulong ditemukan dalam teks klasik zaman Han. Shanhaijing memberikan kisah sejajar mengenai Zhuyin dan Zhulong.
long_description.en: The Chu Ci contains name variants Chuolong and Zhuolong. The names Zhuyin and Zhulong occur in Han-period classical texts. The Shanhaijing gives parallel accounts of Zhuyin and Zhulong.

name.id: Mengatur siang, malam, musim, dan angin
name.en: Governing day, night, seasons and wind

description.id: Teks klasik menyebut bahwa ketika Zhuyin melihat jadilah siang dan ketika memejam jadilah malam, tiupannya menjadi musim dingin dan embusannya musim panas, serta napasnya menjadi angin; teks lain menyebut ia mendatangkan angin dan hujan.
description.en: Classical texts say that when Zhuyin looks it is day and when he shuts his eyes it is night, his blowing makes winter and exhaling makes summer, and his breath becomes wind; another text says he summons wind and rain.

claims.quote: 鍾山之神名曰燭陰，視為晝，瞑為夜，吹為冬，呼為夏，不飲，不食，不息，息為風，身長千里。

statement.id: Teks Shanhaijing menyebut dewa Gunung Zhong (鍾山) bernama Zhuyin (燭陰): ketika ia melihat jadilah siang, ketika memejam jadilah malam, tiupannya menjadi musim dingin dan embusannya musim panas; ia tidak minum, makan, atau bernapas (beristirahat), napasnya menjadi angin, dan panjang tubuhnya seribu li.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing text names the god of Mount Zhong (鍾山) as Zhuyin (燭陰): when he looks it is day, when he closes his eyes it is night, his blowing makes winter and his exhaling makes summer; he does not drink, eat or breathe (rest), his breath becomes wind, and his body is a thousand li long.

claims.quote: 鍾山之神名曰燭陰 ... 其為物，人面，蛇身，赤色，居鍾山下。

statement.id: Teks yang sama menggambarkan dewa Gunung Zhong bernama Zhuyin (燭陰) itu berwajah manusia, bertubuh ular, berwarna merah, dan tinggal di kaki Gunung Zhong.
statement.en: The same text describes the god of Mount Zhong named Zhuyin (燭陰) as having a human face and a snake body, red in colour, and dwelling at the foot of Mount Zhong.

claims.quote: 有神，人面蛇身而赤，直目正乘，其暝乃晦，其視乃明，不食不寢不息，風雨是謁。是燭九陰，是謂燭龍。

statement.id: Teks Shanhaijing bagian padang liar utara menyebut dewa berwajah manusia dan bertubuh ular yang merah, bermata lurus; ketika ia memejam dunia gelap, ketika ia melihat dunia terang; ia tidak makan, tidur, atau bernapas (beristirahat), dan mendatangkan angin dan hujan; dialah Zhu Jiuyin (燭九陰), yang disebut Zhulong (燭龍).
statement.en: The Shanhaijing text for the northern wilds describes a red god with a human face and snake body and straight eyes; when he shuts his eyes it is dark and when he looks it is light; he does not eat, sleep or breathe (rest), and he summons wind and rain; he is Zhu Jiuyin (燭九陰), called Zhulong (燭龍).

claims.quote: 少室、太室在冀州。燭龍在雁門北，蔽於委羽之山，不見日，其神人面龍身而無足。

statement.id: Teks Huainanzi menyebut Zhulong (燭龍) berada di utara Yanmen, terlindung oleh Gunung Weiyu sehingga tidak terlihat matahari; dewanya berwajah manusia, bertubuh naga, dan tanpa kaki.
statement.en: The Huainanzi text says Zhulong (燭龍) is north of Yanmen, hidden by Mount Weiyu so that it does not see the sun; its god has a human face and a dragon body and no feet.

short_description.id: Aigamuxa adalah monster pemakan manusia dalam legenda orang Khoikhoi, yang terkenal karena matanya terletak di kaki, bukan di wajah.
short_description.en: The aigamuxa is a man-eating monster from the legends of the Khoikhoi, best known for having its eyes on its feet rather than in its face.

long_description.id: Aigamuxa adalah makhluk legenda orang Khoikhoi. Kisah-kisahnya dikumpulkan oleh Leonhard Schultze-Jena untuk bukunya Aus Namaland und Kalahari. Dalam buku itu, makhluk dongeng ini dikatakan hidup jauh di pedalaman negeri, dan namanya merujuk pada matanya yang berada di punggung kaki, bukan di wajah.
long_description.en: The aigamuxa is a legendary creature of the Khoikhoi. Its tales were gathered by Leonhard Schultze-Jena for his book Aus Namaland und Kalahari. That book places the fabulous being far in the interior of the land and explains that its name refers to its eyes, which sit on the top of its feet instead of in its face.

long_description.id: Karena matanya di kaki, aigamuxa tak dapat melihat mangsanya ketika berburu. Untuk melihat, ia harus bertumpu pada tangan atau kepala, atau berbaring di pasir. Ia hidup di gurun, bersembunyi di balik bukit pasir, dan konon mengincar pengembara yang berjalan sendirian pada malam hari.
long_description.en: Because its eyes are on its feet, the aigamuxa cannot see its prey while it hunts. To look around it must prop itself on its hands or head, or lie down in the sand. It lives in the desert, lurks behind dunes, and is said to stalk travellers walking alone at night.

long_description.id: Makhluk-makhluk ini hidup berkelompok dan memburu manusia, yang mereka kira zebra, lalu mencabiknya dengan gigi panjang yang runcing. Meski buas, mereka digambarkan bodoh dan canggung, sehingga selalu lapar karena jarang berhasil menangkap mangsa. Dalam banyak kisah, manusia cerdik berhasil lolos dari mereka.
long_description.en: These creatures live in groups and hunt people, whom they mistake for zebras, tearing them with long, pointed teeth. Fierce as they are, they are portrayed as dull and clumsy, and so are always hungry because they rarely catch anyone. In many tales, clever humans manage to slip away from them.

long_description.id: Dalam salah satu kisah, Serigala (Jackal) menemukan bahwa mata Aigamuchab ada di kakinya, lalu menaburkan tembakau ke mata itu dan melarikan diri. Dalam cerita-cerita itu, makhluk ini biasanya tampil sangat mirip manusia sehingga korbannya tertipu tentang wujud aslinya.
long_description.en: In one tale the Jackal discovers that Aigamuchab's eyes are on its feet, then scatters tobacco into them and runs off. In these stories the creature usually appears so human-like that its victims are fooled about its true nature.

short_description.id: Alan adalah roh bercacat dalam cerita rakyat suku Tinguian di Filipina, bersayap dan dapat terbang, dengan jari tangan dan kaki yang menghadap ke belakang.
short_description.en: The alan are deformed spirits of Tinguian folklore in the Philippines, winged and able to fly, with fingers and toes pointing backwards.

long_description.id: Alan adalah roh bercacat dalam cerita rakyat suku Tinguian di Filipina. Mereka bersayap dan dapat terbang, dan jari tangan serta kaki mereka menghadap ke belakang. Menurut sebuah koleksi cerita, alan sebesar manusia dan tinggal di hutan; artikel lain menyebut mereka ras makhluk kecil, setengah manusia setengah burung, yang bergantung terbalik dari pohon dan dikabarkan relatif tidak berbahaya.
long_description.en: The alan are deformed spirits in the folklore of the Tinguian people of the Philippines. Winged and able to fly, they have fingers and toes that point backwards. According to one story collection the alan are as large as people and live in the forests; another article calls them a race of small, half-human, half-avian creatures that hang upside down from trees and are rumoured to be relatively harmless.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah-kisah itu alan berulang kali menjadi ibu asuh. Mereka mengambil setetes darah haid, keguguran, atau ari-ari, mengubahnya menjadi anak tanpa sepengetahuan orang tua sebenarnya, dan membesarkannya di rumah emas dekat mata air yang kerikilnya dari emas atau manik-manik. Ketika hubungan darah anak itu terungkap, ia pulang kepada orang tua kandungnya membawa kekayaan itu. Rumah alan tampak mirip tetapi jauh lebih bagus daripada rumah orang-orang Kadalayapan dan Kaodanan.
long_description.en: In the tales the alan repeatedly act as foster mothers. They take a drop of menstrual blood, a miscarriage or afterbirth, change it into a child unknown to the real parents, and raise it in a house of gold near springs whose pebbles are of gold or beads. When the child's blood relationship is established, it goes to its blood parents carrying those riches. Their homes seem much finer than, though otherwise like, those of the people of Kadalayapan and Kaodanan.

long_description.id: Kisah lain menampilkan sisi yang lebih ganas. Dalam "The Alan and the Hunters", seekor alan membantu dua pemburu memotong babi dengan kukunya, tetapi akhirnya jatuh dan mati ketika sulur yang dipanjatnya dipotong. Dalam "Man and the Alan", para alan meratapi lelaki yang dikira mati dan membawa emas serta manik-manik, lalu rumahnya terbakar setelah ia menolak permintaan mereka. Menurut catatan kaki kompilator, orang Tinguian masa kini sering mengolok-olok dan menipu roh yang kurang berkuasa seperti ini dalam upacara.
long_description.en: Other tales show a fiercer side. In "The Alan and the Hunters" an alan helps two hunters cut up a pig with her nails but ends up falling to her death when the vine she climbs is cut. In "Man and the Alan" the alan mourn a man they believe dead and bring gold and beads, then his house burns after he refuses their request. According to the compiler's footnote, the Tinguian today often make fun of and cheat such less powerful spirits at ceremonies.

long_description.id: Menurut seorang penulis, kisah alan berasal dari orang Itneg (Tinguian) di provinsi Abra, Luzon barat laut, dan kadang dikacaukan dengan kisah aran dari orang Isnag. Dalam sebuah karya klasifikasi, alan digabung dengan aran di bawah golongan ogre. Penulis yang sama menyebut kemunculan terbaru alan dalam "The Lost Journal of Alejandro Pardo".
long_description.en: According to one writer, alan stories originate with the Itneg (Tinguian) of Abra province in northwestern Luzon and are sometimes confused with stories of the aran of the Isnag people. In one classification work the alan was combined with the aran under the ogre category. The same writer notes the alan's recent inclusion in "The Lost Journal of Alejandro Pardo".

claims.quote: The Alan are deformed spirits from the folklore of the Tinguian tribe of the Philippines. They have wings and can fly, and their fingers and toes point backwards.

statement.id: Alan adalah roh bercacat dari cerita rakyat suku Tinguian di Filipina, bersayap dan dapat terbang, dengan jari tangan dan kaki menghadap ke belakang.
statement.en: The alan are deformed spirits of Tinguian folklore in the Philippines, winged and able to fly, with fingers and toes pointing backwards.

claims.quote: The Alan are said to take drops of menstrual blood, miscarried fetuses, afterbirth, or other reproductive waste and transform them into human children, whom they then raise as their own. They live near springs in extremely fine houses, made of gold and other valuables.

statement.id: Alan mengambil darah haid, janin keguguran, ari-ari, atau sisa persalinan lain, mengubahnya menjadi anak manusia dan membesarkannya; mereka tinggal di dekat mata air di rumah indah dari emas dan barang berharga.
statement.en: The alan take menstrual blood, miscarried fetuses, afterbirth or other birth remains, turn them into human children and raise them; they live near springs in fine houses of gold and valuables.

claims.quote: The alan, just mentioned, are to-day considered as deformed spirits who live in the forests: “They are as large as people but have wings and can fly; their toes are at the back of their feet and their fingers point backwards from their wrists.”

statement.id: Menurut koleksi ini, alan kini dianggap roh bercacat yang tinggal di hutan: sebesar manusia, bersayap dan dapat terbang, dengan jari kaki di belakang telapak dan jari tangan menghadap ke belakang dari pergelangan.
statement.en: According to this collection the alan are today considered deformed spirits who live in the forests: as large as people, with wings and able to fly, with toes at the back of their feet and fingers pointing backwards from their wrists.

claims.quote: These spirits appear time after time as the foster mothers of the leading characters: Generally they secure a drop of menstrual blood, a miscarriage, or the afterbirth, and all unknown to the real parents, change them into children and raise them

statement.id: Roh-roh ini berulang kali muncul sebagai ibu asuh tokoh-tokoh utama kisah: umumnya mereka mengambil setetes darah haid, keguguran, atau ari-ari, lalu tanpa sepengetahuan orang tua sebenarnya mengubahnya menjadi anak dan membesarkannya.
statement.en: These spirits appear time after time as the foster mothers of the leading characters: generally they secure a drop of menstrual blood, a miscarriage or the afterbirth and, unknown to the real parents, change them into children and raise them.

claims.quote: These foster children are pictured as living in houses of gold situated near springs, the pebbles of which are of gold or beads

statement.id: Anak-anak asuh itu digambarkan tinggal di rumah emas di dekat mata air yang kerikilnya terbuat dari emas atau manik-manik.
statement.en: These foster children are pictured as living in houses of gold situated near springs whose pebbles are of gold or beads.

claims.quote: When the true relationships of these children are established they always go to their blood parents, carrying with them these riches, which are a source of wonder and comment

statement.id: Ketika hubungan darah anak-anak itu terungkap, mereka selalu pergi kepada orang tua kandungnya sambil membawa kekayaan itu, yang menjadi sumber kekaguman dan pembicaraan.
statement.en: When the true relationships of these children are established they always go to their blood parents, carrying these riches with them, which are a source of wonder and comment.

claims.quote: Some of them are addressed as “you alan of the springs,” and in one instance a man dives down into the water where the alan live

statement.id: Sebagian alan disapa sebagai "kalian alan dari mata air", dan dalam satu kisah seorang lelaki menyelam ke air tempat alan tinggal.
statement.en: Some alan are addressed as "you alan of the springs", and in one instance a man dives down into the water where the alan live.

claims.quote: but in general their homes seem to be similar to but much finer than those of the people of Kadalayapan and Kaodanan.

statement.id: Secara umum rumah alan tampak mirip tetapi jauh lebih bagus daripada rumah orang-orang Kadalayapan dan Kaodanan.
statement.en: In general the homes of the alan seem similar to but much finer than those of the people of Kadalayapan and Kaodanan.

claims.quote: Two men went to hunt wild pig. They killed one, but had no fire to singe it, so one man climbed a tree to see if he could see where was a fire. He saw a little fire at a distance and went to get it. When he got where the fire was, he saw it was in the house of an alan.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, dua lelaki berburu babi hutan dan tidak punya api untuk membakar bulunya; salah satunya mencari api dan mendapati api itu berada di rumah seekor alan.
statement.en: In one tale two men hunt wild pig and have no fire to singe it; one goes looking for fire and finds it in the house of an alan.

claims.quote: Then the alan gave him the fire, and she took her big basket and went with him to where the pig was. They singed the pig, and the alan cut it up with her nails. Then she gave the liver to the man, and told him to take it to her house and feed the baby.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, alan memberikan api, ikut membawa keranjang besarnya ke tempat babi, memotong babi dengan kukunya, lalu menyerahkan hati babi kepada lelaki itu untuk diberikan kepada bayinya.
statement.en: In the tale the alan gives him the fire, goes with her big basket to where the pig is, cuts it up with her nails and gives the liver to the man to feed her baby.

claims.quote: “We climbed up feet first.” Then the alan seized a vine and started up the tree feet first. When she had almost reached them, they cut the vine and the alan fell to the ground and was dead. The men came down from the tree and went to the house of the alan. When they got there, they saw three jars: the first was full of dung; the second, of beads; the third, of gold.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, alan memanjat pohon dengan kaki lebih dulu memegang sulur; para lelaki memotong sulur itu sehingga alan jatuh dan mati, lalu mereka mendapati tiga guci di rumahnya: berisi kotoran, manik-manik, dan emas.
statement.en: In the tale the alan climbs the tree feet first on a vine; the men cut the vine so that she falls and dies, and they then find three jars in her house: one of dung, one of beads and one of gold.

claims.quote: a mysterious race of small, deformed half-human, half-avian creatures. Their elongated fingers and feet are said to point backwards, which they use to hang upside down from trees with.

statement.id: Artikel itu menyebut alan sebagai ras misterius makhluk kecil, cacat, setengah manusia setengah burung; jari tangan dan kaki mereka yang panjang dikatakan menghadap ke belakang dan dipakai untuk bergantung terbalik dari pohon.
statement.en: The article describes the alan as a mysterious race of small, deformed half-human, half-avian creatures whose elongated fingers and feet are said to point backwards, which they use to hang upside down from trees.

claims.quote: As horrific as this may sound, they are relatively harmless. They are even rumoured to adopt children who have been lost in the jungle.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, alan relatif tidak berbahaya dan bahkan dikabarkan mengadopsi anak-anak yang tersesat di hutan.
statement.en: According to the article the alan are relatively harmless and are even rumoured to adopt children who have been lost in the jungle.

claims.quote: They are said to procreate by collecting menstrual blood, aborted fetuses, and afterbirth from humans, which they form into Alan children.

statement.id: Alan dikatakan berkembang biak dengan mengumpulkan darah haid, janin yang digugurkan, dan ari-ari dari manusia, yang mereka bentuk menjadi anak-anak alan.
statement.en: The alan are said to procreate by collecting menstrual blood, aborted fetuses and afterbirth from humans, which they form into alan children.

claims.quote: the origin of Alan folktales are with the Itneg people (sometimes referred to as “Tinguian”/“Tingguian”), the Austronesian ethnic group from the upland province of Abra in northwestern Luzon.

statement.id: Menurut penulis, sejauh yang ia temukan, asal kisah alan ada pada orang Itneg (kadang disebut Tinguian atau Tingguian), kelompok etnis Austronesia dari provinsi dataran tinggi Abra di Luzon barat laut.
statement.en: According to the writer, as far as he can find, alan folktales originate with the Itneg people (sometimes called Tinguian or Tingguian), the Austronesian ethnic group from the upland province of Abra in northwestern Luzon.

claims.quote: This is sometimes confused or combined with the stories of the “Aran” (who had cannibalistic tendencies) from the Isnag people

statement.id: Kisah alan kadang dikacaukan atau digabung dengan kisah "aran" (yang berkecenderungan kanibal) dari orang Isnag.
statement.en: Alan stories are sometimes confused or combined with the stories of the "aran" (who had cannibalistic tendencies) from the Isnag people.

claims.quote: In The Creatures of Philippine Lower Mythology the Alan was combined with stories of the Aran – both under the Ogre classification.

statement.id: Dalam The Creatures of Philippine Lower Mythology, alan digabung dengan kisah aran, keduanya di bawah klasifikasi raksasa pemakan manusia (ogre).
statement.en: In The Creatures of Philippine Lower Mythology the alan was combined with stories of the aran, both under the ogre classification.

claims.quote: Activities: An alan hung upside down from a tree like a bat.

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat, seekor alan bergantung terbalik dari pohon seperti kelelawar.
statement.en: In the recorded tales an alan hung upside down from a tree like a bat.

claims.quote: The Alan and the Hunters ... Then the men came down and went to the Alan’s house, where they found a jar full of beads and another of gold, and these they brought with them when they returned home.

statement.id: Dalam versi tutur yang dimuat artikel itu, para lelaki menemukan di rumah alan sebuah guci penuh manik-manik dan satu guci emas.
statement.en: In the retelling printed in the article, the men find in the alan's house a jar full of beads and another of gold.

claims.quote: I’ve always been fascinated with the Alan, and the recent inclusion in “The Lost Journal of Alejandro Pardo” and accompanying artistic imagining by Mervin Malonzo, reinvigorated that interest.

statement.id: Penulis menyebut alan baru-baru ini muncul dalam "The Lost Journal of Alejandro Pardo" dengan gambaran artistik oleh Mervin Malonzo.
statement.en: The writer notes the alan's recent inclusion in "The Lost Journal of Alejandro Pardo", with an artistic imagining by Mervin Malonzo.

claims.quote: In the depths of a dark forest where people seldom went, lived a wizened old Alan.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, seorang alan tua yang keriput tinggal di kedalaman hutan gelap yang jarang dikunjungi orang.
statement.en: In one tale a wizened old alan lived in the depths of a dark forest where people seldom went.

claims.quote: The skin on her wrinkled face was as tough as a carabao hide, and her long arms with fingers pointing back from the wrist were horrible to look at. Now this frightful creature had a son whose name was Sayen, and he was as handsome as his mother was ugly.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, kulit wajah alan yang keriput sekeras kulit kerbau, lengannya panjang dengan jari menghadap ke belakang dari pergelangan, dan ia memiliki putra bernama Sayen yang setampan ibunya seburuk rupa.
statement.en: In the tale the alan's wrinkled face had skin as tough as carabao hide, her long arms had fingers pointing back from the wrist, and she had a son named Sayen who was as handsome as she was ugly.

claims.quote: Man and the Alan ... hanging from the limbs of the tree with their heads down like bats. They had wings to fly, and their toes were at the back of their feet

statement.id: Dalam kisah "Man and the Alan", alan bergantung dari dahan pohon dengan kepala di bawah seperti kelelawar; mereka bersayap untuk terbang dan jari kakinya berada di belakang kaki.
statement.en: In "Man and the Alan" the alan hang from the limbs of a tree with their heads down like bats; they have wings to fly and their toes are at the back of their feet.

claims.quote: At this the Alan began to wail loudly, for they saw him fall and believed him dead And they came down out of the tree with gold and beads which they laid on him.

statement.id: Ketika seorang lelaki jatuh terkapar, para alan meratap keras karena mengira ia mati dan turun dari pohon membawa emas dan manik-manik untuk diletakkan di atasnya.
statement.en: When a man fell on his face the alan wailed loudly, believing him dead, and came down from the tree with gold and beads to lay on him.

claims.quote: When the man refused to do this, they were angry and turned away, crying, "Then we are going to burn your house, for you are a bad man." ... Thereupon the man went home as fast as he could go, but very soon after that his house burned, for the Alan kept their word.

statement.id: Ketika lelaki itu menolak permintaan mereka, para alan marah dan mengancam akan membakar rumahnya; tak lama kemudian rumah itu terbakar karena para alan menepati kata-kata mereka.
statement.en: When the man refused their request the alan were angry and threatened to burn his house; very soon after, his house burned, for the alan kept their word.

claims.quote: This treatment of the Alan is typical of that accorded to the less powerful of the spirits by the Tinguian today. At the ceremonies they often make fun of them and cheat them in the sacrifices.

statement.id: Menurut catatan kaki kompilator, perlakuan terhadap alan lazim diberikan kepada roh yang kurang berkuasa oleh orang Tinguian masa kini: dalam upacara mereka sering mengolok-olok dan menipu roh itu dalam persembahan.
statement.en: According to the compiler's note, this treatment of the alan is typical of that given to the less powerful spirits by the Tinguian today: at ceremonies they often make fun of them and cheat them in the sacrifices.

short_description.id: Amarok adalah serigala raksasa dalam agama Inuit yang dikatakan menguntit dan melahap siapa pun yang berburu sendirian pada malam hari.
short_description.en: The Amarok is a giant wolf of Inuit religion said to track and devour anyone who hunts alone after dark.

long_description.id: Amarok atau Amaroq adalah serigala raksasa dalam agama Inuit. Ia dikatakan menguntit dan melahap siapa pun yang cukup bodoh berburu sendirian pada malam hari, dan berburu sendiri, tidak seperti serigala yang berburu berkawanan. Kata 'amarok' dalam budaya Inuit berarti 'serigala' atau 'roh serigala' dan mencakup esensi spiritual serigala dalam animisme Inuit.
long_description.en: The Amarok, or Amaroq, is a giant wolf of Inuit religion. It is said to track and devour anyone foolish enough to hunt alone after dark, and it hunts alone, unlike wolves that hunt in packs. In Inuit culture the word 'amarok' means 'wolf' or 'wolf spirit' and includes the wolf's spiritual essence in Inuit animism.

long_description.id: Pada abad ke-19, Hinrich Johannes Rink melaporkan bahwa Inuit Greenland memakai kata Amarok khusus untuk serigala legendaris ini, sedangkan bangsa Arktik lain memakainya untuk serigala mana pun. Dalam bukunya Tales and Traditions of the Eskimo, Rink menceritakan beberapa legenda; dalam satu kisah seorang anak kerdil yang dianiaya memanggil penguasa kekuatan dan seekor Amarok menjatuhkannya dengan ekor, melepaskan tulang kecil dari tubuhnya; setelah berlatih bergulat setiap hari ia cukup kuat mengalahkan tiga beruang besar.
long_description.en: In the 19th century Hinrich Johannes Rink reported that Greenlandic Inuit keep the word Amarok for this legendary wolf alone, while other Arctic peoples apply it to any wolf. Rink's Tales and Traditions of the Eskimo retells several folk legends featuring it; in one a persecuted, stunted boy calls on the lord of strength and an Amarok wrestles him down with its tail, loosening small bones from his body; after daily wrestling he is strong enough to overcome three large bears.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah lain, seorang pria yang berduka mencari Amarok bersama seorang kerabat, menemukan anak-anaknya, dan membunuh semuanya. Amarok menyasar pemburu manusia atau kawanan serigala yang sendirian atau ceroboh keluar pada malam hari, dan sumber lain menyebut makhluk Inuit ini tampak berkaitan erat dengan Waheela.
long_description.en: In another story a mourning man searches for an Amarok with a relative, finds her pups instead, and kills them all. It targets human hunters or wolf packs who are alone or careless enough to come out at night, and another source says this Inuit creature appears closely related to the Waheela.

short_description.id: Andrealphus adalah iblis dalam demonologi Eropa yang menurut Goetia berpangkat markis, tampil sebagai merak bersuara gaduh, lalu berwujud manusia dan mengajarkan geometri.
short_description.en: Andrealphus is a demon in European demonology who, according to the Goetia, holds the rank of marquis, appears as a noisy peacock, then takes human form and teaches geometry.

long_description.id: Andrealphus (juga ditulis Androalphus) adalah iblis dalam demonologi Eropa. Menurut Goetia, ia menempati urutan ke-65 di antara roh-roh yang dikenal dalam tradisi itu, berpangkat markis agung, dan memimpin 30 legiun.
long_description.en: Andrealphus (also written Androalphus) is a demon in European demonology. According to the Goetia he is the 65th of its spirits, a great marquis who commands 30 legions.

long_description.id: Teks Goetia melukiskan bahwa ia mula-mula tampil sebagai merak disertai bunyi gaduh, kemudian mengenakan wujud manusia. Ia dikatakan dapat mengajarkan geometri dan segala hal tentang pengukuran serta astronomi, dan dapat mengubah manusia menjadi rupa burung.
long_description.en: The Goetia describes him appearing at first as a peacock with great noises, then putting on human shape. He is said to teach geometry and everything belonging to measuring, as well as astronomy, and to transform a man into the likeness of a bird.

long_description.id: Pseudomonarchia Daemonum karya Weyer, dalam terjemahan Scot, memuat uraian serupa. Penyunting Goetia mencatat bahwa nama itu tertulis Androalphus pada Weyer dan Andrealphus pada Scot. Collin de Plancy, menurut sumber Jepang, menyebutnya penyebar dalih yang berbelit.
long_description.en: Weyer's Pseudomonarchia Daemonum, in Scot's translation, contains a similar description. The Goetia's editor notes that the name is written Androalphus in Weyer and Andrealphus in Scot. According to the Japanese source, Collin de Plancy called him a preacher of sophistry.

long_description.id: Dalam okultisme populer Jepang, penulis 江口之隆 menambahkan penggambaran sendiri tentang wujud manusianya; ini bukan bagian dari teks tradisional.
long_description.en: In Japanese popular occultism, the writer 江口之隆 added his own description of the demon's human form; this is not part of the traditional texts.

claims.quote: Andrealphus [*Androalphus] is a great marquesse, appearing as a pecocke, he raiseth great [*bass, heavy] noises, and in humane shape perfectlie teacheth geometrie

statement.id: Dalam Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (terjemahan Scot), Andrealphus adalah markis agung yang tampil sebagai merak, menimbulkan bunyi berat, dan dalam wujud manusia mengajarkan geometri dengan sempurna.
statement.en: In the Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (Scot's translation) Andrealphus is a great marquis who appears as a peacock, raises great heavy noises, and in human shape perfectly teaches geometry.

claims.quote: he maketh a man to be a subtill disputer, and cunning in astronomie, and transformeth a man into the likenes of a bird, and there are under him thirtie legions.

statement.id: Teks Weyer-Scot menambahkan bahwa ia membuat orang menjadi pendebat yang halus dan cerdik dalam astronomi, mengubah manusia menjadi rupa burung, dan memiliki tiga puluh legiun di bawahnya.
statement.en: The Weyer-Scot text adds that he makes a man a subtle disputer and cunning in astronomy, transforms a man into the likeness of a bird, and has thirty legions under him.

text.en: Appears in traditions from the medieval period onward; recorded in the Taiheiki

short_description.id: Azumi no Isora adalah dewa laut dalam tradisi Shinto yang dianggap leluhur klan Azumi dan dipuja di sejumlah kuil. Dalam legenda abad pertengahan ia membantu Permaisuri Jingū dengan permata pasang-surut dari istana naga.
short_description.en: Azumi no Isora is a sea deity in the Shinto tradition, regarded as an ancestor of the Azumi people and worshiped at several shrines. In medieval legend he helps Empress Jingū with tide jewels from the dragon palace.

long_description.id: Azumi no Isora (阿曇磯良) adalah kami pantai dalam tradisi Shinto, dianggap sebagai dewa laut dan leluhur suku maupun klan Azumi. Ia juga dikenal dengan nama Atobe no Isora dan Isotakera, dan kamus Nihon Kokugo Daijiten menyebutnya dewa dasar laut yang konon tinggal di Chikuzen.
long_description.en: Azumi no Isora (阿曇磯良) is a kami of the seashore in the Shinto tradition, regarded as a sea deity and as an ancestor of the Azumi people and clan. He is also known as Atobe no Isora and Isotakera, and the Nihon Kokugo Daijiten calls him a god of the sea floor said to live in Chikuzen.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Taiheiki, ketika Permaisuri Jingū memanggil para dewa untuk persiapan ke Tiga Han, hanya Atobe no Isora yang tidak datang. Para dewa memainkan musik dan menyanyi, lalu ia muncul dengan tubuh yang ditempeli kerang dan serangga laut. Ia kemudian diutus meminjam permata surut dan pasang dari istana naga, dan dewa naga menyerahkannya.
long_description.en: In the Taiheiki account, when Empress Jingū gathered the gods in preparation for the Three Han, only Atobe no Isora failed to come. The gods played music and sang, and he showed up with shellfish and sea insects clinging to his body. He was then sent to borrow the ebb and flood tide jewels from the dragon palace, and the dragon god handed them over.

long_description.id: Situs resmi Kuil Shikaumi menyebut Permaisuri Jingū memanggil Azumi no Isora dari Pulau Shika sehingga menerima permata dari dewa naga. Isora dipuja antara lain di Kuil Mekari di Kitakyushu, Kuil Shikaumi di Pulau Shika, dan Kuil Shiga di Tsushima. Satu legenda yang lebih belakangan menempatkannya sebagai dewa laut tingkat rendah yang disewa menjadi pemandu perjalanan utusan Takenouchi no Sukune menuju Raja Naga.
long_description.en: The official Shikaumi Shrine site says Empress Jingū summoned Azumi no Isora of Shika Island and thereby received the jewels from the dragon god. Isora is worshiped at shrines including Mekari Shrine in Kitakyushu, Shikaumi Shrine on Shika Island and Shiga Shrine on Tsushima. One later legend casts him as a minor sea deity engaged as guide for the emissary Takenouchi no Sukune on the way to the Dragon King.

long_description.id: Legenda ini hidup dalam ritual: tradisi Tarian Isora diwariskan di 風浪宮, 高祖神社, dan Iwato Kagura, dan di Kasuga Taisha tarian itu dipersembahkan sebagai tarian Seinō oleh para penari berpenutup wajah kain putih. Sumber-sumber berbeda tentang hakikatnya; lihat bagian perbedaan sumber.
long_description.en: The legend lives on in ritual: the Isora dance tradition is handed down at 風浪宮, 高祖神社 and the Iwato Kagura, and at Kasuga Taisha it is offered as the Seinō dance by dancers in white-cloth masks. Sources differ on his nature; see the conflicts section.

cultural_context.id: Kisah Isora dan permata pasang-surut diperingati melalui tarian ritual di beberapa tempat di Fukuoka dan di Kasuga Taisha (Nara), sehingga legenda itu tetap hadir dalam upacara kuil.
cultural_context.en: The story of Isora and the tide jewels is commemorated through ritual dances at several places in Fukuoka and at Kasuga Taisha (Nara), keeping the legend present in shrine ceremonies.

who.id: Dewa laut Shinto yang dianggap leluhur klan Azumi.
who.en: A Shinto sea deity regarded as an ancestor of the Azumi clan.

origin.id: Dikenal dalam tradisi Jepang, dicatat dalam Taiheiki dan dipuja di Kuil Shikaumi di Pulau Shika, Fukuoka.
origin.en: Known in Japanese tradition, recorded in the Taiheiki and worshiped at Shikaumi Shrine on Shika Island, Fukuoka.

role.id: Dalam legenda ia membantu Permaisuri Jingū dengan membawa permata pasang-surut dari istana naga.
role.en: In legend he assists Empress Jingū by bringing the tide jewels from the dragon palace.

famous_for.id: Dikenal karena rupanya yang tertutup kerang dan karena legenda permata pasang-surut.
famous_for.en: Known for his shell-covered appearance and for the legend of the tide jewels.

did_you_know.id: Di Kasuga Taisha, para penari Seinō memakai penutup wajah kain putih untuk menggambarkan Isora yang menyembunyikan wajahnya yang ditempeli kerang.
did_you_know.en: At Kasuga Taisha the Seinō dancers wear white-cloth masks to depict Isora hiding his shell-covered face.

role.id: Dewa dasar laut yang dipanggil para dewa dan menjadi utusan ke istana naga.
role.en: The sea-floor deity whom the gods lure out and who becomes the messenger to the dragon palace.

summary.id: Atobe no Isora tidak menghadiri pertemuan para dewa karena rupanya yang ditempeli kerang, tetapi datang setelah para dewa memainkan musik. Ia lalu menjadi utusan yang meminjam permata surut dan pasang dari dewa naga untuk Permaisuri Jingū.
summary.en: Atobe no Isora does not attend the gods' assembly, but comes after the gods play music; shellfish cling to his body. He then becomes the messenger who borrows the ebb and flood jewels from the dragon god for Empress Jingū.

description.id: Kuil di Pulau Shika, Fukuoka, yang menurut kamus Nihon Kokugo Daijiten memuja Isora, dan yang situsnya menyebut Isora dipanggil dari pulau itu oleh Permaisuri Jingū.
description.en: The shrine on Shika Island, Fukuoka, which the Nihon Kokugo Daijiten gives as enshrining Isora, and whose site says Empress Jingū summoned Isora of the island.

description.id: Menurut situs Kuil Shikaumi, di sinilah kagura dimainkan tujuh hari tujuh malam untuk memanggil Azumi no Isora dari negeri laut.
description.en: According to the Shikaumi Shrine site, this is where kagura was played for seven days and nights to summon Azumi no Isora from the sea country.

description.id: Salah satu kuil yang memuja Isora menurut sumber ensiklopedia daring.
description.en: One of the shrines that worship Isora according to an online encyclopedia source.

description.id: Tempat Isora juga dipuja dan Tarian Isora dipersembahkan pada festival Kasuga Wakamiya On-matsuri.
description.en: Where Isora is also enshrined and the Isora dance is offered at the Kasuga Wakamiya On-matsuri festival.

note.id: Dalam legenda belakangan, Isora diperkenalkan sebagai pemandu untuk membawa utusan Takenouchi no Sukune menemui Raja Naga.
note.en: In the later legend, Isora serves as navigator to bring the emissary Takenouchi no Sukune to the Dragon King.

note.id: Hachiman Gudokun menyatakan Isora sama dengan Ame no Koyane yang dipuja di Kasuga Taisha.
note.en: The Hachiman Gudokun states that Isora is the same deity as Ame no Koyane, enshrined at Kasuga Taisha.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa sebuah legenda tentang dewa laut dapat terus dihidupkan melalui tarian dan festival kuil?
learning_questions.en: Why might a legend about a sea deity be kept alive through dances and shrine festivals?

learning_questions.id: Bagaimana sumber yang berbeda (kuil, kisah abad pertengahan, ensiklopedia) menggambarkan sosok yang sama?
learning_questions.en: How do different kinds of sources (shrine, medieval tale, encyclopedia) describe the same figure?

claims.quote: 阿曇磯良（あづみのいそら、安曇磯良とも書く）は、神道の神である。海の神とされ、また、安曇氏（阿曇氏）の祖神とされる。阿度部磯良（あとべのいそら）や磯武良（いそたけら）とも。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang: Azumi no Isora (juga ditulis 安曇磯良) adalah dewa Shinto, dianggap dewa laut dan leluhur klan Azumi; ia juga disebut Atobe no Isora dan Isotakera.

claims.quote: また、『八幡愚童訓』では、磯良は春日大社に祀られる天児屋根命と同神であるとしている。

statement.id: Hachiman Gudokun menyatakan bahwa Isora adalah dewa yang sama dengan Ame no Koyane yang dipuja di Kasuga Taisha.
statement.en: The Hachiman Gudokun states that Isora is the same deity as Ame no Koyane, who is enshrined at Kasuga Taisha.

claims.quote: この地方では福岡県大川市の風浪宮や、糸島市の高祖神社（高祖神楽）、那珂川市の岩戸神楽にも磯良の舞の伝承が伝わる。

statement.id: Tradisi Tarian Isora juga diwariskan di 風浪宮 (Kota Ōkawa, Prefektur Fukuoka), Kuil 高祖神社 (Itoshima; 高祖神楽), dan Iwato Kagura di Nakagawa.
statement.en: The tradition of the Isora dance is also handed down at 風浪宮 in Ōkawa, Fukuoka Prefecture, at 高祖神社 in Itoshima (高祖神楽), and in the Iwato Kagura of Nakagawa.

claims.quote: 磯良の明神は上述したように奈良春日大社でも祀られており、春日若宮おん祭の細男（せいのう/せいのお/さいのお）と称して磯良の舞が奉納される。

statement.id: Isora juga dipuja di Kasuga Taisha di Nara, tempat Tarian Isora dipersembahkan sebagai tarian Seinō pada festival Kasuga Wakamiya On-matsuri.
statement.en: Isora is also enshrined at Kasuga Taisha in Nara, where the Isora dance is offered as the Seinō dance at the Kasuga Wakamiya On-matsuri festival.

claims.quote: 春日大社のそれは、筑紫の浜で老人から「細男の舞をすれば、磯良が出てきて干珠・満珠を授ける」と聞いた神功皇后が舞わせたところ、貝殻のついた醜い顔を白布で隠した磯良が現れたという物語を表現したもので、白布の覆面姿の男たちが舞う。

statement.id: Tarian di Kasuga Taisha menggambarkan kisah ketika Permaisuri Jingū, setelah mendengar dari seorang tua di pantai Tsukushi bahwa menari Seinō akan memunculkan Isora yang memberi permata, menyuruh orang menari lalu Isora yang menyembunyikan wajah buruk berkerang dengan kain putih muncul; para penari memakai penutup wajah kain putih.
statement.en: The Kasuga Taisha dance depicts the story in which Empress Jingū, told by an old man on the Tsukushi shore that dancing the Seinō would make Isora appear and grant the jewels, had it danced and Isora appeared hiding his ugly shell-covered face with white cloth; the dancers wear white-cloth masks.

claims.quote: 神功皇后は三韓出兵に際して、志賀島の阿曇磯良を召されました。そして龍神より干珠満珠を授かり、無事に三韓を平定して帰還されました。

statement.id: Menurut situs resmi Kuil Shikaumi, saat mengirim pasukan ke Tiga Han, Permaisuri Jingū memanggil Azumi no Isora dari Pulau Shika, menerima permata surut dan pasang dari dewa naga, lalu kembali setelah menaklukkan Tiga Han.
statement.en: According to the official Shikaumi Shrine site, when sending forces to the Three Han Empress Jingū summoned Azumi no Isora of Shika Island, received the ebb and flood tide jewels from the dragon god, and returned after pacifying the Three Han.

claims.quote: 二世紀から四世紀の間に表津宮を勝山の麓である現在の場所に遷座し、併せて仲津綿津見神、表津綿津見神が奉祀されたと伝えられています。綿津見三神を祖神とする阿曇族が代々奉斎してきました。

statement.id: Menurut tradisi kuil, antara abad ke-2 dan ke-4 kuil 表津宮 dipindahkan ke lokasi sekarang di kaki 勝山, dan suku Azumi, yang menjadikan tiga dewa 綿津見三神 sebagai leluhur, melayani kuil itu turun-temurun.
statement.en: According to shrine tradition, between the second and fourth centuries the shrine 表津宮 was moved to its present site at the foot of 勝山, and the Azumi people, who take the three 綿津見三神 deities as ancestral deities, have served the shrine for generations.

claims.quote: 阿曇磯良を海国から召し出そうと7日7晩神楽を奏したところが舞能ヶ浜、志賀島にお着きになり願いがかなったと仰せられたところが叶ヶ浜、皇后が馬から下りられたところが下馬ヶ浜、志賀大明神に奉賽した際に馬が喜びいなないたので勝馬となったといわれています。

statement.id: Di Pulau Shika, tempat kagura dimainkan tujuh hari tujuh malam untuk memanggil Azumi no Isora dari negeri laut disebut 舞能ヶ浜; tempat sang permaisuri turun dari kuda disebut 下馬ヶ浜, dan tempat kuda meringkik gembira disebut 勝馬.
statement.en: On Shika Island, the place where kagura was played for seven days and nights to summon Azumi no Isora from the sea country is called 舞能ヶ浜; the place where the empress dismounted is 下馬ヶ浜, and the place where the horse whinnied with joy is 勝馬.

claims.quote: 皇后諸の天神地祇を請じ給ふに、日本一万の大小の神祇冥道、皆勅請に随て常陸の鹿島に来給ふ。雖然、海底に迹を垂給阿度部の磯良一人不応召。

statement.id: Menurut Taiheiki, Permaisuri Jingū memanggil para dewa langit dan bumi ke Kashima di Hitachi; semuanya datang, kecuali Atobe no Isora yang menampakkan diri di dasar laut.
statement.en: According to the Taiheiki, Empress Jingū summoned the gods of heaven and earth to Kashima in Hitachi; all came except Atobe no Isora, who had manifested himself on the sea floor.

claims.quote: 磯良感に堪兼て、神遊の庭にぞ参たる。其貌を御覧ずるに、細螺・石花貝・藻に棲虫、手足五体に取付て、更に人の形にては無りけり。

statement.id: Taiheiki mencatat bahwa setelah para dewa menyanyi, Isora tak tahan lagi dan datang ke tempat pesta dewa; tubuhnya ditempeli kerang, kerang laut, dan serangga rumput laut sehingga sama sekali tidak tampak seperti manusia.
statement.en: The Taiheiki records that, after the gods sang, Isora could not hold back and came to the gods' playing ground; shellfish, clams and seaweed-dwelling insects clung to his body so that he did not look like a human at all.

claims.quote: 軈て是を御使にて、竜宮城に宝とする干珠・満珠を被借召。竜神即応神勅二の玉を奉る。

statement.id: Isora kemudian dijadikan utusan untuk meminjam permata surut dan pasang (kanju dan manju) yang menjadi harta istana naga; dewa naga segera menyerahkan kedua permata itu.
statement.en: Isora was then made the messenger to borrow the ebb and flood jewels (kanju and manju) treasured in the dragon palace, and the dragon god promptly presented the two jewels.

claims.quote: 中世以降の伝承に現れる古代の精霊。阿度部（あとべの）磯良ともいう。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典

statement.id: Menurut Heibonsha (Sekai Daihyakka Jiten), ia adalah roh kuno yang muncul dalam tradisi sejak abad pertengahan, dan juga disebut Atobe no Isora.
statement.en: According to Heibonsha's encyclopedia, he is an ancient spirit who appears in traditions from the medieval period onward, and is also called Atobe no Isora.

claims.quote: 安曇氏は海人（あま）を宰領した古代豪族で，おそらく安曇磯良は海人の間に伝承された半神半人のシャーマンであったかと思われる。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典

statement.id: Penulis ensiklopedia Heibonsha menafsirkan bahwa klan Azumi adalah bangsawan kuno pemimpin para ama (pelaut dan penyelam), dan Isora mungkin seorang syaman setengah dewa setengah manusia yang diwariskan di antara mereka.
statement.en: The Heibonsha encyclopedia's author interprets the Azumi as an ancient clan that supervised the ama (sea people), and Isora as probably a half-divine, half-human shaman handed down among them.

claims.quote: 筑前に住むといわれた海底の神。福岡市東区志賀島の志賀海神社の祭神。「九州道の記」「八幡愚童訓」に所見。
claims.locator: 精選版 日本国語大辞典

statement.id: Nihon Kokugo Daijiten menyebutnya dewa dasar laut yang konon tinggal di Chikuzen dan dewa utama Kuil Shikaumi di Pulau Shika, Fukuoka; ia tercantum dalam 「九州道の記」 dan 「八幡愚童訓」.
statement.en: The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten calls him a god of the sea floor said to live in Chikuzen and the enshrined deity of Shikaumi Shrine on Shika Island, Fukuoka; he is attested in 「九州道の記」 and the 「八幡愚童訓」.

items.prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mythics illustration of AZUMI-NO-ISORA as recorded in the TAIHEIKI, the Shinto sea-floor deity returning as messenger with TWO tide jewels.
ANATOMY: ONE venerable head, TWO arms TWO legs, entire body and face densely encrusted with shellfish, clams and tiny seaweed-dwelling insects so he hardly looks human at all. Opaque dark high-neck robe covers chest and pelvis beneath shells. TWO natural eyes glimpsed between shell clusters, no horns, wings or added mouths. Exactly TWO jewels: one amber stone gripped by one closed hand and one dark green stone in the other closed hand, fingers naturally curled and occluded. [azumi-no-isora-c14,c15]
MOMENT: rising out of seawater and advancing toward the viewer to PRESENT the two nonluminous jewels obtained from the dragon palace; cascades drain from his shell-covered shoulders, authoritative sacred messenger, not a zombie. [azumi-no-isora-c13,c14,c15]
POWER: seawater splashes only from his physical arrival from sea floor. No invented tide-controlling effect, no glowing jewel beams. The two gems are borrowed ebb and flood jewels. [azumi-no-isora-c13,c15]
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle at water surface; huge-in-frame shell-covered face and two gem-bearing clenched hands dominate, actual body scale unspecified.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one low warm sun shaft cutting deep walnut storm shadows, spray and flowing water catch the rim.
SURFACE: heavy wet shells, ridged clams, dark coarse cloth, small crustacean-like seaweed insects; realistic marine encrustation, no gore.
SETTING: sea margin editorial transition from the sea floor to gods' meeting-ground. [azumi-no-isora-c13,c14]
MOOD: sacred, reverent, imposing and awe-inspiring, not evil monster, ordinary fisherman or shell statue.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: square at least1024px; no text, lettering, glyphs, inscriptions, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from films, games, anime or comics; no nudity, exposed breasts or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outlines, floating runes or energy ribbons.

visual_requirements.description: Sosok encrusted kerang, clam dan serangga rumput laut sehingga tidak seperti manusia.
Muncul dari tempat laut menuju pertemuan dewa dan membawa dua permata yang diterima dari dragon palace.
Tepi laut sebagai transisi visual dari dasar laut menuju playing ground dewa.

items.aura: Keagungan messenger Shinto datang dari kemunculan tubuh berkerang dari laut dan dua permata pasang-surut (azumi-no-isora-c13, azumi-no-isora-c14, azumi-no-isora-c15), tanpa mengarang kendali gelombang.

visual_review.notes: Native dan 200px diperiksa: kepala tunggal bermata dua, tubuh penuh shellfish/clams dan serangga laut sehingga bukan orang biasa, dua tangan berkepalan dengan dua permata nonluminous. Kemunculan/cipratan fisik laut dan presentasi permata sesuai azumi-no-isora-c13/c14/c15; tanpa klaim tide-control tambahan, mask dance, glyph, gore atau anatomi ekstra. Keagungan reverent kuat.

cultural_context.id: Dalam catatan yang dikutip Skeat, tuduhan memelihara bajang dapat berujung pada hukuman berat atau pengusiran terhadap tertuduh, dan bajang dipandang sebagai penyebab penyakit tak terjelaskan.
cultural_context.en: In the account quoted by Skeat, an accusation of keeping a bajang could lead to severe punishment or expulsion of the accused, and the bajang was seen as the cause of unexplained illness.

short_description.id: Bajang adalah makhluk halus dalam kepercayaan Melayu, roh jahat yang biasanya berwujud musang dan dipelihara untuk mencelakai musuh, serta dianggap sangat berbahaya bagi anak-anak.
short_description.en: The bajang is a spirit of Malay belief, a malign spirit usually taking the form of a pole-cat, kept to harm enemies and considered very dangerous to children.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan Melayu, bajang adalah sejenis makhluk halus dari golongan jin atau setan yang dipelihara untuk mencelakai musuh. Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Melayu ia dipuja dari mayat bayi yang lahir mati, setan jantan yang sering menjelma kucing musang, sering menyerang anak-anak, dan dapat menyebabkan penyakit misterius yang mematikan. Kamus Dewan mendefinisikannya sebagai hantu berkuku panjang yang suka mengganggu perempuan hamil atau kanak-kanak.
long_description.en: In Malay belief, the bajang is a kind of spirit of the jinn or devil class kept in order to harm enemies. According to Wikipedia it is raised from the corpse of a stillborn baby, a male devil that often takes the form of a pole-cat, frequently attacks children and can cause mysterious fatal illness. The Kamus Dewan defines it as a long-nailed ghost that likes to disturb pregnant women or children.

long_description.id: Pemiliknya menyimpan bajang di dalam tabung buluh yang disumbat daun khusus dan dikunci dengan tangkal, dan hanya mengeluarkannya untuk mengenai musuh. Bajang diberi makan telur dan susu; bila diabaikan, ia dapat menyerang tuannya, dan tuan yang belum menemukan penerima konon sukar mati. Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Melayu tidak ada cara membunuh bajang, dan tuannya yang diketahui biasanya dibunuh atau diusir dari kampung.
long_description.en: Its owner keeps the bajang in a bamboo tube stoppered with a special leaf and locked with a charm, releasing it only to strike at enemies. The bajang is fed eggs and milk; if neglected it may attack its master, and a master who has found no one to take it over is said to find it hard to die. According to Wikipedia there is no way to kill a bajang, and a master who is identified is usually killed or driven out of the village.

long_description.id: Walter William Skeat, dalam Malay Magic, mencatat bajang sebagai salah satu dari empat roh kelahiran yang biasanya berwujud musang dan mengganggu rumah tangga dengan mengeong seperti kucing besar. Seorang dukun Melayu pernah mengatakan kepadanya bahwa bajang dapat berwujud jangkrik rumah dan dipelihara oleh laki-laki, tetapi ia menilai keterangan itu tak boleh diterima begitu saja. Anak-anak kadang diberi gelang benang sutra hitam yang disebut gelang bajang untuk melindungi mereka.
long_description.en: Walter William Skeat, in Malay Magic, recorded the bajang as one of four birth-spirits that usually takes the form of a pole-cat and disturbs the household by mewing like a great cat. A Malay magician told him the bajang could take the form of a house-cricket and be kept by a man, though he judged that statement should not be accepted without reserve. Children are sometimes given an armlet of black silk threads called a bajang bracelet to protect them.

long_description.id: Sebuah catatan yang dikutip Skeat menggambarkan korban jatuh sakit dengan gejala tak lazim, seperti kejang, pingsan, atau mengigau, lalu muncul dugaan bahwa ia korban bajang dan siapa pemiliknya. Menurut catatan itu, seorang pawang dapat mengikis bejana besi dengan pisau cukur sehingga rambut pelaku rontok, pelaku yang dianggap terbukti dahulu dibunuh, dan di Perak penduduk sebuah kampung pernah menghanyutkan seorang lelaki yang dituduh memelihara bajang bersama keluarganya. Bajang warisan disebut datang dari leluhur, sedangkan bajang yang diperoleh diambil dari jasad bayi lahir mati yang baru dikubur.
long_description.en: An account quoted by Skeat describes a victim falling ill with unusual symptoms such as convulsions, unconsciousness or delirium, after which the suspicion arises that the victim is under a bajang and who the owner is. In that account, a pawang can scrape an iron vessel with a razor so that the culprit's hair falls off, culprits whose guilt was held to be established were formerly killed, and in Perak the people of a village once sent a man accused of keeping a bajang down the river with his family. A hereditary bajang is said to come from ancestors, while an acquired one is taken from the newly buried body of a stillborn child.

long_description.id: Di seluruh Semenanjung bajang dikatakan berjenis kelamin laki-laki dan umumnya dipercaya sebagai roh jahat yang menghantui manusia dan pertanda malapetaka; di Perak dan beberapa tempat lain ia dipandang sebagai iblis yang dapat diperbudak menjadi roh peliharaan dan diwariskan dalam keluarga. Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, dahulu benda logam tajam seperti gunting diletakkan di dekat bayi sebagai perlindungan, dan garis regangan kehamilan setengah bercanda disebut bekas serangan bajang.
long_description.en: Across the Peninsula the bajang is said to be male and is usually believed to be a malignant spirit that haunts mankind and foretells disaster; in Perak and some other parts it is regarded as a demon that can be enslaved as a familiar spirit and handed down in families. According to Wikipedia, sharp metal objects such as scissors were formerly placed near babies as protection, and the striations of pregnancy are somewhat jokingly said to be scars left by a bajang's attack.

statement.en: Walter William Skeat in Malay Magic (1900) lists four birth-spirits; one is the bajang, usually a pole-cat that disturbs the household by mewing like a great cat.

claims.quote: Thus a Malay magician once told me that the Bajang took the form of a house-cricket, and that when thus embodied it may be kept by a man, as the Pĕlĕsit may be kept by a woman.

statement.id: Di seluruh Semenanjung Malaya bajang dianggap laki-laki dan langsuir perempuan; orang Melayu umumnya percaya bajang roh jahat yang menghantui manusia dan kehadirannya pertanda malapetaka.
statement.en: Across the Malay Peninsula the bajang is male and the langsuir female; Malays generally believe the bajang is a malignant spirit haunting people, its presence foretelling disaster.

statement.en: In that account, relatives call a native doctor and an impression arises that the patient is the victim of a bajang; the impression quickly becomes certainty and any trifle may point to the owner of the evil spirit.

claims.quote: he will place the sorcerer in one room, and, while he in another scrapes an iron vessel with a razor, the culprit’s hair will fall off as though the razor had been applied to his head instead of to the vessel

statement.id: Menurut catatan itu, seorang pawang menaruh tersangka di satu ruangan dan mengikis bejana besi dengan pisau cukur di ruangan lain; rambut pelaku dikatakan rontok seolah-olah pisau dipakai pada kepalanya.
statement.en: According to that account, a pawang places the suspected sorcerer in one room and scrapes an iron vessel with a razor in another; the culprit's hair is said to fall off as if the razor had been used on his head.

claims.quote: Before the advent of British influence it was the practice to kill the wizard or witch whose guilt had been established to Malay satisfaction, and such executions were carried out not many years ago.

statement.id: Menurut catatan itu, sebelum pengaruh Inggris datang, penyihir yang kesalahannya terbukti menurut kepuasan orang Melayu biasanya dibunuh, dan hukuman mati itu masih dilakukan belum lama berselang.
statement.en: According to that account, before British influence arrived the practice was to kill the wizard or witch whose guilt was established to Malay satisfaction, and such executions were carried out not many years earlier.

claims.quote: I remember a case in Perak less than ten years ago, when the people of an up-river village accused a man of keeping a bâjang ... Before anything could be done they put him, his family, and effects on a raft and started them down the river.

statement.id: Catatan itu menceritakan kasus di Perak kurang dari sepuluh tahun sebelumnya: penduduk sebuah kampung hulu sungai menuduh seorang lelaki memelihara bajang, lalu menaikkannya bersama keluarga dan hartanya ke rakit dan menghanyutkannya ke hilir sungai.
statement.en: The account tells of a case in Perak less than ten years earlier: the people of an up-river village accused a man of keeping a bajang and put him, his family and his effects on a raft and sent them down the river.

claims.quote: The hereditary bâjang comes like other evils, the unsought heritage of a dissolute ancestry, but the acquired bâjang is usually obtained from the newly-buried body of a stillborn child, which is supposed to be the abiding-place of a familiar spirit until lured therefrom by the solicitations of some one who, at dead of night, stands over the grave

statement.id: Menurut catatan itu, bajang warisan datang sebagai pusaka tak dikehendaki dari leluhur yang bejat, sedangkan bajang yang diperoleh biasanya diambil dari jasad bayi lahir mati yang baru dikubur, yang dianggap tempat tinggal roh peliharaan sampai dibujuk keluar oleh orang yang berdiri di atas kubur pada tengah malam.
statement.en: According to that account, the hereditary bajang is the unsought heritage of a dissolute ancestry, while the acquired bajang is usually obtained from the newly buried body of a stillborn child, thought to house a familiar spirit until lured out by someone standing over the grave at dead of night.

claims.quote: I have also been assured that the bâjang, in the shape of a lizard, has been seen to issue from the drowning person’s nose.

statement.id: Penulis catatan itu mengaku diyakinkan bahwa bajang, berbentuk kadal, pernah terlihat keluar dari hidung orang yang ditenggelamkan.
statement.en: The account's author says he was assured that the bajang, in the shape of a lizard, has been seen to issue from the nose of the person being drowned.

claims.quote: In Perak and some other parts of the Peninsula, however, the Bajang is regarded as one of the several kinds of demons which, the Malays hold, can be enslaved by man and become his familiar spirit. Such familiars, it is believed, are handed down in certain families as heirlooms.

statement.id: Di Perak dan beberapa tempat lain di Semenanjung, bajang dipandang sebagai salah satu iblis yang menurut orang Melayu dapat diperbudak manusia dan menjadi roh peliharaannya; roh semacam itu dipercaya diwariskan dalam keluarga tertentu sebagai pusaka.
statement.en: In Perak and some other parts of the Peninsula the bajang is regarded as one of the demons that, the Malays hold, can be enslaved by man and become his familiar spirit; such familiars are believed to be handed down in certain families as heirlooms.

claims.quote: The familiar is fed with eggs and milk. When its master wishes to make use of it he sends it forth to possess and prey upon the vitals of any one whom his malice may select as a victim.

statement.id: Roh peliharaan itu diberi makan telur dan susu; bila tuannya hendak memakainya, ia dikirim untuk merasuki dan memangsa isi tubuh korban yang dipilih tuannya karena dendam.
statement.en: The familiar is fed eggs and milk; when its master wishes to use it he sends it forth to possess and prey upon the vitals of a victim chosen out of malice.

claims.quote: The individual thus persecuted is at once seized by a deadly and unaccountable ailment, which can only be cured by magic agencies. If the Bajang is neglected by its owner, and if the latter omits to feed it regularly, it is said that he often falls a victim to his own familiar.

statement.id: Korban langsung diserang penyakit mematikan yang tak terjelaskan dan hanya dapat disembuhkan dengan kekuatan gaib; bila bajang diabaikan dan tidak diberi makan teratur, pemiliknya konon sering menjadi korban roh peliharaannya sendiri.
statement.en: The victim is at once seized by a deadly, unaccountable ailment that can only be cured by magic; if the bajang is neglected and not fed regularly, its owner is said often to fall victim to his own familiar.

claims.quote: which appears to represent the outline of a Bajang, “scripturally” modified to serve as a counter-charm against the Bajang itself.

statement.id: Skeat memuat gambar yang tampaknya menggambarkan garis besar bajang, diubah secara "skriptural" untuk menjadi penangkal terhadap bajang itu sendiri.
statement.en: Skeat reproduces a drawing that appears to show the outline of a bajang, "scripturally" modified to serve as a counter-charm against the bajang itself.

claims.quote: The outlines of the figure are made up from varying combinations of the names “Allah,” “Muhammad,” “ʿAli,” etc., in the Arabic character.

statement.id: Garis gambar penangkal itu tersusun dari berbagai gabungan nama "Allah", "Muhammad", "Ali", dan lain-lain dalam aksara Arab.
statement.en: The outlines of that counter-charm figure are made up of varying combinations of the names "Allah", "Muhammad", "Ali" and others in Arabic script.

claims.quote: Langsuior, the female familiar, differs hardly at all from the bâjang, except that she is a little more baneful, and when under the control of a man he sometimes becomes the victim of her attractions, and she will even bear him elfin children.

statement.id: Menurut kutipan dalam catatan kaki Skeat, langsuior, roh peliharaan perempuan, nyaris tak berbeda dari bajang kecuali sedikit lebih jahat.
statement.en: According to a quotation in Skeat's footnote, the langsuior, the female familiar, differs hardly at all from the bajang except in being a little more baneful.

claims.quote: MALAY MAGIC BEING AN INTRODUCTION TO THE FOLKLORE AND POPULAR RELIGION OF THE MALAY PENINSULA BY WALTER WILLIAM SKEAT OF THE CIVIL SERVICE OF THE FEDERATED MALAY STATES

statement.id: Sumbernya adalah Malay Magic, pengantar folklor dan agama rakyat Semenanjung Melayu karya Walter William Skeat dari dinas sipil Federated Malay States.
statement.en: The source is Malay Magic, an introduction to the folklore and popular religion of the Malay Peninsula by Walter William Skeat of the civil service of the Federated Malay States.

claims.quote: A kind of familiar spirit acquired by a male who says the proper incantations over the newly buried body of a stillborn child. It takes the form of a civet or musang and may cause convulsions, unconsciousness or delirium.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, bajang adalah roh peliharaan yang diperoleh seorang lelaki dengan mantra yang tepat di atas jasad bayi lahir mati yang baru dikubur; ia berwujud luwak atau musang dan dapat menyebabkan kejang, pingsan, atau mengigau.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia, the bajang is a familiar spirit acquired by a man reciting the proper incantations over the newly buried body of a stillborn child; it takes the form of a civet or musang and may cause convulsions, unconsciousness or delirium.

claims.quote: As with other spirits of this type, a bajang may turn on its master if it is neglected. Although a bajang can be made to attack any whom its master chooses, it is considered particularly dangerous to infants and young children.

statement.id: Seperti roh sejenisnya, bajang dapat berbalik menyerang tuannya bila diabaikan; ia dapat disuruh menyerang siapa pun yang dipilih tuannya, tetapi dianggap sangat berbahaya bagi bayi dan anak kecil.
statement.en: Like other spirits of its type, a bajang may turn on its master if neglected; it can be made to attack anyone its master chooses but is considered particularly dangerous to infants and young children.

claims.quote: In former times, some children would be given "bajang bracelets" (gelang bajang) made of black silk to protect them against it, and sharp metal objects such as scissors would be placed near babies for the same purpose.

statement.id: Pada masa lalu, sebagian anak diberi "gelang bajang" dari sutra hitam sebagai pelindung, dan benda logam tajam seperti gunting diletakkan di dekat bayi untuk tujuan yang sama.
statement.en: In former times some children were given black-silk "bajang bracelets" (gelang bajang) for protection, and sharp metal objects such as scissors were placed near babies for the same purpose.

claims.quote: Even the striations of pregnancy are somewhat jokingly said to be the scars left by a bajang's attack.

statement.id: Garis-garis regangan akibat kehamilan bahkan setengah bercanda disebut bekas luka serangan bajang.
statement.en: Even the striations of pregnancy are somewhat jokingly said to be the scars left by a bajang's attack.

claims.quote: The pelesit is in many ways comparable to the bajang, but whereas the bajang's owner is always male, the pelesit may only be kept by a female.

statement.id: Pelesit dalam banyak hal sebanding dengan bajang, tetapi pemilik bajang selalu laki-laki, sedangkan pelesit hanya boleh dipelihara perempuan.
statement.en: The pelesit is in many ways comparable to the bajang, but a bajang's owner is always male whereas a pelesit may only be kept by a female.

short_description.id: Naga hitam adalah sosok naga dalam tradisi Eropa dan Asia Timur.
short_description.en: The black dragon is a dragon figure in European and East Asian traditions.

long_description.id: Naga hitam adalah sosok naga dalam tradisi Eropa dan Asia Timur. Dalam pemikiran lima unsur ia dikaitkan dengan air dan utara.
long_description.en: The black dragon is a dragon figure in European and East Asian traditions. In five-phase thought it is associated with water and the north.

long_description.id: Ia ditafsirkan sebagai penjaga suci utara. Gambarnya sering memberi naga timur sisik hitam dan dua kaki depan.
long_description.en: It is interpreted as a sacred guardian of the north. Its depictions often give an eastern dragon black scales and two forelegs.

long_description.id: Dalam teks klasik Huainanzi, Nüwa membunuh naga hitam untuk menyelamatkan Jizhou. Sebagian daerah menghormati naga hitam sebagai makhluk suci, dan Takaokami no Ōkami kadang disebut Kokuryū Daimyōjin. Di Hōgon-ji di Pulau Chikubu, naga hitam dipuja sebagai salah satu dari Delapan Raja Naga.
long_description.en: In the classical text Huainanzi, Nüwa slays a black dragon to save Jizhou. Some regions worship the black dragon as a sacred being, and Takaokami no Ōkami is sometimes identified as Kokuryū Daimyōjin. At Hōgon-ji on Chikubu Island, the black dragon is enshrined as one of the Eight Dragon Kings.

role.id: Naga hitam yang dibunuh Nüwa
role.en: The black dragon killed by Nüwa

summary.id: Dalam Huainanzi, Nüwa membunuh naga hitam untuk menyelamatkan Jizhou dan menimbun abu alang-alang untuk menghentikan banjir.
summary.en: In the Huainanzi, Nüwa slays a black dragon to save Jizhou and piles up reed ashes to stop the flood waters.

description.id: Di Kokuryū-dō di halaman kuil ini, naga hitam dipuja sebagai salah satu dari Delapan Raja Naga.
description.en: In the Kokuryū-dō (Black Dragon Hall) in the temple grounds, the black dragon is enshrined as one of the Eight Dragon Kings.

claims.quote: 黒竜（旧字体: 黑龍󠄂、こくりゅう、拼音: hēilóng ヘイロン）は、ヨーロッパや中国や日本の伝承および物語、神話に登場する竜の一種。

statement.id: Naga hitam adalah sosok naga dalam tradisi Eropa dan Asia Timur.
statement.en: The black dragon is a dragon figure in European and East Asian traditions.

claims.quote: 五行思想においては、黒は北と同じく水に対応するので、黒竜を玄武と同様、「北方を守護する神聖な竜」としている。

statement.id: Dalam pemikiran lima unsur ia dikaitkan dengan air dan utara.
statement.en: In five-phase thought it is associated with water and the north.

claims.quote: 五行思想においては、黒は北と同じく水に対応するので、黒竜を玄武と同様、「北方を守護する神聖な竜」としている。

statement.id: Ia ditafsirkan sebagai penjaga suci utara.
statement.en: It is interpreted as a sacred guardian of the north.

claims.quote: 名前通り全身の鱗が黒く、前足が2本しかない東洋の竜として描かれる事が多い。驪竜（りりょう）とも呼ばれ、これは顎の下に貴重な珠を持っているともされる 。

statement.id: Gambarnya sering memberi naga timur sisik hitam dan dua kaki depan.
statement.en: Its depictions often give an eastern dragon black scales and two forelegs.

claims.quote: よって、一部の地域では、黒竜を他の竜同様に、神聖な存在として祀っている。
claims.locator: 五行思想における黒竜

statement.id: Di sebagian daerah, naga hitam dihormati sebagai makhluk suci seperti naga-naga lain.
statement.en: In some regions the black dragon is worshipped as a sacred being, like other dragons.

claims.quote: 於是女媧煉五色石以補蒼天，斷鼇足以立四極。殺黑龍以濟冀州，積蘆灰以止淫水。

statement.id: Dalam Huainanzi, Nüwa (女媧) membunuh naga hitam (黑龍) untuk menyelamatkan Jizhou (冀州) dan menimbun abu alang-alang untuk menghentikan banjir.
statement.en: In the Huainanzi, Nüwa (女媧) slew a black dragon (黑龍) to save Jizhou (冀州), and piled up reed ashes to stop the flood waters.

claims.quote: また高龗大神（たかおかみ）のことを黒龍大明神とすることもある。
claims.locator: 信仰対象としての黒竜

statement.id: Takaokami no Ōkami (高龗大神) kadang disebut Kokuryū Daimyōjin (黒龍大明神).
statement.en: Takaokami no Ōkami (高龗大神) is sometimes identified as Kokuryū Daimyōjin (黒龍大明神, "Great Deity Black Dragon").

claims.quote: 竹生島の宝厳寺境内にある黒龍堂（黒龍大神・黒龍姫大神）に八大龍王の一尊である黒龍として祀られている。

statement.id: Di Hōgon-ji di Pulau Chikubu, naga hitam dipuja sebagai salah satu dari Delapan Raja Naga di Kokuryū-dō.
statement.en: At Hōgon-ji on Chikubu Island, the black dragon is enshrined as one of the Eight Dragon Kings in the Kokuryū-dō (Black Dragon Hall).

short_description.id: Cabraboc adalah makhluk setengah manusia setengah kambing dalam imajinasi rakyat Katalan yang mengejar pejalan malam di hutan.
short_description.en: The cabraboc is a half-human, half-goat being of Catalan folk imagination that chases night travellers in the forest.

long_description.id: Cabraboc adalah makhluk setengah manusia di bagian atas dan setengah kambing di bagian bawah. Mereka makhluk hutan yang mengejar pejalan malam, sering sampai korban terjatuh dari tebing, dan kadang digambarkan bersayap kelelawar.
long_description.en: The cabraboc is a being that is human above and goat below. They are forest creatures that chase night travellers, often until the victim falls off a cliff, and are sometimes described with bat wings.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda Ripollet, seekor kucing keluar dari keranjang sepasang orang tua lalu berubah menjadi iblis Cabraboc. Legenda ini dipentaskan pada karnaval Ripollet, dan kelompok Diables de Caldes de Montbui menamai cabraboc helm berkepala kambing iblis utama mereka.
long_description.en: In a Ripollet legend a cat came out of an old couple's basket and turned into the devil Cabraboc. The legend is staged at the Ripollet carnival, and the Diables de Caldes de Montbui call their main devil's goat-headed helmet a cabraboc.

long_description.id: Sebuah buku legenda yang disusun di Ripollet mencatat versi yang sama. Cabraboc digambarkan setengah manusia di bagian atas dan setengah kambing di bagian bawah. pada hari Karnaval seorang kakek dan nenek berjalan-jalan dan sang nenek membawa keranjang berisi panci. Seorang iblis kecil memukul panci itu dan keluarlah seekor kucing yang secara ajaib berubah menjadi cabraboc. Karena begitu banyak dibicarakan, sejak itu kelompok comparsa menampilkannya setiap tahun saat Karnaval.
long_description.en: A legend booklet compiled in Ripollet records the same version. The cabraboc is described as half person above and half goat below. on Carnival day an old man and an old woman went for a walk and the woman carried a basket with a pot. A little devil struck the pot and a cat came out that by magic turned into a cabraboc. Because it was talked about so much, the comparsa groups have portrayed it every year at Carnival ever since.

who.en: A half-goat being.

claims.quote: Un cabraboc és un ésser fantàstic propi de l'imaginari popular català, mig humà per la part de dalt i mig cabra o boc per la part de baix.

statement.id: Cabraboc adalah makhluk khayalan imajinasi rakyat Katalan, setengah manusia di bagian atas dan setengah kambing di bagian bawah.
statement.en: A cabraboc is a fantastic being of Catalan folk imagination, half human above and half goat below.

claims.quote: Es diu que els cabrabocs persegueixen els homes com si fossin cabres i les dones com si fossin bocs. Són éssers del bosc i cal evitar-los quan es viatja de nit

statement.id: Para cabraboc konon mengejar lelaki seperti kambing betina dan perempuan seperti kambing jantan; mereka makhluk hutan yang harus dihindari saat bepergian malam.
statement.en: Cabrabocs are said to chase men as if they were nanny goats and women as if they were billy goats; they are forest beings to be avoided when travelling at night.

statement.en: The chases often end with the victim falling off a cliff, and they were sometimes described with bat wings.

claims.quote: Aleshores, del cistell en sortí un gat que es convertí en un diable més, el Cabraboc.

statement.id: Dalam legenda Ripollet El vell i la vella, seekor kucing keluar dari keranjang sepasang orang tua dan berubah menjadi iblis, si Cabraboc.
statement.en: In the Ripollet legend El vell i la vella, a cat came out of an old couple's basket and turned into one more devil, the Cabraboc.

statement.id: Kelompok Diables de Caldes de Montbui menamai cabraboc helm yang dipakai iblis utama mereka, Llucifer.
statement.en: The Diables de Caldes de Montbui give the name cabraboc to the helmet worn by their main devil, Llucifer.

claims.quote: Les Bruixes de Ripollet n'escenifiquen la llegenda durant el carnaval infantil, i els Diables de Ripollet el treuen al capdavant de la rua de Carnaval de dissabte.

statement.id: Les Bruixes de Ripollet mementaskan legenda ini pada karnaval anak, dan Diables de Ripollet membawanya di depan pawai karnaval hari Sabtu.
statement.en: Les Bruixes de Ripollet stage the legend at the children's carnival, and the Diables de Ripollet carry it at the head of Saturday's carnival parade.

claims.quote: El Cabraboc és un ésser mig persona per la part de dalt i mig cabra i boc per la part de sota.

statement.id: Cabraboc adalah makhluk setengah manusia di bagian atas dan setengah kambing betina dan kambing jantan di bagian bawah.
statement.en: The Cabraboc is a being half person on the upper part and half goat and billy goat on the lower part.

claims.quote: Explica la llegenda que a Ripollet la diada de Carnestoltes van sortir a passejar un vell i una vella. La vella portava un cistell amb una olla dins, tot feia pensar que hi portava el dinar.

statement.id: Legenda mengatakan bahwa di Ripollet pada hari Karnaval seorang kakek dan nenek keluar berjalan-jalan; sang nenek membawa keranjang berisi panci, dan segalanya menunjukkan bahwa itu bekal makan siang.
statement.en: The legend says that in Ripollet on Carnival day an old man and an old woman went out for a walk; the old woman carried a basket with a pot inside, and everything suggested it held their lunch.

claims.quote: Un dels diablots va veure la vella i el cistell i va pensar: “Ara és la meva”, i amb un bastó que portava va donar un cop a l’olla. Tothom es va quedar parat, perquè de l’olla, en lloc d’escudella, en va sortir un gat, que per art de màgia i en un tres i no res es va convertir en cabraboc.

statement.id: Salah satu iblis kecil melihat si nenek dan keranjangnya lalu memukul panci dengan tongkat; alih-alih sup, keluar seekor kucing yang secara ajaib seketika berubah menjadi cabraboc.
statement.en: One of the little devils saw the old woman and her basket and struck the pot with a stick; instead of stew a cat came out of it, which by magic in no time turned into a cabraboc.

claims.quote: Se’n va parlar tant, del fet, que des de llavors cada any per Carnaval les colles de comparses el representen.

statement.id: Peristiwa itu begitu banyak dibicarakan sehingga sejak itu setiap tahun saat Karnaval kelompok-kelompok comparsa menampilkannya.
statement.en: The event was talked about so much that from then on, every year at Carnival, the comparsa groups portray it.
