short_description.id: Camahueto adalah banteng legendaris bertanduk tunggal dalam mitologi Chilote yang tumbuh di sungai lalu pindah ke laut [camahueto-c01, camahueto-c02, camahueto-c03].
short_description.en: The Camahueto is a one-horned legendary bull of Chilote mythology that grows in rivers and moves to the sea [camahueto-c01, camahueto-c02, camahueto-c03].

long_description.id: Camahueto adalah banteng legendaris mitologi Chilote [camahueto-c01] yang bertanduk tunggal seperti unicorn [camahueto-c02]. Ia tumbuh di sungai dan pindah ke laut setelah dewasa [camahueto-c03]. Berbagai versi menyebutnya memangsa manusia, mengendalikan waktu, dan menciptakan hujan atau petir [camahueto-c04], serta menyeret orang ke dasar laut [camahueto-c05]. Hanya machi yang dapat menggiringnya kembali ke laut dengan laso rumput laut [camahueto-c06].
long_description.en: The Camahueto is a legendary bull of Chilote mythology [camahueto-c01] with a single unicorn-like horn [camahueto-c02]. It grows in rivers and moves to the ocean when grown [camahueto-c03]. Versions say it eats humans, controls time and makes rain or thunder [camahueto-c04], and drags people into the sea [camahueto-c05]. Only a machi can lead it back to sea with a kelp lasso [camahueto-c06].

long_description.id: Menurut Chiloé Mitológico, Camahueto lahir dari kedalaman bumi di puncak bukit dekat laut [camahueto-c08]. Wujudnya seperti anak sapi hijau dengan satu tanduk kecil di dahi, mirip unicorn Yunani [camahueto-c07]. Seorang machi menangkapnya dengan laso dari "boqui", mencabut tanduknya ("cacho"), lalu melepasnya menuju laut [camahueto-c09]. Potongan kecil tanduk itu ditanam para machi di bukit lain, dan setelah dua puluh lima tahun lahirlah camahueto lain [camahueto-c10]. Kerokan tanduknya disebut sebagai obat paling manjur dalam farmakope Chiloé kuno [camahueto-c11].
long_description.en: According to Chiloé Mitológico, the Camahueto is born from the depths of the earth on a hill near the sea [camahueto-c08]. It looks like a green calf with a single small horn on its forehead, like the Greek unicorn [camahueto-c07]. A machi catches it with a lasso of "boqui", tears off its horn ("cacho") and lets it go on to the sea [camahueto-c09]. The machis plant small pieces of the horn on other hills, and after twenty-five years other camahuetos are born [camahueto-c10]. Scrapings of the horn are described as the most effective medicine of the early Chilote pharmacopoeia [camahueto-c11].

long_description.id: Sumber yang sama menyatakan bahwa kehidupan akuatik Camahueto hampir tidak diketahui; konon ia kembali ke laut karena laut adalah miliknya [camahueto-c14]. Keberadaannya di darat disebut sebagai pembalasan yang ditinggalkan roh air Coicoi-vilu untuk melanjutkan karya perusaknya [camahueto-c15]. Penulisnya menafsirkan hewan imajiner ini sebagai penjelasan atas longsor tanah yang tampak spontan [camahueto-c12], dan sebagai lambang kekuatan, kesuburan, dan kelimpahan [camahueto-c13].
long_description.en: The same source says little is known of its aquatic life; it is said to return to the sea because the sea is where it belongs [camahueto-c14]. Its stay on land is described as revenge left behind by the water spirit Coicoi-vilu to continue his destructive work [camahueto-c15]. Its author interprets the imaginary animal as an explanation for apparently spontaneous landslides [camahueto-c12] and as a symbol of strength, fertility and abundance [camahueto-c13].

cultural_context.id: Menurut penulis Chiloé Mitológico, hewan imajiner ini dipakai untuk menjelaskan longsor tanah yang tampak spontan [camahueto-c12], dan ia melambangkan kekuatan, kesuburan, dan kelimpahan [camahueto-c13].
cultural_context.en: According to the author of Chiloé Mitológico, this imaginary animal was used to explain apparently spontaneous landslides [camahueto-c12], and it represents strength, fertility and abundance [camahueto-c13].

short_description.id: Carbuncle adalah hewan kecil legendaris Amerika Selatan yang konon memiliki permata merah menyala seperti bara di kepalanya [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c01, carbuncle-legendary-creature-c02].
short_description.en: The carbuncle is a legendary small South American animal said to bear a glowing red gem on its head [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c01, carbuncle-legendary-creature-c02].

long_description.id: Carbuncle adalah hewan kecil legendaris dari Paraguay dan cerita rakyat tambang Chile utara [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c01]. Di kepalanya ada cermin merah berkilau seperti bara yang dianggap permata [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c02]. Bagi orang Spanyol dan Portugis kolonial, ia mewujudkan kisah naga penyimpan permata [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c03]. Namanya dari bahasa Latin carbunculus, "bara kecil" [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c04].
long_description.en: The carbuncle is a legendary small animal of Paraguay and the mining folklore of northern Chile [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c01]. On its head is a red shining mirror like glowing coal, thought to be a gem [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c02]. To colonial Spaniards and Portuguese it embodied the lore of gem-hiding dragons [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c03]. Its name comes from Latin carbunculus, "little coal" [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c04].

long_description.id: Dalam La Argentina (1602), Martín del Barco Centenera, seorang pendeta dan penjelajah, menyebutnya Anagpitán dan melukiskannya sebagai hewan agak kecil berkaca kilau di kepala laksana bara [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c12]. Gambarannya berbeda-beda, dan konon tak ada yang pernah memandangnya cukup jelas untuk menentukan apakah ia burung atau mamalia [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c13]. Konon ia menyimpan harta sehingga penangkapnya menjadi kaya [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c05]. Di Tarapacá, ia digambarkan seperti kerang berpendar putih kebiruan yang peka pendengarannya dan mengatup bila manusia mendekat [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c10].
long_description.en: In La Argentina (1602), Martín del Barco Centenera, a chaplain and explorer, named it Anagpitán and pictured a smallish animal with a bright mirror on its head, much like a burning coal [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c12]. Accounts differ, and reportedly nobody ever got a good enough look to tell whether it was a bird or a mammal [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c13]. It is said to hold treasures so that whoever captures it becomes wealthy [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c05]. In Tarapacá it is said to look like a white-blue shining bivalve with acute hearing that clams up when humans approach [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c10].

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Chilote di Chile selatan, carbunclo disebut penjaga logam, dengan wujud yang beragam dari anjing kecil bercahaya hingga cahaya api kehijauan-merah [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c06]. Sebuah kamus mitologi juga menyebutnya membawa jumput cahaya di bawah dagu dan dianggap penjaga harta yang warnanya ia tiru [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c15]. Ia konon menampakkan diri pada malam hari sekitar titik balik matahari musim dingin belahan bumi selatan [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c07]. Legenda menyebut pemburu harta harus melempar tali, sabuk, atau barang pribadi ke arahnya dan kembali sebelum fajar [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c08]; bila ritual tidak dijalankan, penggali mati karena gas beracun [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c09].
long_description.en: In the Chilote mythology of southern Chile the carbunclo is called the guardian of the metals, with forms ranging from a luminescent small dog to a greenish-red fiery light [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c06]. A mythology dictionary also says it carries a luminous tuft under its chin and is considered a guardian of treasures whose colors it takes on [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c15]. It is said to manifest at night around the Southern Hemisphere winter solstice [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c07]. The legend says a treasure seeker must cast a string, belt or personal belonging towards it and return before dawn [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c08]; if the ritual is not performed, the digger dies from noxious gas [carbuncle-legendary-creature-c09].

claims.quote: is a legendary species of small animal in South American folklore, specifically in Paraguay or the mining folklore of northern Chile.

statement.id: Carbuncle adalah hewan kecil legendaris dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Selatan, khususnya Paraguay dan cerita rakyat tambang di Chile utara.
statement.en: The carbuncle is a legendary small animal of South American folklore, especially in Paraguay and the mining folklore of northern Chile.

claims.quote: The animal is said to have a red shining mirror, like hot glowing coal, on its head, thought to be a precious stone.

statement.id: Hewan ini konon memiliki cermin merah berkilau seperti bara di kepalanya, yang dianggap batu permata.
statement.en: It is said to have a red shining mirror like glowing coal on its head, thought to be a gem.

claims.quote: To the colonial Spaniards and Portuguese, the creature was a realization of the medieval lore that a dragon or wyvern concealed a precious gem in its brain or body

statement.id: Bagi orang Spanyol dan Portugis masa kolonial, makhluk ini mewujudkan kisah abad pertengahan tentang naga yang menyimpan permata di otak atau tubuhnya.
statement.en: To colonial Spaniards and Portuguese it embodied medieval lore of a dragon hiding a gem in its brain or body.

claims.quote: comes from the Latin carbunculus, meaning "little coal"

statement.id: Namanya berasal dari bahasa Latin carbunculus, "bara kecil".
statement.en: The name comes from Latin carbunculus, "little coal".

claims.quote: In Latin American lore, it is said to hold treasures inside so whoever manages to capture it will become wealthy.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Latin, konon ia menyimpan harta di dalam dirinya sehingga siapa pun yang berhasil menangkapnya akan menjadi kaya.
statement.en: In Latin American lore, it is said to hold treasures inside, so whoever manages to capture it becomes wealthy.

claims.quote: In the Chilote mythology of southern Chile the carbunclo is said to be the "guardian of the metals". Descriptions of it vary, from a luminescent small dog, a luminescent bivalve, a cat with a luminescent lock or tuft under its beard or a greenish-red fiery light reminiscent of fireflies.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Chilote di Chile selatan, carbunclo disebut "penjaga logam"; wujudnya digambarkan beragam: anjing kecil bercahaya, kerang bercahaya, kucing dengan jumput bercahaya di bawah janggut, atau cahaya api kehijauan-merah yang mengingatkan pada kunang-kunang.
statement.en: In the Chilote mythology of southern Chile the carbunclo is said to be the "guardian of the metals"; descriptions vary from a luminescent small dog, a luminescent bivalve or a cat with a luminescent tuft under its beard to a greenish-red fiery light reminiscent of fireflies.

claims.quote: The carbunclo is said to manifest itself at night around the Southern Hemisphere winter solstice (late June).

statement.id: Konon carbunclo menampakkan diri pada malam hari sekitar titik balik matahari musim dingin belahan bumi selatan (akhir Juni).
statement.en: The carbunclo is said to manifest itself at night around the Southern Hemisphere winter solstice (late June).

claims.quote: First, a length of string, or a belt (or some personal belonging) must be cast towards the carbunclo which will snatch it and disappear. The treasure seeker shall wait and return to the site in the morning before dawn

statement.id: Menurut legenda, pemburu harta harus lebih dulu melempar seutas tali, sabuk, atau barang pribadi ke arah carbunclo, yang akan menyambarnya lalu menghilang; sang pemburu menunggu dan kembali ke tempat itu pagi sebelum fajar.
statement.en: According to the legend, a treasure seeker must first cast a length of string, a belt or some personal belonging towards the carbunclo, which snatches it and disappears; the seeker waits and returns to the site in the morning before dawn.

claims.quote: If this ritual is not performed, the digger will die in the pit due to noxious gas. He must also not show any sign of fear the treasure will turn into rock.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, bila ritual itu tidak dijalankan penggali akan mati di lubang karena gas beracun, dan ia tidak boleh menunjukkan rasa takut agar harta itu tidak berubah menjadi batu.
statement.en: According to the legend, if the ritual is not performed the digger will die in the pit from noxious gas, and he must show no sign of fear or the treasure will turn into rock.

claims.quote: In Tarapacá, it is said to look like a bivalve with a strong white-blue shine from within the shell which can be observed from a distance 1 league away; this "bivalve" has an acute sense of hearing, so that it can quickly detect humans approaching, and clam up inside its hard shell

statement.id: Di Tarapacá, konon ia tampak seperti kerang dengan cahaya putih kebiruan kuat dari dalam cangkangnya yang terlihat dari jarak satu liga; "kerang" itu sangat peka pendengarannya sehingga cepat mengetahui manusia mendekat dan mengatup di dalam cangkang kerasnya.
statement.en: In Tarapacá, it is said to look like a bivalve with a strong white-blue shine from within the shell, visible from one league away; this "bivalve" has acute hearing, quickly detects humans approaching and clams up inside its hard shell.

claims.quote: According to some, the carbuncle is explainable as a bivalve mollusk which glows because of bioluminescence from the "cauquil" (Noctiluca scintillans) or from fireflies.

statement.id: Menurut sebagian orang, carbuncle dapat dijelaskan sebagai moluska bercangkang dua yang berpendar karena bioluminesensi "cauquil" (Noctiluca scintillans) atau kunang-kunang.
statement.en: According to some, the carbuncle can be explained as a bivalve mollusk that glows because of bioluminescence from the "cauquil" (Noctiluca scintillans) or from fireflies.

claims.quote: The chaplain and explorer Martín del Barco Centenera in La Argentina (1602) called it Anagpitán (recté Añagpitán; cf. anhangapitã below) and described it as "a smallish animal, with a shining mirror on its head, like a glowing coal".

statement.en: The chaplain and explorer Martín del Barco Centenera, in La Argentina (1602), called it Anagpitán and described it as "a smallish animal, with a shining mirror on its head, like a glowing coal".

claims.quote: The description of the animal vary; and "no one ever saw it well enough to know whether it was a bird or a mammal, whether is had feathers or fur".

statement.id: Gambaran hewan ini beragam, dan "tak seorang pun pernah melihatnya cukup jelas untuk tahu apakah ia burung atau mamalia, berbulu atau berbulu halus".
statement.en: Descriptions of the animal vary, and "no one ever saw it well enough to know whether it was a bird or a mammal, whether is had feathers or fur".

claims.quote: Carbuncle is a recurring character in the Final Fantasy series of role-playing games, and "appears as a small creature, fox-, cat-, rabbit- or squirrel-like, with green or blue fur, depending on the game".

short_description.id: Crinisus (Crimisus) adalah dewa sungai Crinisus di Sisilia yang, menurut kebanyakan versi, dalam wujud anjing menjadi ayah Acestes dari seorang perempuan Troya.
short_description.en: Crinisus (Crimisus) is the god of the Sicilian river Crinisus who, in most versions, fathered Acestes with a Trojan woman in the form of a dog.

long_description.id: Crinisus, atau Crimisus, adalah dewa sungai Crinisus di Sisilia dalam mitologi Yunani dan Romawi. Sungainya terletak di barat laut Sikelia dan bermuara ke Laut Tengah dekat koloni Yunani Egesta.
long_description.en: Crinisus, also called Crimisus, was the god of the river Crinisus in Sicily in Greek and Roman myth. His river lay in north-western Sikelia and flowed into the Mediterranean close to the Greek colony of Egesta.

long_description.id: Menurut kebanyakan versi mitos, ia dalam wujud anjing menjadi ayah Acestes dari seorang perempuan Troya, putri seorang pemukim Troya. Dalam Alexandra karya Lycophron, ia mengambil putri itu sebagai pengantin dan melahirkan anak mulia; Aeneid karya Virgil menyebut Acestes lahir dari ibu Troya oleh dewa sungai Crimisus. Komentar Servius menambahkan bahwa ia berubah menjadi beruang atau anjing dan menurunkan Egestus, pendiri Egesta, yang kemudian dikenal sebagai Segesta.
long_description.en: In most versions of the myth he fathered Acestes with a Trojan woman, the daughter of a Trojan settler, in the form of a dog. In Lycophron's Alexandra he takes the daughter as his bride and begets a noble whelp; Virgil's Aeneid says Acestes was born of a Trojan mother to the river god Crimisus. Servius's commentary adds that he turned into a bear or a dog and fathered Egestus, founder of Egesta, later known as Segesta.

long_description.id: Menurut Aelian, orang Egesta menghormatinya dalam wujud manusia, bertentangan dengan kisah wujud anjing. Koin Segesta dari 475-390 SM sering bergambar anjing pada satu sisi dan kepala perempuan pada sisi lain, yang secara tradisional dikaitkan dengan Crinisus dan Segesta.
long_description.en: According to Aelian, the Egestans honour him in the form of men, unlike the dog-form story. Coins from Segesta dating 475-390 BCE often carry a dog and a woman's head on opposite faces, traditionally linked with Crinisus and Segesta.

short_description.id: Cuca adalah salah satu makhluk mitologi utama dalam cerita rakyat Brasil: penyihir tua berwajah aligator yang menculik anak-anak.
short_description.en: The Cuca is one of the main mythological beings of Brazilian folklore: an old witch with an alligator appearance who kidnaps children.

long_description.id: Cuca adalah salah satu makhluk mitologi utama dalam cerita rakyat Brasil. Ia digambarkan sebagai penyihir yang menculik anak-anak dan dapat berwujud perempuan tua atau penyihir berkepala aligator. Dalam versi lain ia adalah entitas berwujud penyihir tua berpenampilan aligator yang usianya tidak diketahui pasti tetapi bisa lebih dari 3 ribu tahun. Menurut legenda, ia tidur sekali setiap tujuh tahun.
long_description.en: The Cuca is one of the main mythological beings of Brazilian folklore. She is described as a witch who kidnaps children and can take the form of an old woman or a witch with an alligator head. In another version she is an entity in the form of an old witch with an alligator appearance whose age is not known for sure but may exceed 3,000 years. According to legend, she sleeps once every seven years.

long_description.id: Menurut sebagian tradisi, Cuca baru muncul dari sebuah telur setiap 1.000 tahun; Cuca sebelumnya berubah menjadi burung berkicau sedih, sedangkan yang baru menjalankan perannya dan menimbulkan lebih banyak kerugian. Ada pula versi yang mengenal lebih dari satu cuca, seolah subkelas bicho-papão.
long_description.en: According to some traditions, a new Cuca emerges from an egg every 1,000 years; the previous Cuca turns into a bird with a sad song, while the new one takes up her role, causing more harm. There are also versions in which more than one cuca exists, as a kind of subclass of the bicho-papão.

long_description.id: Asal-usulnya diperdebatkan. Legenda ini diturunkan dari Coca (atau Coco) dalam cerita rakyat Iberia yang diduga masuk ke Brasil pada masa kolonisasi. Menurut Câmara Cascudo, Cuca adalah mitos asal Portugis yang terkait dengan Coca, tokoh dalam prosesi di provinsi Minho, tempat "cuca" juga nama sejenis labu yang dilubangi membentuk mata dan mulut. Kemungkinan lain adalah Farricoco, tokoh prosesi Passos di Algarve.
long_description.en: Its origin is debated. The legend derives from the Coca (or Coco) of Iberian folklore, probably introduced into Brazil at the time of colonisation. According to Câmara Cascudo, the Cuca is a myth of Portuguese origin related to the Coca, a figure in processions in the province of Minho, where "cuca" is also the name of a kind of pumpkin pierced with the outlines of eyes and mouth. Another possibility is the Farricoco, a figure of the Passos procession in the Algarve.

long_description.id: Di Brasil, Cuca dipopulerkan oleh buku "O Saci" (1921) karya Monteiro Lobato, satu-satunya karya Lobato tempat ia muncul. Di sana ia digambarkan sebagai "penyihir mengerikan" berpendengaran sangat tajam, "setua waktu", tinggal di gua di hutan dan hanya tidur satu malam setiap tujuh tahun, berwajah seperti aligator dan bercakar seperti elang. Dalam dua serial adaptasi karya Lobato oleh Rede Globo, lima kostum berbeda dipakai untuknya.
long_description.en: In Brazil the Cuca was popularised by Monteiro Lobato's book "O Saci" (1921), the only work by Lobato in which she appears. There she is described as a "horrible witch" with very fine hearing, "as old as time", living in a cave in the forest and sleeping only one night every seven years, with a face like an alligator and claws like hawks. In the two series adapted from Lobato's work by Rede Globo, five different costumes were used for her.

short_description.id: Daidarabotchi adalah raksasa legendaris Jepang yang jejak kakinya konon membentuk danau dan rawa, dan yang dikaitkan dengan terbentuknya gunung.
short_description.en: Daidarabotchi is a legendary Japanese giant whose footprints were said to form lakes and marshes, and who is linked to the creation of mountains.

long_description.id: Daidarabotchi (ダイダラボッチ, 大座法師) adalah jenis yōkai raksasa dalam mitologi Jepang, yang kadang disebut menyerupai pegunungan ketika tidur. Ia juga dikenal dengan nama ダダ坊, デイラボー, dan 大太法師, dan ceritanya tersebar luas terutama di wilayah Kantō dan Chūbu.
long_description.en: Daidarabotchi (ダイダラボッチ, 大座法師) is a colossal kind of yōkai in Japanese myth, at times said to lie like a mountain range while asleep. He also goes by the names ダダ坊, デイラボー and 大太法師, and stories of him are found widely, chiefly in the Kantō and Chūbu regions.

long_description.id: Ukurannya begitu besar sehingga jejak kakinya dikatakan membentuk danau dan kolam yang tak terhitung. Tradisi menyebut jejak besar dan rawa yang terbentuk dari air di jejak itu, serta bukit kecil dari lumpur yang tumpah ketika ia membuat gunung. Dalam satu legenda ia menimbang Gunung Fuji dan Gunung Tsukuba, tetapi tanpa sengaja membelah puncak Tsukuba.
long_description.en: So vast was he that his footprints supposedly formed countless lakes and ponds. Tradition tells of great footprints and a marsh formed by water in them, and of small hills from mud spilled while he made mountains. In one legend he weighed Mount Fuji and Mount Tsukuba, but accidentally split the peak of Tsukuba.

long_description.id: Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki, catatan adat kekaisaran di daerah Hitachi yang disusun pada abad ke-8, menceritakan Daidarabotchi yang memakan kerang raksasa dari pantai dan menumpuk cangkangnya di atas bukit. Menurut ensiklopedia, di Kyūshū ia disebut Ōhito Yagorō, dan kisah serupa tentang raksasa tercatat dalam fudoki Hitachi dan Harima.
long_description.en: The Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki, a record of customs in Hitachi Province compiled in the 8th century, tells of a Daidarabotchi who fed on giant clams from the beach and piled the shells on a hill. According to an encyclopedia, in Kyūshū he is called Ōhito Yagorō, and giant legends are recorded in the Hitachi and Harima fudoki.

long_description.id: Sebuah ensiklopedia menafsirkan bahwa karena kisahnya berkaitan dengan terbentuknya kolam, rawa, dan gunung, semula orang meyakini raksasa sebagai dewa pencipta langit dan bumi. Asal-usul namanya masih diperdebatkan.
long_description.en: An encyclopedia interprets that because the tales relate to the formation of ponds, marshes and mountains, a giant as a creator god of heaven and earth was originally believed in. The origin of his name remains debated.

description.id: Di Kyūshū raksasa semacam ini disebut Ōhito Yagorō.
description.en: In Kyūshū a giant of this kind is called Ōhito Yagorō.

summary.en: Tales in various places say Daidarabotchi tried to carry and move a mountain; earth that fell when the binding vines snapped became a small hill.

description.id: Dalam satu legenda Daidarabotchi menimbang Gunung Fuji dan Gunung Tsukuba untuk mengetahui mana yang lebih berat.
description.en: In one legend Daidarabotchi weighed Mount Fuji and Mount Tsukuba to see which was heavier.

claims.quote: Daidarabotchi (ダイダラボッチ, 大座法師) was a gigantic type of yōkai in Japanese mythology, sometimes said to pose as a mountain range when sleeping.

statement.id: Daidarabotchi adalah yōkai raksasa dalam dongeng Jepang.
statement.en: Daidarabotchi is a giant yōkai in Japanese tales.

claims.quote: The size of a Daidarabotchi was so great that his footprints were said to have created innumerable lakes and ponds.

statement.id: Jejaknya dikatakan membentuk danau dan kolam.
statement.en: Its footprints were said to form lakes and ponds.

claims.quote: In one legend, a Daidarabotchi weighed Mount Fuji and Mount Tsukuba to see which was heavier, but he accidentally split Tsukuba's peak after he was finished with it.

statement.id: Salah satu legenda menghubungkan aksinya dengan Gunung Fuji dan Gunung Tsukuba.
statement.en: One legend connects its actions with Mount Fuji and Mount Tsukuba.

claims.quote: The Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki, a recording of the imperial customs in the Hitachi Province compiled in the 8th century, also told of a Daidarabotchi living on a hill west of a post office of Hiratsu Ogushi who fed on giant clams from the beach, piling the shells on top of a hill.

statement.id: Catatan daerah lama menggambarkan raksasa yang menumpuk cangkang kerang di bukit.
statement.en: An old regional record describes a giant who gathered clam shells into a hill.

claims.quote: ダダ坊，デイラボー，大太法師などとも呼ばれる伝説の巨人。関東，中部地方を中心に広く分布している。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典「だいだらぼっち」

statement.id: Daidarabotchi adalah raksasa legendaris yang juga disebut ダダ坊, デイラボー, atau 大太法師, dan ceritanya tersebar luas terutama di wilayah Kantō dan Chūbu.
statement.en: Daidarabotchi is a legendary giant also called ダダ坊, デイラボー, or 大太法師, whose tales are widely distributed mainly in the Kantō and Chūbu regions.

claims.quote: この巨人の大足跡とか，その足跡に水がたまってできた沼があると伝えている。また富士山を背負おうとしたとか，山作りの際にこぼした泥が小山になったとも語られている。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典「だいだらぼっち」

statement.id: Tradisi menyebut adanya jejak kaki besar raksasa ini dan rawa yang terbentuk dari air yang menggenangi jejaknya; ia juga diceritakan hendak memanggul Gunung Fuji, dan lumpur yang tumpah saat ia membuat gunung menjadi bukit kecil.
statement.en: Tradition says there are great footprints of this giant and a marsh formed by water collecting in his footprints; he is also said to have tried to carry Mount Fuji on his back, and mud spilled while making mountains became small hills.

claims.quote: 一般に池，沼，山などの生成に関係してこの話が伝えられていることから，もともと天地創造神としての巨人の存在が信じられていたのであろう。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典「だいだらぼっち」

statement.id: Karena kisah ini umumnya dikaitkan dengan terbentuknya kolam, rawa, dan gunung, penulis ensiklopedia menafsirkan bahwa semula orang meyakini adanya raksasa sebagai dewa pencipta langit dan bumi.
statement.en: Because the tale is generally linked to the formation of ponds, marshes and mountains, the encyclopedia author interprets that a giant as a creator god of heaven and earth was originally believed in.

claims.quote: ダイダラボッチの呼称について，タラが貴人の尊称であるとか，あるいはタタラ（踏鞴）の転訛であるとも説かれるが，いまだに決定的な見解を得ない。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典「だいだらぼっち」

statement.id: Mengenai nama Daidarabotchi, ada yang menjelaskan bahwa "tara" adalah gelar kehormatan bagi orang mulia, atau bahwa ia berasal dari perubahan bunyi kata tatara (踏鞴), tetapi belum ada pandangan yang pasti.
statement.en: On the name Daidarabotchi, it is explained that "tara" is an honorific for a noble person, or that it is a corruption of tatara (踏鞴), but no definitive view has been reached.

claims.quote: 大太法師の足跡と伝えられるくぼみが関東，中部その他の地方にあり，東京都世田谷区代田にはその足跡という場所が2ヵ所あって，これは大太法師がひとまたぎした足跡といわれる。
claims.locator: ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典「大太法師」

statement.id: Cekungan yang dikatakan jejak kaki Daidarabotchi terdapat di Kantō, Chūbu, dan daerah lain; di Daita, Setagaya, Tokyo, ada dua tempat yang disebut jejaknya, yang konon sekali langkah raksasa itu.
statement.en: Hollows said to be Daidarabotchi's footprints exist in Kantō, Chūbu and other regions; at Daita in Setagaya, Tokyo, there are two places said to be his footprints, made in a single stride.

claims.quote: 九州では大人 (おおひと) 弥五郎という。巨人の伝説は古く『常陸国風土記』『播磨国風土記』に大人として記されており
claims.locator: ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典「大太法師」

statement.id: Di Kyūshū ia disebut Ōhito Yagorō; legenda raksasa sudah tua dan dicatat sebagai "ōhito" (orang besar) dalam Hitachi no kuni fudoki dan Harima no kuni fudoki.
statement.en: In Kyūshū he is called Ōhito Yagorō; giant legends are old and are recorded as "ōhito" (great people) in the Hitachi no kuni fudoki and Harima no kuni fudoki.

claims.quote: これは大太法師がひとまたぎした足跡といわれる。また大太法師が山をかついで移そうとしたという話が各地に伝えられており，藤づるで縛って運んだ際に途中でつるが切れて土が落ちたのが現在のどこどこの小山となっているという伝説が諸地方にある。
claims.locator: ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典「大太法師」

statement.id: Di berbagai daerah diceritakan bahwa Daidarabotchi mencoba memindahkan gunung dengan memanggulnya; ada legenda bahwa ketika diikat dengan sulur wisteria, sulur itu putus di tengah jalan dan tanah yang jatuh menjadi bukit kecil.
statement.en: Tales in many places say Daidarabotchi tried to carry a mountain to move it; legends in various regions say that when it was bound with wisteria vines, the vines snapped on the way and the earth that fell became a small hill.

summary.id: Ada yang menjelaskan "tara" sebagai gelar kehormatan bagi orang mulia.
summary.en: One explanation takes "tara" as an honorific for a noble person.

summary.id: Ada yang menjelaskan bahwa nama itu berasal dari perubahan bunyi kata tatara (踏鞴); belum ada pandangan yang pasti.
summary.en: Another explanation is that the name is a corruption of tatara (踏鞴); no definitive view has been reached.

text.id: Dilaporkan pada 1907, dicatat 1910, dibahas lagi 1913 dan 1918
text.en: Reported in 1907, recorded in 1910, discussed again in 1913 and 1918

short_description.id: Dingonek adalah kriptid, makhluk air bertaring dan bersisik bercorak macan tutul, yang konon terlihat di sekitar Danau Victoria pada 1907 menurut kisah para pemburu.
short_description.en: The dingonek is a cryptid, a fanged, scaly water beast with leopard-like markings, reportedly seen around Lake Victoria in 1907 according to hunters' accounts.

long_description.id: Dingonek dikenal dari kisah pemburu John Alfred Jordan, yang konon melihatnya bersama rombongannya dekat Danau Victoria pada 1907. Kisah itu dicatat Edgar Beecher Bronson dalam memoar In Closed Territory (1910). Dalam memoar itu, nama Dingonek disebut sebagai nama yang diberikan orang Lumbwa.
long_description.en: The dingonek is known from the story of hunter John Alfred Jordan, who reportedly saw it with his party near Lake Victoria in 1907. Edgar Beecher Bronson set the story down in his memoir In Closed Territory (1910). In that memoir the name Dingonek is said to have been given by the Lumbwa.

long_description.id: Jordan melukiskan makhluk sepanjang empat belas atau lima belas kaki dengan kepala sebesar singa betina bercorak macan tutul, sepasang taring putih panjang yang mencuat dari rahang atas, punggung selebar kuda nil yang bersisik seperti armadillo, dan ekor bersirip lebar. Orang Lumbwa yang pertama melihatnya menyebutnya semacam campuran ular laut, macan tutul, dan paus. Jordan menembaknya dari jarak dekat, tetapi makhluk itu melompat dari air dan tak pernah ditemukan lagi meski dicari dua hari.
long_description.en: Jordan pictured a beast fourteen or fifteen feet long, its head the size of a lioness's with leopard markings, two long white fangs jutting down from the upper jaw, a hippo-wide back with armadillo-like scales, and a wide finned tail. The Lumbwa who first spotted it likened it to a blend of sea serpent, leopard and whale. Jordan fired at it from close range, yet it leapt from the water and was never found again despite two days of searching.

long_description.id: Bronson sendiri meragukan pengakuan salah satu anggota rombongan yang mengaku melihatnya dua kali. Pada 1913, Charles William Hobley menulis bahwa ia mendapat laporan lain tentang makhluk serupa: seorang saksi melihat binatang bertotol, bersisik, berkepala seperti berang-berang, hanyut di atas batang kayu, tanpa taring panjang. Pada 1918, MacLean's bahkan menyatakannya spesies hewan baru, dan Jordan menulis bahwa makhluk itu hanya hidup di Danau Victoria Nyanza dan anak-anak sungainya.
long_description.en: Bronson himself doubted a party member who claimed two sightings. In 1913 Charles William Hobley wrote that he had found further reports of a similar creature: one witness saw a spotted, scaly animal with an otter-like head drifting on a log, without long fangs. In 1918 MacLean's even announced it as a new animal species, and Jordan wrote that it lived only in Lake Victoria Nyanza and its tributaries.

long_description.id: Bronson juga mencatat kepercayaan setempat tentang reptil danau raksasa. Penduduk di pantai utara danau disebut menyembah ular atau reptil air besar yang kedatangannya menandakan panen melimpah, dan mempersembahkan korban sapi dan domba kepada reptil danau mengerikan bernama Luquata.
long_description.en: Bronson also recorded local beliefs about a giant lake reptile. People on the lake's north shore were said to worship a great water serpent or reptile whose arrival foretold rich harvests, and to offer cattle and sheep to a fearsome lake reptile named Luquata.

claims.quote: The dingonek is a creature said to have been seen near Lake Victoria in 1907 by big game hunter John Alfred Jordan and members of his hunting party, as recounted by fellow big-game hunter Edgar Beecher Bronson in his 1910 memoir In Closed Territory.

statement.id: Dingonek adalah makhluk yang konon terlihat dekat Danau Victoria (Lake Victoria) pada 1907 oleh pemburu John Alfred Jordan dan rombongannya, sebagaimana dikisahkan Edgar Beecher Bronson dalam memoar tahun 1910, In Closed Territory.
statement.en: The dingonek is a creature said to have been seen near Lake Victoria in 1907 by hunter John Alfred Jordan and his party, as recounted by Edgar Beecher Bronson in his 1910 memoir In Closed Territory.

claims.quote: This account was followed by an article published in 1913 in the East Africa Natural History Society by Charles William Hobley, in which he claims to have encountered further accounts of similarly described creatures.

statement.id: Kisah itu disusul artikel Charles William Hobley tahun 1913 di East Africa Natural History Society, yang mengaku menemukan laporan lain tentang makhluk serupa.
statement.en: This account was followed by a 1913 article by Charles William Hobley in the East Africa Natural History Society, claiming further accounts of similarly described creatures.

claims.quote: In 1918, an article published by MacLean's declared that the beast was a newly discovered animal species.

statement.id: Pada 1918, sebuah artikel di MacLean's menyatakan makhluk itu spesies hewan (animal species) yang baru ditemukan.
statement.en: In 1918 an article in MacLean's declared the beast a newly discovered animal species.

claims.quote: One member of the party, Mataia, claims to have seen it twice, yet Bronson expressed skepticism.

statement.id: Seorang anggota rombongan, Mataia, mengaku melihatnya dua kali, tetapi Bronson meragukannya (skepticism).
statement.en: One member of the party, Mataia, claims to have seen it twice, yet Bronson expressed skepticism.

claims.quote: He describes it as spotted like a leopard, covered with scales, and having a head like an otter; he did not see the long fangs described by Mr. Jordan.

statement.id: Saksi yang dikutip Hobley menggambarkannya bertotol seperti macan tutul (leopard), bersisik, berkepala seperti berang-berang (otter), dan tidak melihat taring panjang seperti yang diceritakan Jordan.
statement.en: The witness quoted by Hobley describes it as spotted like a leopard, covered with scales and with a head like an otter; he did not see the long fangs described by Jordan.

claims.quote: The beast came floating down the river on a big log, and he estimated its length at about sixteen feet

statement.id: Makhluk itu hanyut di sungai di atas batang kayu besar (big log), dan saksi memperkirakan panjangnya sekitar enam belas kaki (sixteen feet).
statement.en: The beast came floating down the river on a big log, and the witness estimated its length at about sixteen feet.

claims.quote: It lives in Lake Victoria Nyanza and its numerous tributaries, and there is no record of the monster having been seen in any other part of the world.

statement.id: Menurut Jordan, makhluk itu hidup di Danau Victoria Nyanza dan banyak anak sungainya (tributaries), dan tidak pernah tercatat terlihat di tempat lain.
statement.en: According to Jordan it lives in Lake Victoria Nyanza and its numerous tributaries, with no record of it seen anywhere else in the world.

claims.quote: comes up the Maggori River out of the lake the Lumbwa have christened Dingonek.

statement.id: Jordan menyebut makhluk dari danau itu dinamai Dingonek oleh orang Lumbwa, dan memperkirakan nilainya lima sampai sepuluh ribu pound (five or ten thousand quid).
statement.en: Jordan says the lake creature was christened Dingonek by the Lumbwa, and reckons it would fetch five or ten thousand quid at least.

claims.quote: some sort of cross between a sea serpent, a leopard, and a whale

statement.id: Orang Lumbwa melukiskannya sebagai semacam campuran ular laut (sea serpent), macan tutul (leopard), dan paus (whale).
statement.en: The Lumbwa described it as some sort of cross between a sea serpent, a leopard and a whale.

claims.quote: fourteen or fifteen feet long, head big as that of a lioness but shaped and marked like a leopard, two long white fangs sticking down straight out of his upper jaw, back broad as a hippo, scaled like an armadillo, but colored and marked like a leopard, and a broad fin tail

statement.id: Jordan menggambarkannya sepanjang empat belas atau lima belas kaki (fourteen or fifteen feet), berkepala sebesar singa betina bercorak macan tutul, bertaring putih panjang dari rahang atas, berpunggung selebar kuda nil (hippo), bersisik seperti armadillo, dan berekor sirip lebar.
statement.en: Jordan describes it as fourteen or fifteen feet long, with a head as big as a lioness's but marked like a leopard, two long white fangs from the upper jaw, a back as broad as a hippo, scaled like an armadillo, and a broad fin tail.

claims.quote: Blast that blighter's fangs, but they looked long enough to go clean through a man.

statement.id: Jordan berkata taringnya tampak cukup panjang untuk menembus tubuh manusia (go clean through a man).
statement.en: Jordan says its fangs looked long enough to go clean through a man.

claims.quote: a .303, where placed, should have killed anything, for he was less than ten yards from me when I shot, but though we watched waters and shores over a range of several miles for two days, no sight did we get of him or his tracks.

statement.id: Jordan menembaknya dengan peluru .303 dari jarak kurang dari sepuluh yard (ten yards), tetapi meski mencari selama dua hari sepanjang beberapa mil, mereka tak melihatnya lagi atau jejaknya.
statement.en: Jordan shot it with a .303 from less than ten yards, but though they watched waters and shores over several miles for two days, they saw neither it nor its tracks.

claims.quote: a great water serpent or reptile was seen on or near the north shore of the lake, which was worshipped by the natives, who believed its coming a harbinger of heavy crops and large increase of their flocks and herds.

statement.id: Menurut keterangan dalam memoar itu, seekor ular atau reptil air besar (water serpent or reptile) kadang terlihat di pantai utara danau dan disembah penduduk, yang menganggap kedatangannya pertanda panen melimpah dan ternak bertambah.
statement.en: According to information in the memoir, a great water serpent or reptile was seen near the north shore of the lake and worshipped by the natives, who took its coming as a harbinger of heavy crops and increasing herds.

claims.quote: sacrificed burnt offerings of cattle and sheep to a lake reptile of great size and terrible appearance they called Luquata, which occasionally appeared along or near the shore

statement.id: Penduduk pantai utara danau mempersembahkan korban bakaran sapi dan domba (cattle and sheep) kepada reptil danau raksasa berpenampilan mengerikan yang mereka sebut Luquata.
statement.en: People of the north shore of the lake sacrificed burnt offerings of cattle and sheep to a huge, terrible lake reptile they called Luquata.

summary.id: Jordan: bertaring putih panjang, berkepala seperti singa betina bercorak macan tutul.
summary.en: Jordan: long white fangs, lioness-sized head marked like a leopard.

summary.id: Saksi Hobley: berkepala seperti berang-berang dan tanpa taring panjang.
summary.en: Hobley's witness: an otter-like head and no long fangs.

short_description.id: Dover Demon adalah kriptid kecil berkepala besar yang dilaporkan oleh remaja di Dover, Massachusetts, pada 21–22 April 1977 dan tidak pernah terlihat lagi.
short_description.en: The Dover Demon is a small, large-headed cryptid reported by teenagers in Dover, Massachusetts, on April 21–22, 1977, and never seen again.

long_description.id: Dover Demon adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan terlihat pada 21–22 April 1977 di Dover, Massachusetts. Bill Bartlett (17) melaporkan melihat makhluk setinggi sekitar 4 kaki bermata oranye menyala, tanpa hidung atau mulut yang terlihat, dan berkepala berbentuk semangka yang bertengger di dinding batu yang rusak. Pada malam yang sama John Baxter (15) melaporkan hal serupa di Miller Hill Road, dan malam berikutnya Abby Brabham (15) di Springdale Avenue. Baxter menggambarkan makhluk berkepala besar berlobus dua seperti kacang dengan lengan dan kaki kurus berjari panjang.
long_description.en: The Dover Demon is a cryptid said to have been seen on April 21–22, 1977, in Dover, Massachusetts. Bill Bartlett, 17, reported a creature about 4 feet tall with glowing orange eyes, no visible nose or mouth, and a watermelon-shaped head, perched on a broken stone wall. That same evening John Baxter, 15, reported something similar on Miller Hill Road, and the next night Abby Brabham, 15, on Springdale Avenue. Baxter described a huge double-lobed, peanut-like head with skinny arms and legs and long fingers.

long_description.id: Ketiga remaja itu membuat sketsa masing-masing; sketsa Bartlett dan Baxter sangat mirip: makhluk kurus berkepala besar berlobus dua tanpa ciri wajah selain mata menyala. Penampakan baru diketahui publik pada paruh pertama Mei dan diselidiki oleh Mutual UFO Network serta organisasi lain, tetapi tidak pernah ditemukan bukti. Tidak ada bukti fisik, hanya kesaksian para remaja itu.
long_description.en: The three teenagers each made sketches, and those of Bartlett and Baxter were strikingly similar: a thin creature with a huge double-lobed head and no facial features except glowing eyes. The sightings only became public in the first half of May and were investigated by the Mutual UFO Network and other organizations, but no evidence was ever found. There is no physical evidence, only the teenagers' testimony.

long_description.id: Sebagai penjelasan, ada yang mengusulkan anak kuda atau anak moose, dan Joe Nickell mengusulkan burung hantu salju yang bulunya memantulkan lampu mobil. Brian Dunning menilai ilusi seperti itu seharusnya menipu orang lain pula, padahal tidak pernah. Polisi menyebut gambaran para remaja itu mungkin tidak lebih dari lelucon liburan sekolah.
long_description.en: As explanations, some proposed a foal or moose calf, and Joe Nickell proposed a snowy owl whose plumage reflected car headlights. Brian Dunning judged that such an illusion should have fooled others too, but it never did. Police said the teenagers' descriptions were probably nothing more than a school vacation hoax.

claims.quote: The Dover Demon is a cryptid reportedly sighted on April 21–22, 1977, in Dover, Massachusetts, a town approximately 15 miles (24 km) southwest of Boston.

statement.en: The Dover Demon is a cryptid reportedly sighted on April 21–22, 1977, in Dover, Massachusetts, a town approximately 15 miles (24 km) southwest of Boston.

claims.quote: While driving along Farm Street in Dover, Massachusetts on April 21, 1977, seventeen-year-old William "Bill" Bartlett reported seeing an unknown being approximately 4 feet (1.2 m) tall, which he claimed possessed glowing orange eyes, lacked a visible nose or mouth, and had a watermelon-shaped head.

statement.id: Saat berkendara di Farm Street, Dover, pada 21 April 1977, William 'Bill' Bartlett (17) melaporkan melihat makhluk tak dikenal setinggi sekitar 4 kaki (1,2 m) yang menurutnya bermata oranye menyala, tanpa hidung atau mulut yang terlihat, dan berkepala berbentuk semangka.
statement.en: While driving along Farm Street in Dover on April 21, 1977, seventeen-year-old William 'Bill' Bartlett reported seeing an unknown being about 4 feet (1.2 m) tall, which he claimed had glowing orange eyes, no visible nose or mouth, and a watermelon-shaped head.

claims.quote: That same evening, 15-year-old John Baxter reported seeing something similar on Miller Hill Road. The following night, another 15-year-old, Abby Brabham, claimed to have encountered the being on Springdale Avenue.

statement.id: Pada malam yang sama, John Baxter (15) melaporkan melihat sesuatu yang serupa di Miller Hill Road; malam berikutnya Abby Brabham (15) mengaku bertemu makhluk itu di Springdale Avenue.
statement.en: That same evening, 15-year-old John Baxter reported seeing something similar on Miller Hill Road; the following night, another 15-year-old, Abby Brabham, claimed to have encountered the being on Springdale Avenue.

claims.quote: A local news report noted that the locations of the alleged sightings, when plotted on a map, formed a straight line extending for more than 2 miles (3.2 km). The sightings did not become public until the first half of May.

statement.id: Sebuah laporan berita lokal mencatat bahwa lokasi dugaan penampakan, bila diplot di peta, membentuk garis lurus sepanjang lebih dari 2 mil (3,2 km); penampakan itu baru diketahui publik pada paruh pertama Mei.
statement.en: A local news report noted that the locations of the alleged sightings, plotted on a map, formed a straight line extending more than 2 miles (3.2 km); the sightings did not become public until the first half of May.

claims.quote: Although none of the witnesses reported seeing a UFO, the sightings were investigated by the Mutual UFO Network and other associated organizations.

statement.id: Meski tak satu pun saksi melaporkan melihat UFO, penampakan itu diselidiki oleh Mutual UFO Network dan organisasi terkait lainnya.
statement.en: Although none of the witnesses reported seeing a UFO, the sightings were investigated by the Mutual UFO Network and other associated organizations.

statement.id: Sebagian penjelasan mengusulkan bahwa yang sebenarnya dilihat para saksi mungkin anak kuda atau anak moose.
statement.en: Some explanations have proposed that what the witnesses may have actually seen was a foal or moose calf.

claims.quote: Skeptic Joe Nickell suggested that a snowy owl could account for the reported sightings. He speculated that the owl's plumage may have reflected the yellow headlights of older automobiles, producing the peach-colored appearance described by Bartlett.

statement.id: Skeptis Joe Nickell menyarankan bahwa burung hantu salju dapat menjelaskan penampakan itu; ia menduga bulunya memantulkan lampu depan kuning mobil lama sehingga tampak berwarna persik seperti yang digambarkan Bartlett.
statement.en: Skeptic Joe Nickell suggested that a snowy owl could account for the reported sightings, speculating that the owl's plumage may have reflected the yellow headlights of older automobiles, producing the peach-colored appearance Bartlett described.

claims.quote: Late on the nights of April 21st and 22nd, 1977, four students from Dover-Sherborn High School (total enrollment just under 500) all shared an incredible experience, but in three (apparently unconnected) incidents. Their ages ranged from 15 to 18.

statement.id: Pada larut malam 21 dan 22 April 1977, empat siswa Dover-Sherborn High School (jumlah siswa kurang dari 500) mengalami pengalaman luar biasa dalam tiga kejadian yang tampaknya tak berhubungan; usia mereka 15 sampai 18 tahun.
statement.en: Late on the nights of April 21 and 22, 1977, four students from Dover-Sherborn High School (enrollment just under 500) shared an incredible experience in three apparently unconnected incidents; their ages ranged from 15 to 18.

claims.quote: The first came when Bill Bartlett, 17, was rolling in his sweet Volkswagen with some friends. Suddenly he saw — though nobody else in the car did — a bizarre creature on the side of the road: short but with a huge head, white or peach in color, big eyes and no other facial features, and very thin neck and limbs.

statement.id: Menurut tulisan ini, Bill Bartlett (17) berkendara bersama beberapa teman dan tiba-tiba melihat, tanpa terlihat oleh orang lain di mobil, makhluk aneh di tepi jalan: pendek tetapi berkepala besar, berwarna putih atau persik, bermata besar tanpa ciri wajah lain, dengan leher dan anggota badan sangat kurus.
statement.en: According to this account, Bill Bartlett, 17, was driving with some friends and suddenly saw, though nobody else in the car did, a bizarre creature at the roadside: short but with a huge head, white or peach in color, big eyes and no other facial features, and a very thin neck and limbs.

claims.quote: Two hours later, John Baxter (15) was walking home when he encountered a silhouette walking toward him. He called out, and the creature ran away across a ditch, and John then caught his first good look at it. It had a huge double-lobed head like a peanut, and skinny arms and legs with long fingers

statement.id: Dua jam kemudian, John Baxter (15) yang berjalan pulang bertemu siluet yang berjalan ke arahnya; ia berseru, makhluk itu lari melintasi parit, dan John melihatnya dengan jelas: kepala besar berlobus dua seperti kacang, serta lengan dan kaki kurus berjari panjang.
statement.en: Two hours later, John Baxter (15) was walking home when he met a silhouette walking toward him; he called out, the creature ran away across a ditch, and John then got a good look: a huge double-lobed head like a peanut, and skinny arms and legs with long fingers.

claims.quote: Bartlett (today a professional artist) and Baxter both drew sketches of what they saw, and they were strikingly similar. A small thin creature with a huge double-lobed head, tiny body, and shockingly skinny neck and limbs — and no features on its face except glowing eyes, reflecting the headlights.

statement.id: Bartlett (kini seniman profesional) dan Baxter sama-sama menggambar sketsa apa yang mereka lihat, dan sketsa itu sangat mirip: makhluk kecil kurus berkepala besar berlobus dua, bertubuh mungil, berleher dan anggota badan sangat kurus, tanpa ciri wajah selain mata menyala yang memantulkan lampu.
statement.en: Bartlett (today a professional artist) and Baxter both drew sketches of what they saw, and the sketches were strikingly similar: a small thin creature with a huge double-lobed head, tiny body, and shockingly skinny neck and limbs, with no facial features except glowing eyes reflecting the headlights.

claims.quote: We have no physical evidence that anything happened at all; just the testimony of these four young people.

statement.id: Tidak ada bukti fisik bahwa sesuatu terjadi sama sekali, hanya kesaksian keempat anak muda itu.
statement.en: There is no physical evidence that anything happened at all, just the testimony of these four young people.

claims.quote: Despite police searches and the participation of four researchers from five different UFO and Fortean organizations, including [cryptozoologist] Loren Coleman, no evidence was ever found.

statement.id: Meski ada pencarian polisi dan keterlibatan empat peneliti dari lima organisasi UFO dan Fortean berbeda, termasuk [kriptozoolog] Loren Coleman, tidak pernah ditemukan bukti.
statement.en: Despite police searches and the participation of four researchers from five different UFO and Fortean organizations, including [cryptozoologist] Loren Coleman, no evidence was ever found.

claims.quote: But if it happened to four people in town in just 24 hours, it must be a very compelling illusion. Yet the illusion never fooled anyone, ever, before or since.

statement.id: Dunning berpendapat bahwa jika hal itu terjadi pada empat orang dalam 24 jam, ilusinya pasti sangat meyakinkan, namun ilusi itu tidak pernah menipu siapa pun sebelum maupun sesudahnya.
statement.en: Dunning argues that if it happened to four people in town in just 24 hours, it must be a very compelling illusion, yet the illusion never fooled anyone before or since.

claims.quote: In 2009, the Dover Demon was featured in an episode of the American horror television series Lost Tapes, which aired on Animal Planet.

statement.en: In 2009, the Dover Demon was featured in an episode of the American horror television series Lost Tapes, which aired on Animal Planet.

long_description.id: Engkanto adalah roh lingkungan mitos yang konon dapat tampil dalam wujud manusia dan sering dikaitkan dengan arwah leluhur serta arwah orang mati yang disebut anito. Istilah ini adalah sebutan payung untuk makhluk-makhluk mirip manusia yang terpesona, yang diambil dari bahasa Spanyol ketika para penjajah bingung menghadapi beragamnya makhluk mitos di Filipina. Menurut Demetrio, kata engkanto tampaknya berasal dari "encantado", bentuk lampau kata kerja Spanyol encantar yang berarti tersihir atau terpesona. Menurut esai itu, kepercayaan ini ditemukan di Luzon dan cukup umum di Visayas dan Mindanao.
long_description.en: Engkanto are mythical environmental spirits said to be able to appear in human form, often associated with ancestral spirits and with the spirits of the dead called anito. The term is an umbrella for enchanted humanlike beings, adopted from Spanish when the colonizers were bewildered by the variety of mythical beings in the Philippines. According to Demetrio, the word engkanto seems to derive from "encantado", the preterite perfect of the Spanish verb encantar, meaning bewitched or spell-bound. According to the essay, the belief is found in Luzon and is quite common in the Visayas and Mindanao.

long_description.id: Engkanto mirip manusia: mereka menua, tampaknya berjenis kelamin laki-laki dan perempuan, dapat sakit, bahkan mati. Sebagian tampak rupawan dengan mata biru, kulit terang, dan rambut keemasan, atau punya ciri tak biasa seperti hidung mancung dan tanpa lekuk di atas bibir. Tempat tinggal mereka biasanya tampak seperti batu besar, pohon, atau bayangan, tetapi bisa tampak sebagai istana megah bagi manusia yang mereka sukai; mereka menyukai pohon besar seperti balete. Menurut Demetrio, mereka berkulit cerah, berambut keemasan, dan bermata biru, mewakili yang terbaik dari orang Spanyol dan Amerika; makanan mereka berkualitas terbaik tetapi tanpa garam, dan mereka konon tertarik secara romantis pada gadis atau pemuda berkulit cokelat.
long_description.en: Engkanto resemble humans: they age, appear to have male and female sexes, can fall ill and even die. Some look beautiful with blue eyes, fair skin and golden hair, or have unusual features such as high-bridged noses and no philtrum. Their dwellings usually look like large rocks, trees or shadows, but can appear as magnificent palaces to humans they befriend; they favour large trees such as the balete. According to Demetrio, they are fair-complexioned, golden-haired and blue-eyed, exemplifying the best of the Spaniards and Americans; their food is of the very best quality but has no salt, and they are reportedly drawn romantically to dark-skinned young women or men.

long_description.id: Orang yang tidak disukai engkanto dapat menjadi murung, gila, atau menghilang berhari-hari hingga berbulan-bulan, mungkin karena dirasuki; mereka juga dikatakan dapat menyebabkan demam dan penyakit kulit serta menyesatkan pejalan di hutan. Jimat anting-anting atau agimat dikatakan dapat menangkalnya. Sebaliknya, orang yang mereka sukai dapat memperoleh kekuasaan dan kekayaan, dan dukun berusaha berhubungan dengan engkanto untuk memperoleh kemampuan menyembuhkan yang lebih baik. Demetrio mencatat bahwa engkanto kadang dikaitkan dengan arwah leluhur dan menjadi objek rasa takut, serta menghukum orang yang mengabaikan kasih sayang mereka dengan aksi seperti melempar batu. Engkanto dapat berwatak baik atau buruk, dan Demetrio menafsirkan sisi sakralnya sebagai "demonik", yaitu memuat kemungkinan baik maupun jahat.
long_description.en: Those the engkanto do not favour may become depressed, go mad or disappear for days or months, possibly through possession; they are also said to cause fevers and skin diseases and to lead travellers astray in the forest. An anting-anting or agimat amulet is said to ward them off. Those they favour, however, may gain power and riches, and shamans try to commune with engkanto to gain better healing powers. Demetrio notes that engkanto are sometimes associated with ancestral souls and are objects of dread, and punish those who disregard their affections with feats such as stone-throwing. Engkanto may be good or bad, and Demetrio interprets their sacred aspect as "demonic", containing the possibility of both good and evil.

long_description.id: Folklorawan Francisco Demetrio meneliti 87 cerita rakyat dari Visayas dan Mindanao tentang engkanto dan, menurut ringkasan sebuah ensiklopedia daring, berpendapat bahwa sosok engkanto didasarkan pada para biarawan Eropa awal. Dalam esainya, ia menyebut kepercayaan ini tampaknya bertahan setidaknya empat abad, menilai tidak setiap kasus yang dilaporkan itu asli, dan mengajukan hipotesis bahwa hilangnya korban dan kegilaan mereka merupakan bagian dari skenario inisiasi dukun. Artikel Aswang Project menulis bahwa evolusi makhluk folklor hampir selalu berawal dari kepercayaan pada roh-roh ini.
long_description.en: Folklorist Francisco Demetrio studied 87 folk stories from the Visayas and Mindanao about engkanto and, according to an online encyclopedia summary, argued that they were based on early European friars. In his essay he notes that the belief seems to have lasted at least four centuries, judges that not every reported case is authentic, and puts forward the hypothesis that victims' disappearance and madness form part of a shaman's initiation scenario. The Aswang Project article writes that the evolution of folkloric creatures almost always begins with belief in these spirits.

long_description.id: Menurut Demetrio, orang berdiam diri ketika mendekati tempat yang dipercaya sebagai kediaman engkanto, seperti batu besar, pohon besar, gua rahasia, atau mata air; ia juga mencatat bahwa mereka mengerjai orang dan dapat menjelma menyerupai teman dan kerabat manusia, sementara dukun pergi ke gua terpencil pada Kamis Putih atau Jumat Agung untuk berhubungan dengan mereka. Sebuah ensiklopedia daring mencatat varian roh Bagobo, yaitu tahamaling (perempuan) dan mahomanay (laki-laki), serta penampilan engkanto dalam film dan televisi Filipina.
long_description.en: According to Demetrio, people keep silent when approaching places believed to be engkanto habitats, such as large rocks, large trees, secret caves or springs; he also notes that they play jokes on people and can take the likeness of mortal friends and relatives, while shamans go into lonely caves on Holy Thursday or Good Friday to commune with them. An online encyclopedia records the Bagobo spirit variants, the female tahamaling and the male mahomanay, and engkanto portrayals in Philippine film and television.

claims.quote: The engkanto of Philippine mythology are highly similar to elves of European folklore.

statement.en: The engkanto of Philippine mythology are highly similar to the elves of European folklore.

statement.en: Some engkanto appear beautiful with blue eyes, fair complexion and golden hair, but may also have unusual features such as high-bridged noses and absent philtrums.

claims.quote: These spirits also sometimes lead travelers astray in the forest, even kidnap them. This, however, is said to be avoidable by bringing an "anting-anting" or "agimat" a piece of magical charm or amulet that wards away evil spirits and prevents them from harming the wielder.

statement.id: Roh-roh ini kadang menyesatkan pejalan di hutan, bahkan menculik mereka; hal itu dikatakan dapat dihindari dengan membawa "anting-anting" atau "agimat", jimat atau benda bertuah yang menangkal roh jahat dan mencegahnya mencelakai pemakainya.
statement.en: These spirits sometimes lead travelers astray in the forest and even kidnap them; this is said to be avoidable by carrying an "anting-anting" or "agimat", a magical charm or amulet that wards away evil spirits and prevents them from harming the wielder.

claims.quote: However, if they do favor someone, they are generous and capable of bringing power and riches to that person. Shamans often try to commune with engkanto on holy days to obtain better healing powers from them

statement.en: If they do favour someone, however, they are generous and can bring that person power and riches; shamans often try to commune with engkanto on holy days to obtain better healing powers from them.

claims.quote: An engkanto may choose to stay by a human's side as told by stories where characters are usually in either a sense of trance or a deep loss of energy. Engkanto may be good or bad.

statement.id: Seorang engkanto dapat memilih tinggal di sisi manusia, seperti dalam kisah-kisah tempat tokohnya biasanya berada dalam keadaan seperti trans atau kehilangan tenaga yang dalam; engkanto dapat berwatak baik atau buruk.
statement.en: An engkanto may choose to stay by a human's side, as in stories where the characters are usually in a trance or suffer a deep loss of energy; engkanto may be good or bad.

claims.quote: Other variants exhibit sexual dimorphism such as Bagobo spirits which are separated into the female tahamaling and the male mahomanay. The female spirit is alleged to have a red complexion while males have a fair complexion.

statement.id: Varian lain menunjukkan dimorfisme seksual, misalnya roh Bagobo yang dibedakan menjadi tahamaling (perempuan) dan mahomanay (laki-laki); roh perempuan konon berkulit kemerahan, sedangkan yang laki-laki berkulit cerah.
statement.en: Other variants show sexual dimorphism, such as the Bagobo spirits divided into the female tahamaling and the male mahomanay; the female is alleged to have a red complexion while males have a fair complexion.

statement.en: According to the essay, "encantado", from which engkanto seems to be derived, is the preterite perfect of the Spanish verb encantar and means "bewitched", "spell-bound" or "enchanted".

claims.quote: Engkantos are sometimes associated with souls of dead ancestors, and are therefore objects of dread.

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, engkanto kadang dikaitkan dengan arwah leluhur yang telah meninggal sehingga menjadi objek rasa takut.
statement.en: According to the essay, engkanto are sometimes associated with the souls of dead ancestors and are therefore objects of dread.

claims.quote: They inject fear by the spectacular feats they do in order to punish whoever disregards their affections: stonethrowing, wrapping clothes around a post closed on both ends

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, engkanto menebar rasa takut lewat aksi mengejutkan untuk menghukum orang yang mengabaikan kasih sayang mereka, seperti melempar batu dan melilitkan pakaian pada tiang yang tertutup di kedua ujungnya.
statement.en: According to the essay, engkanto instil fear through spectacular feats to punish whoever disregards their affections, such as stone-throwing and wrapping clothes around a post closed at both ends.

claims.quote: The aspect of the sacred which experience of the engkantos manifests seems to be demonic. It is compounded of the possibility for both good and evil; holy and profane.

statement.id: Esai itu menafsirkan sisi sakral yang tampak dalam pengalaman dengan engkanto sebagai "demonik", yaitu memuat kemungkinan baik maupun jahat, suci maupun profan.
statement.en: The essay interprets the sacred aspect shown in experiences of the engkanto as "demonic", containing the possibility of both good and evil, holy and profane.

claims.quote: shortly after the coming of Christianity (Alzina, 1668), the call to the office of bailana or daetan (priestess) among the Bisayans began precisely with this madness, or tiaw which the candidate underwent.

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, tak lama setelah kedatangan agama Kristen (Alzina, 1668), panggilan menjadi bailana atau daetan (pendeta perempuan) di kalangan orang Bisaya bermula tepat dari kegilaan, atau tiaw, yang dialami sang calon.
statement.en: According to the essay, shortly after the coming of Christianity (Alzina, 1668), the call to the office of bailana or daetan (priestess) among the Bisayans began precisely with the madness, or tiaw, that the candidate underwent.

claims.quote: Not every case of reported engkanto phenomenon is authentic. There are fake “victims” of engkanto who aim at catching the attention of the public.

statement.id: Esai itu menulis bahwa tidak setiap kasus engkanto yang dilaporkan itu asli; ada "korban" palsu yang ingin menarik perhatian publik.
statement.en: The essay writes that not every reported engkanto case is authentic; there are fake "victims" who aim to catch the public's attention.

claims.quote: For the engkantos were always seen as handsome people, in fact they were said to look like Spaniards.

statement.id: Esai itu mencatat bahwa engkanto selalu dipandang sebagai orang yang rupawan, bahkan dikatakan mirip orang Spanyol.
statement.en: The essay notes that engkanto were always seen as handsome people, in fact said to look like Spaniards.

claims.quote: the disappearance of the soul (ecstacy) or the actual physical disappearance of the victim, are all part and parcel of the scenario of initiation to which these select few are introduced in order to prepare them for the new role they are to play in the community.

statement.id: Menurut hipotesis esai itu, menghilangnya jiwa (ekstase) atau hilangnya fisik korban merupakan bagian dari skenario inisiasi yang dijalani segelintir orang terpilih untuk menyiapkan peran baru mereka dalam masyarakat.
statement.en: In the essay's hypothesis, the disappearance of the soul (ecstasy) or the actual physical disappearance of the victim is part of an initiation scenario through which a select few are prepared for a new role in the community.

claims.quote: Rural peoples of the Philippines believe in the existence of superhuman beings called engkantos as well as in the influence they exercise on human lives. The belief is found in Luzon, and also is quite common in the Visayas and in Mindanao.

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, masyarakat pedesaan Filipina percaya akan keberadaan makhluk adimanusia bernama engkanto dan pengaruhnya atas kehidupan manusia; kepercayaan ini ditemukan di Luzon dan cukup umum di Visayas dan Mindanao.
statement.en: According to the essay, rural peoples of the Philippines believe in superhuman beings called engkantos and in their influence on human lives; the belief is found in Luzon and is quite common in the Visayas and Mindanao.

claims.quote: this belief seems to have perdured for at least four centuries: Povedano (16th century), Alzina (17th)

statement.id: Esai itu mencatat bahwa kepercayaan ini tampaknya bertahan setidaknya empat abad, dengan rujukan dari Povedano (abad ke-16) dan Alzina (abad ke-17).
statement.en: The essay notes that this belief seems to have lasted at least four centuries, with allusions by Povedano (16th century) and Alzina (17th).

claims.quote: They are of fair complexion, golden haired, blue eyed; they have clean-cut features and perfectly chiselled faces. They exemplify the best of the Spaniards (in the past) and of the Americans (in the present).

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, engkanto digambarkan berkulit cerah, berambut keemasan, bermata biru, dengan wajah bersih dan sempurna, mewakili yang terbaik dari orang Spanyol (dahulu) dan orang Amerika (kini).
statement.en: According to the essay, engkanto are described as fair-complexioned, golden-haired and blue-eyed with clean-cut, perfectly chiselled faces, exemplifying the best of the Spaniards (in the past) and the Americans (in the present).

statement.en: According to the essay, the engkanto's food is of the very best quality but contains no salt.

claims.quote: Though beautiful and fairskinned, engkantos are said to be romantically attracted to a brown-skinned girl, or boy.

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, meski cantik dan berkulit cerah, engkanto konon tertarik secara romantis pada gadis atau pemuda berkulit cokelat.
statement.en: According to the essay, though beautiful and fair-skinned, engkantos are said to be romantically attracted to a brown-skinned girl or boy.

claims.quote: They are whimsical and unpredictable; they play jokes on people; making them go astray in the forest at night, or transform themselves into the likenesses of mortal friends and relatives in order to dupe the objects of their desire.

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, engkanto berubah-ubah dan tak terduga: mereka mengerjai orang dengan menyesatkannya di hutan pada malam hari, atau menjelma menyerupai teman dan kerabat manusia untuk memperdaya orang yang mereka inginkan.
statement.en: According to the essay, engkanto are whimsical and unpredictable: they play jokes on people by making them go astray in the forest at night, or take the likeness of mortal friends and relatives to dupe the objects of their desire.

claims.quote: People observe silence when they approach their reputed habitats: large rocks, large trees, secret caves or springs and fountains.

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, orang berdiam diri ketika mendekati tempat yang dipercaya sebagai kediaman engkanto: batu besar, pohon besar, gua rahasia, atau mata air dan pancuran.
statement.en: According to the essay, people keep silent when approaching the places reputed to be their habitats: large rocks, large trees, secret caves, or springs and fountains.

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, engkanto diketahui dapat menimbulkan penyakit seperti demam, bisul, dan penyakit kulit lain akibat kutukan mereka.
statement.en: According to the essay, engkanto are known to be able to inflict diseases such as fevers, boils and other skin diseases as a result of their curse.

claims.quote: Without knowing it someone may brush against the invisible engkanto, and suddenly he is slapped in the face or his skull is cracked by a blow.

statement.id: Menurut esai itu, seseorang bisa tanpa sadar bersentuhan dengan engkanto yang tak terlihat, lalu tiba-tiba ditampar wajahnya atau dipukul hingga tengkoraknya retak.
statement.en: According to the essay, someone may unknowingly brush against the invisible engkanto and be suddenly slapped in the face or have his skull cracked by a blow.

claims.quote: Shamans and mananambals go out of their way into far and lonely caves on Holy Thursday or Good Friday in order to commune with the engkantos and to acquire power for healing diseases and battling evil spirits.

statement.en: According to the essay, shamans and mananambals go far into lonely caves on Holy Thursday or Good Friday to commune with the engkantos and gain power for healing diseases and battling evil spirits.

long_description.id: Feilong ('naga terbang') adalah makhluk legendaris yang terbang di antara awan dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Feilong adalah nama diri, dan sering dipakai sebagai gelar bagi gagasan dan benda lain.

short_description.id: Hantu Fisher adalah kisah hantu populer Australia dari awal abad ke-19 yang bermula dari peristiwa nyata di Campbelltown: hantu seorang petani yang dibunuh konon menunjukkan tempat jasadnya terkubur.
short_description.en: Fisher's ghost is a popular Australian ghost story from the early 19th century that grew out of real events in Campbelltown: the ghost of a murdered farmer is said to have pointed out where his body lay.

long_description.id: Legenda hantu Fisher adalah cerita rakyat atau kisah hantu populer Australia dari awal abad ke-19. Kisah ini muncul dari serangkaian peristiwa nyata di Campbelltown, New South Wales, yang kini menjadi pusat permukiman besar di pinggiran barat daya Sydney tetapi saat itu merupakan pos pedesaan terpencil.
long_description.en: The legend of Fisher's ghost is a popular Australian folk tale or ghost story from the early 19th century. It grew out of a series of real events in Campbelltown, New South Wales, now a large urban area on the southwestern edge of Sydney but then a remote rural outpost.

long_description.id: Pada 17 Juni 1826, Frederick Fisher menghilang. Tetangganya George Worrall mengaku Fisher telah pulang ke Inggris dan memberinya kuasa atas hartanya, tetapi Dictionary of Sydney mencatat bahwa alasan itu tidak meyakinkan karena Fisher masih narapidana dan berisiko ditangkap di Inggris. Menurut versi legenda, empat bulan kemudian John Farley berlari ke hotel setempat dan mengatakan telah melihat hantu Fisher duduk di pagar jembatan; hantu itu tidak berbicara dan hanya menunjuk ke sebuah padang di seberang kali.
long_description.en: On 17 June 1826 Frederick Fisher disappeared. His neighbour George Worrall claimed Fisher had gone back to England and given him power of attorney over his property, but the Dictionary of Sydney finds the excuse hard to believe, since Fisher was still a convict who risked being arrested if he turned up in England. In the legend, four months later John Farley ran into the local hotel and said he had seen Fisher's ghost sitting on the rail of a bridge; the ghost did not speak and merely pointed to a paddock beyond the creek.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, polisi menggeledah padang yang ditunjuk hantu itu dan menemukan jasad Fisher terkubur di tepi kali; Worrall ditangkap, mengaku, dan digantung. Catatan sejarah memberi gambaran lain: dua anak laki-laki melaporkan noda darah pada pagar pertanian Fisher, polisi menemukan sehelai rambut dan sebuah gigi, lalu seorang pelacak Aborigin bernama Gilbert menuntun polisi ke makam di tanah Worrall. Catatan polisi dan pengadilan sezaman tidak menyebut kisah hantu itu.
long_description.en: In the legend, police searched the paddock the ghost had pointed to and found Fisher's remains buried by a creek; Worrall was arrested, confessed, and hanged. The historical account differs: two boys reported bloodstains on a fence at Fisher's farm, the police found a lock of hair and a tooth, and an Aboriginal tracker named Gilbert then led them to the grave on Worrall's land. Contemporary police and court records do not mention the ghost story.

long_description.id: Asal-usul kisah ini diperdebatkan. Ada usul bahwa Farley mengarangnya untuk menutupi sumber pengetahuan lain tentang letak jasad Fisher, tetapi hal itu tidak dapat dipastikan; Joe Nickell menulis bahwa kisah itu mungkin berawal dari puisi anonim tahun 1832. Dictionary of Sydney mencatat kisah itu pertama kali tercetak dalam puisi "The Sprite of the Creek" pada Agustus 1832.
long_description.en: The origin of the tale is debated. It has been suggested that Farley invented it to conceal some other source of his knowledge of where the body lay, though this cannot be confirmed; Joe Nickell wrote that it may have begun with an anonymous 1832 poem. According to the Dictionary of Sydney, the tale reached print for the first time in August 1832, in the poem "The Sprite of the Creek".

long_description.id: Desas-desus beredar bahwa penemuan jasad Fisher bukan kebetulan, dan kisah hantunya dicetak ulang sejak awal 1830-an. Kisah ini kemudian masuk ke cerita rakyat populer dan menamai Fisher's Ghost Creek, tempat jasad ditemukan. Festival Fisher's Ghost digelar di Campbelltown, dan sebuah film bisu Australia tahun 1924 menceritakan ulang peristiwa dalam legenda itu.
long_description.en: Rumours spread that the finding of Fisher's body was no accident, and the ghost story has been retold in print since the early 1830s. The tale later entered popular folklore and gave its name to Fisher's Ghost Creek, beside which the body was found. A Festival of Fisher's Ghost is held in Campbelltown, and a 1924 Australian silent film retells the events of the legend.

cultural_context.id: Dictionary of Sydney menyebut "Fisher's Ghost" telah menjadi unsur penting ingatan kolektif Campbelltown, dan kisahnya dipentaskan ulang dalam festival tahunan di sana.
cultural_context.en: The Dictionary of Sydney describes "Fisher's Ghost" as a key part of how Campbelltown remembers its past, with the tale acted out each year at a festival.
