short_description.id: Fjalar adalah kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik yang bersama saudaranya Galar membunuh Kvasir yang bijak dan membuat madu puisi dari darahnya.
short_description.en: Fjalar is a dwarf of Norse mythology who with his brother Galar killed the wise Kvasir and made the mead of poetry from his blood.

long_description.id: Fjalar (Nordik Kuno Fjalarr, dari fela, "menyembunyikan"; "si Penyembunyi") adalah nama seorang kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik. Menurut Edda karya Snorri, ia bersama saudaranya Galar membunuh Kvasir yang bijak dan dari darahnya membuat madu puisi, minuman para skald yang kemudian dicuri raksasa Suttung.
long_description.en: Fjalar (Old Norse Fjalarr, from fela, 'to hide'; 'the Hider') is the name of a dwarf in Norse mythology. According to Snorri's Edda he and his brother Galar killed the wise Kvasir and made from his blood the mead of poetry, the skalds' drink later stolen by the giant Suttung.

long_description.id: Nama Fjalar, yang berarti "penipu" atau "penyembunyi", disandang beberapa tokoh mitologi Nordik, dan kurcaci ini yang terpenting. Völuspá mencantumkannya dalam daftar kurcaci, dan Hávamál menyebut "Fjalar yang Bijak", yang birnya membuat sang penutur, mungkin Odin, mabuk; bila itu merujuk madu puisi, Fjalar tersebut mungkin sama dengan kurcaci pembuat madu ini.
long_description.en: The name Fjalar, meaning 'deceiver' or 'hider', is borne by several figures of Norse mythology, and this dwarf is the most important. The Völuspá lists him among the dwarfs, and the Hávamál speaks of 'Fjalar the Wise', whose ale makes the narrator, probably Odin, drunk; if that refers to the mead of poetry, this Fjalar may be the same as the mead-making dwarf.

long_description.id: Dalam terjemahan Prose Edda yang terbuka, Kvasir datang atas undangan ke tempat kurcaci Fjalar dan Galarr; mereka membunuhnya dan membiarkan darahnya mengalir ke dua bejana besar dan sebuah kuali. Darah itu dicampur madu sehingga menjadi madu yang menjadikan peminumnya skald atau cendekiawan, dan para kurcaci melaporkan bahwa Kvasir tersedak oleh kecerdikannya sendiri. Mereka kemudian menenggelamkan raksasa Gillingr dan membunuh istrinya; Suttungr, putra Gillingr, menempatkan mereka di karang yang tergenang air pasang hingga mereka menawarkan madu itu sebagai tebusan.
long_description.en: In the open translation of the Prose Edda, Kvasir came by invitation to the dwarves Fjalar and Galarr, who killed him and let his blood run into two vats and a kettle. The blood was blended with honey into a mead that makes the drinker a skald or scholar, and the dwarves reported that Kvasir had choked on his own shrewdness. They later drowned the giant Gillingr and killed his wife; Suttungr, Gillingr's son, set them on a reef covered at high tide until they offered the mead as ransom.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah terjemahan puisi, penuturnya mabuk berat ketika bersama Fjalar yang bijak; catatan penerjemah menyebut Fjalar itu tampaknya nama lain untuk Suttung, sedangkan sumber lain menduga ia mungkin kurcaci pembuat madu.
long_description.en: In a translated poem the speaker was dead-drunk when with Fjalar the wise; the translator's note says that Fjalar is apparently another name for Suttung, whereas another source suggests he may be the mead-making dwarf.

claims.quote: Fjalar – imię kilku postaci w mitologii nordyckiej, oznaczające „oszusta” lub „ukrywającego”. ... Kolejną, najważniejszą z postaci o tym imieniu, był karzeł, brat Galara. Razem z bratem zabili Kvasera, a z jego krwi stworzyli miód poezji.

statement.id: Fjalar adalah nama beberapa tokoh mitologi Nordik yang berarti "penipu" atau "penyembunyi"; yang terpenting adalah kurcaci saudara Galar, yang bersama saudaranya membunuh Kvasir dan membuat madu puisi dari darahnya.
statement.en: Fjalar is the name of several Norse mythological figures, meaning 'deceiver' or 'hider' (oszusta, ukrywającego); the most important is the dwarf (karzeł), brother of Galar, who with him killed Kvasir (Kvasera) and made the mead of poetry (miód poezji) from his blood.

claims.quote: Fjalar (gammelnorsk; Fjalarr av fela, «gjemme»; «Gjemmeren») på islansk; Fjalar «vitur» eller «fjölfròdur» som betyr klok. Fjalar er navn i norrøn mytologi på en dverg som ifølge Snorres Edda sammen med sin bror Galar drepte den vise Kvase. Av hans blod laget de skaldskapsmjøden. Skaldedrikken blir senere stjålet av jotnen Suttung.

statement.id: Fjalar (Nordik Kuno Fjalarr, dari fela, "menyembunyikan"; "si Penyembunyi") adalah nama kurcaci dalam mitologi Nordik yang menurut Edda Snorri bersama saudaranya Galar membunuh Kvasir yang bijak; dari darahnya mereka membuat madu puisi, yang kemudian dicuri raksasa Suttung.
statement.en: Fjalar (Old Norse Fjalarr, from fela, 'to hide'; 'the Hider') is a dwarf in Norse mythology who, per Snorri's Edda, with his brother Galar killed the wise Kvasir; from his blood they made the mead of poetry, later stolen by the giant Suttung.

claims.quote: Fjalara wymienia Völuspá w swoim katalogu karłów. Poemat Hávamál mówi o Fjalarze Mądrym, którego piwem upija się narrator (prawdopodobnie Odyn). Może to być odniesienie do miodu poezji, i w takim wypadku ten Fjalar byłby tożsamy z karłem, wytwórcą miodu.

statement.id: Völuspá mencantumkan Fjalar dalam daftar kurcacinya; Hávamál menyebut Fjalar yang Bijak, yang birnya membuat sang penutur (mungkin Odin) mabuk, yang mungkin merujuk madu puisi, sehingga Fjalar itu bisa jadi sama dengan kurcaci pembuat madu.
statement.en: The Völuspá lists Fjalar in its catalogue of dwarfs; the Hávamál speaks of Fjalar the Wise, whose ale gets the narrator (probably Odin) drunk, perhaps referring to the mead of poetry, in which case this Fjalar would be the mead-making dwarf.

claims.quote: This man is called Kvasir, and he was so wise that none could question him concerning anything but that he knew the solution. He went up and down the earth to give instruction to men; and when he came upon invitation to the abode of certain dwarves, Fjalar and Galarr, they called him into privy converse with them, and killed him, letting his blood run into two vats and a kettle.

statement.id: Dalam terjemahan Prose Edda ini, Kvasir sangat bijak sehingga tak ada yang bisa menanyainya hal yang jawabannya tak ia ketahui; ketika ia datang atas undangan ke tempat kurcaci Fjalar dan Galarr, mereka memanggilnya untuk berbicara empat mata, membunuhnya, dan membiarkan darahnya mengalir ke dua bejana besar dan sebuah kuali.
statement.en: In this translation of the Prose Edda, Kvasir was so wise that none could question him on anything he could not answer; when he came by invitation to the abode of the dwarves Fjalar and Galarr, they called him into private talk, killed him, and let his blood run into two vats and a kettle.

claims.quote: The kettle is named Ódrerir, and the vats Són and Bodn; they blended honey with the blood, and the outcome was that mead by the virtue of which he who drinks becomes a skald or scholar.

statement.id: Kuali itu bernama Ódrerir dan bejananya Són dan Bodn; mereka mencampur madu dengan darah itu sehingga jadilah madu yang membuat peminumnya menjadi skald atau cendekiawan.
statement.en: The kettle is named Ódrerir and the vats Són and Bodn; they blended honey with the blood, producing a mead that makes whoever drinks it a skald or scholar.

claims.quote: The dwarves reported to the Æsir that Kvasir had choked on his own shrewdness, since there was none so wise there as to be able to question his wisdom.

statement.id: Para kurcaci melaporkan kepada bangsa Æsir bahwa Kvasir tersedak oleh kecerdikannya sendiri, sebab tak ada yang cukup bijak untuk menanyai hikmatnya.
statement.en: The dwarves reported to the Æsir that Kvasir had choked on his own shrewdness, since no one there was wise enough to question his wisdom.

claims.quote: Then these dwarves invited the giant who is called Gillingr to visit them, and his wife with him. Next the dwarves invited Gillingr to row upon the sea with them; but when they had gone out from the land, the dwarves rowed into the breakers and capsized the boat. Gillingr was unable to swim, and he perished

statement.id: Para kurcaci itu kemudian mengundang raksasa Gillingr dan istrinya, mengajak Gillingr berperahu di laut, lalu mendayung ke arah ombak pecah dan membalikkan perahu; Gillingr tak bisa berenang dan tewas.
statement.en: The dwarves then invited the giant Gillingr and his wife, took Gillingr rowing at sea, rowed into the breakers and capsized the boat; Gillingr could not swim and perished.

claims.quote: They reported this accident to his wife, but she took it grievously and wept aloud. Then Fjalar asked her ... Then he spoke softly to Galarr his brother, bidding him go up over the doorway, when she should go out, and let a mill-stone fall on her head, saying that her weeping grew wearisome to him; and even so he did.

statement.id: Setelah kecelakaan itu dilaporkan kepada istri korban, yang menangis keras, Fjalar menanyainya lalu berbisik kepada saudaranya Galarr agar naik ke atas pintu dan menjatuhkan batu kilangan ke kepala perempuan itu karena tangisnya melelahkan, dan Galarr melakukannya.
statement.en: After the accident was reported to the dead man's wife, who wept aloud, Fjalar questioned her and then softly told his brother Galarr to go over the doorway and let a mill-stone fall on her head because her weeping wearied him; and Galarr did so.

claims.quote: Now when the giant Suttungr, Gillingr's son, learned of this, he went over and took the dwarves and carried them out to sea, and set them on a reef which was covered at high tide. They besought Suttungr to grant them respite of their lives, and as the price of reconciliation offered him the precious mead in satisfaction of his father's death.

statement.id: Ketika raksasa Suttungr, putra Gillingr, mengetahui hal itu, ia membawa para kurcaci ke laut dan menempatkan mereka di karang yang tertutup air pasang; mereka memohon agar nyawa mereka diampuni dan sebagai tebusan menawarkan madu berharga itu atas kematian ayahnya.
statement.en: When the giant Suttungr, Gillingr's son, learned of this, he carried the dwarves out to sea and set them on a reef covered at high tide; they begged for their lives and offered him the precious mead as the price of reconciliation for his father's death.

short_description.id: Galloway Puma adalah "kucing hantu" dalam folklor Skotlandia yang konon hidup di Dumfries and Galloway, Skotlandia barat daya.
short_description.en: The Galloway Puma is a 'phantom cat' of Scottish folklore said to live in Dumfries and Galloway, south-west Scotland.

long_description.id: Dalam folklor Skotlandia, Galloway Puma adalah "kucing hantu" yang konon tinggal di Dumfries and Galloway, Skotlandia barat daya. Desas-desus tentang kucing besar di Galloway bermula pada akhir 1990-an, ketika wisatawan Kanada mengaku melihat hewan mirip cougar dekat Kirroughtree, tenggara Newton Stewart, sepulang berjalan di Hutan Galloway. Warga Newton Stewart juga mengaku melihatnya pada 1999.
long_description.en: Scottish folklore places a 'phantom cat', the Galloway Puma, in the Dumfries and Galloway region of south-west Scotland. Talk of a big cat in Galloway started in the late 1990s, when Canadian tourists said they had seen a cougar-like animal near Kirroughtree, south-east of Newton Stewart, on the way back from a walk in Galloway Forest. Locals in Newton Stewart reported it too in 1999.

long_description.id: Setelah itu banyak orang, terutama petani dan pekerja Forestry Commission, mengaku melihat kucing hitam besar di wilayah itu, terutama di daerah Machars. Pada Juni 2001, seorang perempuan yang mengajak anjingnya berjalan dekat lapangan golf Newton Stewart dikejutkan "kucing hitam besar, lebih besar dari anjing alsatian" yang melompat ke arahnya lalu lari ketika anjingnya menggonggong. Artikel zh mencatat penampakan lain pada Desember 2012 oleh Alan Dalton dan istrinya.
long_description.en: Since then many people, especially farmers and Forestry Commission staff, have claimed sightings of a big black cat across the region, mostly in the Machars. In June 2001 a woman walking her dog near Newton Stewart golf course was startled by a 'large black cat, bigger than an alsatian' that sprang out at her and fled when her dog barked. The zh article records another sighting in December 2012 by Alan Dalton and his wife.

long_description.id: The Galloway Gazette pada 2013 melaporkan wisatawan di Kirroughtee Hotel, di luar Newton Stewart, berjumpa dekat dengan kucing besar yang sukar ditangkap. Surat kabar itu juga menyebut dalam empat tahun terakhir ada 20 laporan penampakan kucing besar yang masuk kepadanya.

short_description.id: Greif (griffin Mesir) adalah makhluk fabel dalam mitologi Mesir kuno yang sudah menjadi bagian gambar pada Palet Dua Anjing masa pradinasti dan berfungsi menangkal kejahatan.
short_description.en: The Greif (Egyptian griffin) is a fabulous creature of ancient Egyptian mythology that was already part of the imagery of the predynastic Two Dog Palette and served to ward off evil.

long_description.id: Greif (bahasa Mesir kuno Sefer, Sefre, juga Achech) adalah sebutan makhluk fabel dalam mitologi Mesir kuno. Makhluk ini sudah menjadi bagian tetap program gambar pada Palet Dua Anjing masa pradinasti. Menurut Ashmolean Museum, pada sisi belakang palet itu terdapat griffin bersayap seperti jengger di antara hewan-hewan fantastis dan nyata.
long_description.en: The Greif (ancient Egyptian Sefer, Sefre, also Achech) is the name of a fabulous creature in ancient Egyptian mythology. It was already a fixed part of the imagery of the predynastic Two Dog Palette. According to the Ashmolean Museum, the reverse of that palette shows a griffin with comb-like wings among fabulous and real animals.

long_description.id: Griffin awal dinasti memiliki ciri pemangsa seperti burung bangkai dengan sayap berbentuk jengger. Pada Kerajaan Tengah berkembang bentuk serupa dengan kepala pipih, bulu mirip macan kumbang, kepala manusia di antara sayap, dan kalung; kemudian ia mendapat kepala elang seperti Horus. Sifatnya antara lain menangkal setan dan perbuatan jahat, dan sejak Periode Akhir ia terutama berfungsi melindungi.
long_description.en: The early dynastic griffin had predatory, vulture-like features with comb-like wings. In the Middle Kingdom a similar form developed with a flat head, panther-like fur, a human head between the wings and a collar; later it received a falcon head like Horus. Its nature was, among other things, to avert demons and evil acts, and from the Late Period it served especially a protective function.

long_description.id: Pada Dinasti ke-18, tipe ikonografi baru dengan pengaruh dari luar Mesir masuk ke mitologi Mesir kuno. Pada periode Ptolemeus griffin muncul sebagai makhluk campuran bersayap yang berpadu dengan Mata Matahari, dan fabel demotik menggambarkannya dengan paruh elang, mata manusia, anggota badan singa, telinga ikan, dan ekor ular. Ia juga dikenal sejak dini sebagai hewan pemburu mitologis di gurun, atau sebagai Mata Matahari pelindung yang diutus dewa matahari Re sebagai pembalasan.
long_description.en: In the 18th Dynasty a new iconographic type with influences from outside Egypt entered ancient Egyptian mythology. In the Ptolemaic period the griffin appears as a winged hybrid combined with the sun eye, and a demotic fable describes it with a falcon's beak, human eyes, lion limbs, fish ears and a snake's tail. It is also attested very early as a mythological hunting animal active in the desert, or as a protective sun eye sent by the sun god Re as retribution.

short_description.id: Grootslang adalah ular raksasa legendaris yang konon tinggal di gua dalam di Richtersveld, Afrika Selatan, menjaga timbunan berlian, dan sangat ditakuti penduduk setempat.
short_description.en: The Grootslang is a legendary giant serpent said to live in a deep cave in the Richtersveld, South Africa, guarding a hoard of diamonds and greatly feared by local people.

long_description.id: Grootslang adalah makhluk legendaris berupa ular raksasa yang konon tinggal di gua dalam di Richtersveld, Afrika Selatan. Kepercayaan padanya digambarkan tersebar luas di kalangan orang Khoekhoe setempat, dan dalam pandangan mereka hanya ada satu Ular Besar yang sangat ditakuti. Penduduk enggan memandu ekspedisi ke guanya, yang konon penuh berlian dan terhubung dengan laut sejauh empat puluh mil.
long_description.en: The Grootslang is a legendary giant snake believed to live in a deep cave in the Richtersveld, South Africa. Belief in it is described as widespread among the local Khoekhoe, for whom there is only one greatly feared Great Snake. People there hesitate to lead expeditions to its cave, which is said to hold diamonds and to reach the sea forty miles away.

long_description.id: Para saksi menyebut ular itu sepanjang empat puluh kaki dan meninggalkan jejak selebar sekitar tiga kaki di tepi sungai berlumpur. Ia dipercaya menyambar ternak dari tepi sungai, dan versi lain menyebut ia memancing gajah ke guanya lalu melahapnya. Selain gua, kolam berpusar di bawah King George Cataract di Air Terjun Aughrabies juga dianggap tempat tinggalnya dan sumber berlian.
long_description.en: Witnesses put the snake at forty feet long, with a track about three feet wide left on muddy riverbanks. It is thought to snatch cattle from the riverside, and another version says it lures elephants into its cave and eats them. Apart from the cave, a whirling pool beneath King George Cataract, at the Aughrabies Falls, is also named as its lair and a source of diamonds.

long_description.id: Seorang pencari tambang yang berkemah di tepi sungai diberi tahu pemandunya bahwa ular raksasa itu tinggal di batu besar di tengah sungai. Ia mencatat banyak orang mengaku melihat ular itu atau jejaknya, tetapi ketika ia meledakkan dinamit di dekat batu tersebut, yang muncul hanya beberapa ikan kecil. Menurut satu versi yang dilaporkan Jon Manchip White dari cerita orang Bushmen, Grootslang lebih tua daripada dunia dan akan menjaga hartanya selamanya.
long_description.en: A prospector camped by the river was told by his guide that the giant snake lived in a large rock in midstream. He noted that many people claimed to have seen the snake or its trail, yet when he set off dynamite near the rock only a few small fish turned up. A version reported by Jon Manchip White as told by the Bushmen holds that the Grootslang is older than the world and will guard its treasure forever.

long_description.id: Seorang penulis menepis cerita tentang berlian di rongga mata ular itu dan pengaruh jahat yang dirasakan orang yang melihatnya, lalu menduga yang terlihat sebenarnya piton yang luar biasa besar. Pada 1917 pengusaha Peter Grayson hilang saat mencari harta di Richtersveld setelah rombongannya diserang singa, dan muncul desas-desus bahwa Grootslang membunuhnya. Dalam media abad ke-21, Grootslang sering diberi ciri gajah, yang berasal dari deskripsi Carol Rose bahwa ia sebesar gajah.
long_description.en: One writer dismissed tales of diamonds in the snake's eye-sockets and of an evil influence felt by those who see it, suggesting that unusually large pythons were what people actually saw. In 1917 the businessman Peter Grayson vanished while seeking treasure in the Richtersveld after lions attacked his party, and rumour blamed the Grootslang. Media of the 21st century often give it elephant traits, a habit traced to Carol Rose describing it as elephant-sized.

short_description.id: Gulyabani adalah roh jahat pengubah wujud dalam kepercayaan orang Azerbaijan, Turki, Kirgiz, dan Tajik, yang tinggal di stepa atau pemakaman dan menakuti pengembara malam.
short_description.en: The gulyabani is a shapeshifting evil spirit in the beliefs of Azerbaijanis, Turks, Kyrgyz and Tajiks, living in steppes or cemeteries and frightening night travellers.

long_description.id: Gulyabani adalah makhluk pengubah wujud, roh jahat rendahan dalam kepercayaan orang Azerbaijan, Turki, Kirgiz, dan Tajik. Namanya berasal dari kata Arab ghul ("monster-demon") dan kata Persia yaban ("padang gurun"). Dalam mitologi Azerbaijan ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk liar yang buas dan berbulu; padanannya, Quyux, muncul dalam gelap di padang dan pemakaman, berbulu kuning kemerahan, berbau busuk, dan sangat besar. Menurut mitos Turki, gulyabani adalah ghoul raksasa berjenggot panjang yang berkeliaran pada malam hari.
long_description.en: The gulyabani is a shapeshifter, a lesser evil spirit in the beliefs of the Azerbaijanis, Turks, Kyrgyz and Tajiks. Its name comes from Arabic ghul ("monster-demon") and Persian yaban ("desert"). In Azerbaijani mythology it is a wild, predatory, hairy being; its counterpart Quyux appears in the dark in steppes and cemeteries, covered in yellowish-red hair, foul-smelling and very large. In Turkish myth the gulyabani is pictured as an enormous bearded ghoul that roams after dark.

long_description.id: Menurut orang Azerbaijan dan Turki, gulyabani tinggal di stepa, pemakaman, reruntuhan, atau bekas medan perang, dan suka menakut-nakuti pengembara malam. Pada malam hari ia menunggang kuda dan mengusutkan surainya. Bila ditangkap dan jarum ditancapkan di kerah pakaiannya, ia akan bekerja seperti budak, tetapi semua perintah dikerjakannya terbalik. Di Azerbaijan bagian barat ia sering disamakan dengan roh air yang merugikan.
long_description.en: According to Azerbaijanis and Turks, the gulyabani lives in steppes, cemeteries, ruins or old battlefields and likes to frighten night travellers. At night it rides horses and tangles their manes. If caught and a needle stuck in the collar of its clothes, it will work like a slave, but carries out every order backwards. In western Azerbaijan it was often identified with a harmful water spirit.

long_description.id: Di kalangan orang Kirgiz Pamir Timur dan Tajik, gulyabani (gulbiyaban) digambarkan sebagai makhluk besar mirip manusia, berbulu abu-abu atau hitam, berbau tak sedap, dan berkaki terbalik ke belakang, yang tinggal di tempat sunyi dan menghindari manusia. Dalam kisah-kisah yang dicatat etnograf Rozenfeld, ia menantang orang kuat bergulat; bila kalah, ia melarikan diri dan tak muncul lagi di hadapan lawannya. Artikel ru menyebut citranya berasal dari ghul tradisi Muslim dan bahwa rakyat juga menyebutnya jin.
long_description.en: Among the Kyrgyz of the Eastern Pamir and the Tajiks, the gulyabani (gulbiyaban) is described as a large humanlike being with grey or black hair, a foul smell and backward-turned feet, living in deserted places and avoiding people. In tales recorded by the ethnographer Rozenfeld, it challenges strong men to wrestle; if beaten, it runs away and never appears to its opponent again. The ru article says its image goes back to the Muslim ghul and that people also called it a jinn.

claims.quote: (азерб. Qulyabani — «оборотень», с араб. гул — «чудовище-демон», с перс. ябан — «пустыня») — оборотень, низший злой дух в представлении азербайджанцев (гул-ябаны, гули-ябаны, биабан-гули), турок, киргизов (гульбиябан), таджиков (гул, гул-ёвони).

statement.id: Gulyabani (bahasa Azerbaijan Qulyabani, "manusia jadi-jadian"; dari bahasa Arab ghul, "monster-demon", dan bahasa Persia yaban, "padang gurun") adalah makhluk pengubah wujud, roh jahat rendahan dalam kepercayaan orang Azerbaijan, Turki, Kirgiz, dan Tajik.
statement.en: Gulyabani (Azerbaijani Qulyabani, "werewolf"; from Arabic ghul, "monster-demon", and Persian yaban, "desert") is a shapeshifter, a lesser evil spirit in the beliefs of the Azerbaijanis, Turks, Kyrgyz and Tajiks.

claims.quote: По представлениям азербайджанцев и турок, гульябани был злым духом, жившим в степи или на кладбище. Его также можно было встретить в подземельях, руинах, на местах битв и побоищ. Излюбленным его занятием было пугать припозднившихся ночных путников, странников из караванов.

statement.id: Menurut orang Azerbaijan dan Turki, gulyabani adalah roh jahat yang tinggal di stepa atau pemakaman, juga bisa ditemui di ruang bawah tanah, reruntuhan, dan bekas medan perang; kegemarannya menakut-nakuti pengembara malam yang terlambat dan anggota kafilah.
statement.en: According to Azerbaijanis and Turks, the gulyabani was an evil spirit living in the steppe or a cemetery, also met in underground places, ruins and old battlefields; its favourite pastime was frightening belated night travellers and caravan wanderers.

claims.quote: Согласно поверьям азербайджанцев, гульябани имел черты оборотня, который по ночам любил ездить на лошади, запутывать ей гриву. По поверью если его поймать и воткнуть в ворот его одежды иголку, он, подобно рабу («гул» в переводе с азербайджанского означает «раб»), станет работать на человека. Но все приказы хозяина он будет выполнять наоборот.

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan Azerbaijan, gulyabani bersifat seperti manusia jadi-jadian yang pada malam hari suka menunggang kuda dan mengusutkan surainya; bila ditangkap dan jarum ditancapkan di kerah pakaiannya, ia akan bekerja seperti budak ("gul" dalam bahasa Azerbaijan berarti "budak"), tetapi semua perintah tuannya akan ia kerjakan terbalik.
statement.en: In Azerbaijani belief the gulyabani had werewolf traits, liking to ride horses at night and tangle their manes; if caught and a needle stuck in the collar of its clothes, it would work like a slave ("gul" in Azerbaijani means "slave"), but would carry out all its master's orders backwards.

claims.quote: Quyux, vəhşi varlıq deməkdir. Ən məşhur təsvirə görə, qaranlıqda çöllərdə və qəbiristanlıqlarda ortaya çıxır. Bədəni sarı qırmızı tüklə örtülü, pis qoxuludur. Çox iridir.

statement.id: Menurut artikel Azerbaijan, padanannya Quyux berarti makhluk liar; menurut gambaran paling terkenal ia muncul dalam gelap di padang dan pemakaman, tubuhnya tertutup bulu kuning kemerahan, berbau busuk, dan sangat besar.
statement.en: According to the Azerbaijani article, its counterpart Quyux means a wild being; in the best-known description it appears in the dark in the steppes and cemeteries, its body covered in yellowish-red hair, foul-smelling and very large.

claims.quote: Qulyabanı (fars. غول یابانی‎ və ya غول بیابانی ğoul-e yabani və ya ğoul-e biyabani – "vəhşi nəhəng və ya düzənlik nəhəngi”) — Azərbaycan mifologiyasında vəhşi heyvan, fövqəladə, yırtıcı canlı, tüklü varlıq.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Azerbaijan, Qulyabanı (dari bahasa Persia ghoul-e yabani atau ghoul-e biyabani, "raksasa liar" atau "raksasa padang") adalah binatang liar, makhluk luar biasa yang buas dan berbulu.
statement.en: In Azerbaijani mythology Qulyabanı (from Persian ghoul-e yabani or ghoul-e biyabani, "wild giant" or "giant of the plains") is a wild beast, an extraordinary, predatory, hairy being.

claims.quote: гульбиябан (гульбияван, гуль) —■чело­ векоподобное сущ ество крупных размеров, покрытое желтовато-серог шерстью, напоминающей верблюж

statement.id: Menurut para penutur kisah di Pamir Timur yang dicatat Rozenfeld, gulbiyabon (gulbiyaban, gul) adalah makhluk berwujud manusia berukuran besar, berbulu kuning keabu-abuan seperti bulu unta.
statement.en: According to storytellers of the Eastern Pamir recorded by Rozenfeld, the gulbiyaban (gulbiyavan, gul) is a large humanlike being covered in yellowish-grey hair resembling camel hair.

claims.quote: От гульбиябана исходит резкий, нестерпи­ мый запах, который ощущ ается на значительном расстоянии. Иногда в рассказах о гульбиябане присутствует мотив о том, что у него выворочень ступни: пятка находится спереди, а пальцы — сзади.

statement.id: Dari gulbiyaban menyebar bau menyengat yang tak tertahankan hingga jauh; dalam beberapa kisah telapak kakinya terbalik, dengan tumit di depan dan jari di belakang.
statement.en: A sharp, unbearable smell comes from the gulbiyaban and is perceptible at a considerable distance; in some tales its feet are turned backwards, heel in front and toes behind.

claims.quote: Обитает он якобы в пустынных местах, избегает людей и издает особый характерный крик.

statement.id: Gulbiyaban konon tinggal di tempat-tempat sunyi dan gersang, menghindari manusia, dan mengeluarkan teriakan khas.
statement.en: The gulbiyaban is said to dwell in deserted, barren places, avoids people and utters a characteristic cry.

claims.quote: Гульбиябан, встретившись с палваном, предлагает ему бороться. При этом гульбиябан сначала просит у палвана жевательного табака — нас, который носят в табакерке за поясом; это он якобы делает для того, чтобы проверить, нет ли у палвана ножа. Если побеж дает палзаи, то гульбиябан убегает и больше никогда уж е не попадается ему на глаза.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Pamir Timur, gulbiyaban menantang pahlawan (palvan) bergulat dan lebih dulu meminta tembakau kunyah untuk memeriksa apakah ia membawa pisau; bila palvan menang, gulbiyaban melarikan diri dan tak pernah muncul lagi.
statement.en: In the Eastern Pamir tales, the gulbiyaban challenges a hero (palvan) to wrestle and first asks for chewing tobacco to check whether he carries a knife; if the palvan wins, the gulbiyaban runs away and never appears to him again.

claims.quote: According to Turkish myth, Gulyabani is a humongous ghoul with a long beard who wanders at night and scares people.

statement.id: Menurut mitos Turki, Gulyabani adalah ghoul raksasa berjenggot panjang yang berkeliaran pada malam hari dan menakut-nakuti orang.
statement.en: According to Turkish myth, Gulyabani is a humongous ghoul with a long beard who wanders at night and scares people.

claims.quote: Gulyabani is a 2014 Turkish horror-comedy film directed by Orçun Benli.

statement.id: Gulyabani adalah film horor-komedi Turki tahun 2014 yang disutradarai Orçun Benli.
statement.en: Gulyabani is a 2014 Turkish horror-comedy film directed by Orçun Benli.

claims.quote: У киргизов Восточного Памира и таджиков гульябани обитал в пустынных местах (в горных лесах). Был похожим на человека, покрытым серой (или чёрной) шерстью, крупного размера, с неприятным запахом и имеющим вывернутые назад ступни.

statement.id: Menurut orang Kirgiz Pamir Timur dan Tajik, gulyabani tinggal di tempat sunyi (hutan pegunungan), mirip manusia, besar, berbulu abu-abu atau hitam, berbau tak sedap, dan berkaki terbalik ke belakang.
statement.en: According to the Kyrgyz of the Eastern Pamir and the Tajiks, the gulyabani lived in deserted places (mountain forests), resembled a human, was large, covered in grey or black hair, foul-smelling, with feet turned backwards.

claims.quote: В западных районах Азербайджана гульябани часто отождествляли с вредоносным духом воды.

statement.id: Di wilayah barat Azerbaijan, gulyabani sering disamakan dengan roh air yang merugikan.
statement.en: In the western districts of Azerbaijan, the gulyabani was often identified with a harmful water spirit.

claims.quote: Образ гюль-ябани восходит к мусульманскому гуль. В народе его называли также и джинном (злой дух)

statement.id: Menurut artikel ru, citra gyul-yabani berasal dari ghul dalam tradisi Muslim, dan di kalangan rakyat ia juga disebut jin (roh jahat).
statement.en: According to the ru article, the image of gyul-yabani goes back to the Muslim ghul, and among the people it was also called a jinn (evil spirit).

summary.id: Orang Azerbaijan dan Turki: roh jahat/pengubah wujud di stepa dan pemakaman; di Azerbaijan barat sering disamakan dengan roh air; mitos Turki: ghoul raksasa berjenggot panjang.
summary.en: Azerbaijanis and Turks: an evil, shapeshifting spirit of steppes and cemeteries; in western Azerbaijan often identified with a water spirit; Turkish myth: a humongous long-bearded ghoul.

summary.id: Orang Kirgiz Pamir Timur dan Tajik: makhluk besar mirip manusia, berbulu abu-abu atau hitam, berkaki terbalik, yang menantang orang bergulat.
summary.en: Kyrgyz of the Eastern Pamir and Tajiks: a large humanlike being with grey or black hair and backward feet that challenges people to wrestle.

short_description.id: Hırtık adalah jin jahat dalam kepercayaan rakyat yang dipercaya tinggal di sungai, berbadan atas manusia dan berbadan bawah hewan, serta menyamar sebagai orang yang dikenal untuk memancing korbannya ke air.
short_description.en: Hırtık is a malevolent jinn of folk belief said to live in rivers, human above and animal below, which takes the guise of familiar people to lure its victims to the water.

long_description.id: Hırtık digambarkan sebagai jin atau makhluk jahat yang bagian atas tubuhnya seperti manusia dan bagian bawahnya seperti hewan. Badannya penuh bulu dan kakinya menghadap ke belakang. Ia dianggap tinggal di sungai, terutama di Sungai Fırat di daerah Elazığ, tempat ia juga disebut Çay hırtığı; nama lainnya adalah Kırtık dan Hırtıh.
long_description.en: Hırtık is described as a malevolent jinn or creature whose upper body is like a human's and whose lower body is like an animal's. Its body is covered in hair and its feet face backwards. It is held to live in rivers, above all the Fırat River in the Elazığ area, where it is also called Çay hırtığı; other names are Kırtık and Hırtıh.

long_description.id: Ia meniru rupa seseorang, lalu mendatangi sahabat atau kerabat orang itu, mengajak mereka bercakap, dan membawa mereka ke hutan atau tepi sungai untuk ditenggelamkan. Sumber kedua menambahkan bahwa ia memakan orang yang telah dicekiknya. Hırtık terutama muncul dalam gelap, dan satu-satunya perlindungan adalah api: orang yang curiga melewatkan api di sekitar tubuh atau di bawah kakinya. Karena sifatnya suka meniru, hırtık mengulangi gerakan itu, bulunya terbakar, dan ia lari menceburkan diri ke air.
long_description.en: It copies someone's appearance, then visits that person's friends or relatives, talks with them and leads them to a forest or riverbank to drown them. The second source adds that it eats the people it has strangled. Hırtık appears mostly in the dark, and the only protection is fire: a suspicious person passes fire around their body or under their feet. Being an imitator, the hırtık repeats the gesture, its hair catches fire, and it flees into the water.

long_description.id: Hırtık juga dipercaya menunggang kuda orang pada malam hari sambil menyamar, sehingga kuda-kuda ditemukan lelah dan berkeringat pada pagi hari. Untuk memeriksanya, pemilik kuda mengoleskan bahan perekat pada pelana atau punggung kuda; bulu hırtık akan menempel dan tercabut ketika ia turun, sehingga ia kesakitan dan tidak menunggang kuda itu lagi.
long_description.en: Hırtık is also believed to ride people's horses in disguise, so that the horses are found tired and sweaty in the morning. To check, owners smear a sticky substance on the saddle or back; the hırtık's hair sticks and is torn out when it dismounts, hurting it so that it leaves the animal alone.

cultural_context.id: Peneliti folklor memasukkan Hırtik ke dalam daftar makhluk demonik yang muncul dalam memorat, yaitu kisah pengalaman yang dipercaya benar-benar terjadi.
cultural_context.en: Folklorists list Hırtik among the demonic beings that appear in memorates, accounts of experiences believed to have really happened.

who.id: Jin jahat yang separuh manusia dan separuh hewan, berbulu dan berkaki terbalik.
who.en: A malevolent jinn, half human and half animal, hairy and backward-footed.

origin.id: Kepercayaan rakyat di sekitar sungai, terutama Sungai Fırat di daerah Elazığ.
origin.en: Folk belief along rivers, especially the Fırat River in the Elazığ area.

role.id: Ia menyamar sebagai orang yang dikenal untuk memancing korban ke hutan atau tepi sungai dan menenggelamkan mereka.
role.en: It disguises itself as someone familiar to lure victims to a forest or riverbank and drown them.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal karena sifatnya yang suka meniru, yang membuatnya terbakar ketika mengulangi gerakan api.
famous_for.en: It is known for its imitative nature, which makes it burn itself when it repeats the fire gesture.

did_you_know.id: Pemilik kuda mengoleskan perekat pada pelana untuk mengetahui apakah hırtık telah menunggangi kuda mereka pada malam hari.
did_you_know.en: Horse owners smeared glue on saddles to find out whether a hırtık had been riding their horses.

description.id: Mengambil rupa orang tertentu untuk mendekati sahabat atau kerabatnya.
description.en: Takes the form of a particular person to approach that person's friends or relatives.

description.id: Api adalah satu-satunya perlindungan; ketika meniru gerakan api, bulunya terbakar dan ia lari ke air.
description.en: Fire is the only protection; when it imitates the fire gesture its hair burns and it flees into the water.

description.id: Perekat pada pelana membuat bulunya menempel dan tercabut.
description.en: Glue on the saddle makes its hair stick and tear out.

description.id: Sungai tempat hırtık terutama dipercaya tinggal.
description.en: The river where the hırtık is chiefly believed to live.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa makhluk penyamar dalam cerita rakyat sering dikalahkan oleh sifat menirunya sendiri?
learning_questions.en: Why are disguising creatures in folklore often undone by their own habit of imitation?

claims.quote: Hırtık; üst kısmının insan, alt kısmının hayvan şeklinde olduğuna inanılan, bedeni tüylerle kaplı, ayakları ters kötücül cin, yaratık.

statement.id: Hırtık adalah jin atau makhluk jahat (kötücül cin) yang dipercaya bertubuh atas manusia dan bertubuh bawah hewan, badannya berbulu, dan kakinya terbalik (ayakları ters).
statement.en: Hırtık is a malevolent jinn or creature (kötücül cin) believed to be human above and animal below, with a hair-covered body and backward feet (ayakları ters).

claims.quote: Akarsularda (Elazığ yöresinde özellikle Fırat Nehri'nde) yaşadığı kabul edilir. Bu yörelerde adına Çay hırtığı da denilmektedir.

statement.id: Ia dianggap tinggal di sungai (akarsularda), terutama di Sungai Fırat (Efrat) di daerah Elazığ, dan di sana disebut juga Çay hırtığı.
statement.en: It is held to live in running waters (akarsularda), especially the Fırat (Euphrates) River in the Elazığ area, where it is also called Çay hırtığı.

claims.quote: Hırtık insan kılığına girip, kılığına girdiği kişinin yakın arkadaşlarına veya akrabalarına gidip, onlarla konuşarak orman ya da akarsu kıyısına götürüp boğmakta, öldürmektedir.

statement.id: Hırtık menyamar sebagai manusia (insan kılığına), mendatangi sahabat atau kerabat orang yang ditirunya, mengajak mereka bicara, membawa mereka ke hutan atau tepi sungai, lalu menenggelamkan dan membunuh mereka.
statement.en: Hırtık takes on a human guise (insan kılığına), goes to the close friends or relatives of the person it imitates, talks with them, leads them to a forest or riverbank, and drowns and kills them.

claims.quote: Özellikle karanlıkta ortaya çıkan hırtıktan korunmanın tek yolu ateş yakmaktır. Konuştukları kişinin hırtık olduğundan şüphelenen kişiler, vücutlarının çevresinden veya ayaklarının altından ateş geçirirler.

statement.id: Hırtık terutama muncul dalam gelap (karanlıkta), dan satu-satunya cara melindungi diri adalah menyalakan api (ateş); orang yang curiga lawan bicaranya hırtık melewatkan api di sekitar tubuh atau di bawah kaki mereka.
statement.en: Hırtık appears especially in the dark (karanlıkta), and the only protection is to light a fire (ateş); people who suspect the person they are talking to is a hırtık pass fire around their bodies or under their feet.

claims.quote: Yine hırtığın zaman zaman çeşitli kişilerin kılığında, ata binip gezdiğine ve atları yorduğuna inanılmaktadır.

statement.id: Dipercaya pula bahwa hırtık kadang menyamar sebagai berbagai orang, menunggang kuda (ata binip), dan membuat kuda-kuda kelelahan.
statement.en: It is also believed that the hırtık at times, in the guise of various people, rides horses about (ata binip) and tires them out.

claims.quote: Atlarını sabah yorgun ve terli bir şekilde bulan kişiler hayvanlarını hırtıkın götürüp götürmediğini anlamak için atların semerlerine veya sırtına yapıştırıcı maddeler sürmektedir.

statement.id: Orang yang menemukan kudanya lelah dan berkeringat pada pagi hari mengoleskan bahan perekat (yapıştırıcı maddeler) pada pelana atau punggung kuda untuk mengetahui apakah hırtık telah membawanya.
statement.en: People who find their horses tired and sweaty in the morning smear sticky substances (yapıştırıcı maddeler) on the saddles or backs to find out whether a hırtık has taken them.

claims.quote: Eşdeğer: KIRTIK. HIRTIH Yakaladığı insanları boğarak öldüren sonra da yiyen bir canavar olarak tanımlanır.

statement.id: Nama padanannya Kırtık dan Hırtıh; ia digambarkan sebagai monster (canavar) yang membunuh orang yang ditangkapnya dengan mencekik, lalu memakannya.
statement.en: Equivalent names are Kırtık and Hırtıh; it is described as a monster (canavar) that kills those it catches by strangling and then eats them.

claims.quote: Üst kısmının insan görünümlü, ayaklarıyla bacaklarının ise hayvan biçimli olduğuna inanılır. Bedeni tüylerle kaplı, ayakları terstir.

statement.id: Bagian atasnya dipercaya tampak seperti manusia, sedangkan kaki dan tungkainya berbentuk hewan; badannya berbulu (tüylerle kaplı) dan kakinya terbalik.
statement.en: Its upper part is believed to look human while its feet and legs are animal-shaped; its body is covered with hair (tüylerle kaplı) and its feet point backwards.

claims.quote: Öykünmeci (taklitçi) bir varlık olan Hırtık bu davranışı yineleyince tüyleri yanmaya başlar ve kaçarak kendisini suların içine atar.

statement.id: Karena Hırtık adalah makhluk peniru (öykünmeci, taklitçi), ketika ia mengulangi gerakan api itu bulunya mulai terbakar, dan ia lari lalu menceburkan diri ke air.
statement.en: Because Hırtık is an imitative being (öykünmeci, taklitçi), when it repeats the fire gesture its hair starts to burn, and it flees and throws itself into the water.

claims.quote: Böylece bu hayvana binen Hırtığın tüyleri oraya yapışır ve inerken bu tüyler kopacağı için canı yanar.

statement.id: Dengan begitu bulu Hırtık yang menunggang kuda itu menempel, dan saat turun bulunya tercabut sehingga ia kesakitan (canı yanar).
statement.en: In this way the hair of the Hırtık riding the animal sticks there, and when it dismounts the hair is torn out and it is hurt (canı yanar).

claims.quote: Memoratların Tematik Özellikleri kısmında yaptığı tasnif denemesi içerisinde şu demonik varlıklara yer vermiştir: Cinler, Ağırlık Basması-Karabasan, Congoloz, Erkebit, Hırtik

statement.id: Dalam klasifikasi tema memorat (memoratların tematik özellikleri) karya Çobanoğlu, Hırtik termasuk dalam daftar makhluk demonik bersama Cinler, Karabasan, Congoloz, dan Erkebit.
statement.en: In Çobanoğlu's classification of memorate themes (memoratların tematik özellikleri), Hırtik is listed among the demonic beings, along with Cinler, Karabasan, Congoloz and Erkebit.

short_description.id: Hāhau-whenua adalah nama ikan raksasa yang ditangkap Māui dalam tradisi Māori Ngāti Hau yang dicatat John White; ikan itu menjadi North Island of New Zealand.
short_description.en: Hāhau-whenua names the huge fish that Māui hauled in, according to a Māori tradition of the Ngāti Hau that John White recorded; the fish turned into the North Island of New Zealand.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Māori yang oleh John White dikaitkan dengan suku Ngāti Hau, Hāhau-whenua adalah nama ikan besar yang ditangkap Māui dan menjadi North Island of New Zealand. Dalam bahasa Māori pulau itu disebut Te ika-a-Māui, ikan Māui. Tregear menjelaskan bahwa Te Ika-a-Maui adalah pulau yang ditarik Maui dari kedalaman samudra.
long_description.en: John White attributes to the Ngāti Hau tribe a Māori tradition in which the huge fish that Māui landed, called Hāhau-whenua, turned into the North Island of New Zealand. In Māori the island is called Te ika-a-Māui, the fish of Māui. Tregear explains that Te Ika-a-Maui is the island Maui pulled up from the depths of the ocean.

long_description.id: Menurut kisah itu, ketika ikan menyambar kailnya Māui menduga ikan itu mungkin Hāhau-tangaroa, Hāhau-uru, atau Hāhau-whenua. Setelah menariknya ke atas, ia melihat bahwa ikan itu Hāhau-whenua. Nama itu diterjemahkan sebagai mencari daratan, dan Tregear mencatat bahwa hahau berarti mencari.
long_description.en: In the tale, when a fish took his hook Māui guessed it might be Hāhau-tangaroa, Hāhau-uru or Hāhau-whenua. When he pulled it up he saw that it was Hāhau-whenua. The name is rendered as search for land, and Tregear records that hahau means to seek.

long_description.en: Wikipedia's article on Māui adds the general version in which the giant fish became the North Island and its valleys and mountains were made by Māui's brothers chopping up the fish.

short_description.id: Hakawai atau Hōkioi adalah burung mitos Māori yang kadang terdengar tetapi jarang terlihat, dan pendengarannya dianggap pertanda buruk.
short_description.en: Hakawai, also Hōkioi, is a Māori mythological bird that was sometimes heard but not usually seen, and hearing it was considered a bad omen.

long_description.id: Hakawai, juga disebut Hōkioi di Pulau Utara, adalah burung mitos bagi orang Māori New Zealand yang kadang terdengar tetapi biasanya tidak terlihat. Dalam mitologi Māori, ia salah satu dari sebelas burung tapu (sakral) milik Raka-maomao, dewa angin, hidup di langit dan hanya turun ke bumi pada malam hari. Sumber ornitologi mencatatnya sebagai keturunan Tangaroa dan Rehua.
long_description.en: To New Zealand Māori, Hakawai (Hōkioi in the North Island) was a mythical bird that was at times heard but seldom seen. Māori mythology counts it among the eleven tapu (sacred) birds of Raka-maomao, a wind god; it lived in the heavens and came down to earth only after dark. An ornithological source records it as a descendant of Tangaroa and Rehua.

long_description.id: Burung ini dianggap sebagai burung pemangsa raksasa. Kamus Tregear mencatat bahwa menurut penutur Māori, hokioi sebesar moa, berbulu warna-warni dengan seikat bulu merah di kepalanya. Sebuah peribahasa yang dikutip menyamakan sebuah burung dengan Hakawai yang membuat dirinya tak terlihat.
long_description.en: It was considered a gigantic bird of prey. Tregear's dictionary records that, according to Māori speakers, the hokioi was as large as the moa, with colourful plumage and a tuft of red feathers on its head. A quoted proverb likens a bird to the Hakawai, which makes itself invisible.

long_description.id: Mendengar Hakawai dianggap pertanda buruk, yang secara tradisional menandakan perang. Panggilannya terdengar pada malam berbulan yang tenang dari ketinggian; suaranya terdiri atas seruan yang dirangkai sebagai hakwai, hakwai, hakwai, disusul deru tanpa suara seperti benda yang melaju di udara.
long_description.en: Hearing the Hakawai was considered a bad omen, traditionally presaging war. Its call was heard on calm moonlit nights from a great height; the sound began with a cry written hakwai, hakwai, hakwai, then a wordless roar like something rushing through the air at speed.

long_description.id: Legenda yang paling banyak dikutip tentang hokioi adalah perlombaan terbang tertinggi dengan kahu (elang), yang menjelaskan mengapa hokioi hanya turun pada malam hari dan mengucapkan namanya. Tentang jati dirinya, Miskelly menyimpulkan bahwa datanya mendukung hipotesis bahwa hakawai adalah burung snipe, sedangkan Sir W. Buller, menurut Tregear, menganggap Hokioi identik dengan Great Frigate Bird.
long_description.en: The most widely quoted legend about hokioi is a contest with the kahu (hawk) over who could fly highest, which explains why hokioi descends only at night and calls out his name. On its identity, Miskelly concludes that his data support the hypothesis that the hakawai was a snipe, while Sir W. Buller, according to Tregear, considers the Hokioi identical with the Great Frigate Bird.

short_description.id: Hasshaku-sama adalah hantu perempuan raksasa dalam legenda urban Jepang modern yang bermula dari kisah daring tahun 2008.
short_description.en: Hasshaku-sama is a giant woman-like ghost in a modern Japanese urban legend that began with an online story posted in 2008.

long_description.id: Hasshaku-sama adalah hantu perempuan raksasa dalam legenda urban Jepang modern. Sebuah kisah daring awal diunggah ke 2channel pada Agustus 2008.
long_description.en: Hasshaku-sama is a giant woman-like ghost in a modern Japanese urban legend. An early online story was posted to 2channel in August 2008.

long_description.id: Sosok itu digambarkan tinggi dan pucat serta memakai gaun terusan, dengan topi dan bunyi po po po yang berulang. Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menyebut tingginya delapan shaku dengan usia tak tentu, dan ia menyerang manusia, terutama anak-anak, serta dapat meniru suara kenalan sasarannya.
long_description.en: The figure is portrayed as tall and pale, wearing a one-piece dress, with a hat and a repeated po po po sound. Japanese Wikipedia gives her height as eight shaku with indeterminate age, and says she attacks people, especially children, and can imitate the voices of a target’s acquaintances.

long_description.id: Cerita yang beredar menyebut penangkal berupa jimat, ruangan dengan garam di empat sudut, doa, dan tidak berbicara atau menunjuknya. Satu versi menyebut arca Jizo dahulu menyegelnya. Ia juga kadang disebut yokai perempuan raksasa dari wilayah San'in, dan sebuah gim horor komedi mengolah legendanya.
long_description.en: Lore mentions countermeasures such as a talisman, a room with salt in its four corners, prayer, and not speaking to or pointing at her. One version says a Jizo statue once sealed her. She is also sometimes called a giant-woman yokai of the San'in region, and a comedy horror game riffs off her legend.

description.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, ia dapat mengubah suara dan memancing sasaran dengan suara kenalannya.
description.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, she can change her voice and lure targets with the voice of an acquaintance.

description.id: Jimat, ruangan dengan garam di empat sudut hingga pukul tujuh pagi, doa, serta tidak berbicara dan tidak menunjuk bila bertemu, menurut cerita yang diwariskan.
description.en: A talisman, a room with salt in its four corners until seven in the morning, prayer, and not speaking to or pointing at her if met, according to the lore.

description.id: Dahulu arca Jizo menyegelnya di daerah tertentu, tetapi arca itu kini dirusak.
description.en: A Jizo statue once sealed her in a particular area, but the statue has since been destroyed.

short_description.id: Hoop snake adalah makhluk legendaris Amerika Serikat, Kanada, dan Australia: ular yang menggigit ekornya dan berguling seperti roda mengejar mangsa.
short_description.en: The hoop snake is a legendary creature known in the United States, Canada and Australia: a snake said to take its tail in its jaws and roll after prey like a wheel.

long_description.id: Hoop snake adalah makhluk legendaris di Amerika Serikat, Kanada, dan Australia. Menurut cerita rakyat, ciri khasnya adalah ia dapat menggigit ekornya dengan rahangnya, seperti ouroboros dalam mitologi Yunani, dan berguling mengejar mangsa seperti roda.
long_description.en: The hoop snake is a creature of legend in the United States, Canada and Australia. In folklore its defining trait is gripping its tail in its jaws, like the Greek ouroboros, and rolling after prey like a wheel.

long_description.id: Dalam satu versi mitos, ular itu meluruskan tubuh pada detik terakhir dan menusuk korbannya dengan ekornya yang berbisa; dalam penuturan Australia, ular itu berbentuk lingkaran sebesar roda kemudi dengan deretan duri panjang yang berjarak sama di bagian dalam tubuhnya. Uraian sebuah penanda sejarah menyebut hoop snake berguling ke arah korban lalu meluruskan tubuh pada saat terakhir dan menyerang dengan ekornya yang berduri.
long_description.en: In one version of the myth the snake uncoils at the last moment and impales its victim on its venomous tail; in an Australian version it is a ring-shaped snake about the size of a steering wheel, with long spines spaced evenly along the inside of its body. A historical marker's description says the hoop snake rolls at its victims, straightens at the last moment and strikes with its spiked tail.

long_description.id: Sebuah kolom yang mengutip buku herpetologi menyebut kisah ini biasanya dikenakan pada mud snake dan rainbow snake, dan menyatakan bahwa ular itu tidak dapat menyengat dengan ekornya, meski memiliki duri keras yang dapat melukai bila dikibaskan. Sebuah penanda sejarah mencatat legenda setempat tentang ular raksasa yang berguling menuruni bukit ke arah korbannya.
long_description.en: A column quoting a herpetology book says the tale is usually applied to the mud snake and the rainbow snake, and states that the snake cannot sting with its tail, though it has a hard spine that can draw blood when thrashed. A historical marker records a local legend of an enormous snake that rolled down a hill toward its victims.

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.
The accepted research entry is embedded unchanged; the image may only depict what its claims document.
Creatures an earlier batch left out keep that reason as catatan_sebelumnya; the generator may decline them with status tidak-digambar.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
